children.text: sāṃkhyasaptatiṭīkā jayamaṅgalā //
children.translated_text: Commentary on the <s>Sāṃkhya-saptati</s> (Seventy Verses on <s>Sāṃkhya</s>) called <s>Jayamaṅgalā</s>.

children.text: kārikā 1
children.translated_text: Kārikā 1

children.text: adhigatatattvālokaṃ lokottaravādinaṃ praṇamya munim /
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the sage who has attained the light of truth, who speaks of what is beyond the world,

children.text: kriyate saptatikāyāṣṭīkā jayamaṅgalā nāma //
children.translated_text: a commentary called <s>Jayamaṅgalā</s> is composed on the Seventy Verses.

children.text: prekṣāvanto 'nukte prayojane na kvacitpravartanta iti prayojanamucyate tattvajñānānmokṣaḥ tattvāni pañcaviṃśatiḥ / tathā coktam -
pañcaviṃśatitattvajño yatra kutrāśrame rataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The knower of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>, delighting in whatever <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life),

children.text: jaṭī muṇḍī śikhī vāpi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: whether wearing matted locks, shaven-headed, or with a topknot—is liberated; there is no doubt about this.'

Discerning persons do not engage in any undertaking without a stated purpose; therefore the purpose is stated: liberation comes from knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles of reality); the <s>tattvas</s> are twenty-five. And thus it is said—

children.text: teṣu ca ṣaṣṭitantrādikhyāteṣviti / vistaratvāt ṣaṣṭitantrasya saṃkṣiptarucisattvānugrahārthaṃ saptatikārambhaḥ / vakṣyati ca 'etadāryābhiḥ saṃkṣiptam'; iti / mokṣeṇa kiṃ phalamiti cedduḥkhanivṛttiḥ / atattvajño duḥkhairabhihanyamānassaṃsarannāste / tattvajñānāttu kaivalyamāpnoti, na duḥkhairabhihanyate / hanyamānena ko heturjijñāsitavya ityatrāha-
children.translated_text: Among these, as proclaimed in the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> (Treatise of Sixty Topics) and other [works]— because of the prolixity of the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>, the composition of the Seventy Verses is undertaken for the benefit of beings who prefer conciseness. As will be stated: 'This has been condensed by the noble [<s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>].' If one asks: what is the fruit of liberation? — [the answer is:] the cessation of suffering. One who does not know the <s>tattvas</s>, being afflicted by sufferings, continues to wander in <s>saṃsāra</s>. But through knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s>, one attains <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute isolation/liberation) and is not afflicted by sufferings. As to what cause should be investigated by one who is afflicted — to this he says:

children.text: duḥkhatrayābhighātājjijñāsā tadavaghātake hetau /
children.translated_text: From the affliction of the threefold suffering, [arises] the desire to know the cause that removes it;

children.text: dṛṣṭe sāpārthā cennaikāntātyantato 'bhāvāt || 1 ||
children.translated_text: [if one says] that is pointless when the [remedy] is seen — [we reply:] no, because of the non-existence of absolute and permanent [cessation through seen remedies]. || 1 ||

children.text: 'duḥkhatrayābhighātājjijñāsā'; ityādi / duḥkhānāṃ trayaṃ duḥkhatrayam / ādhyātmikam, ādhibhautikam, ādhidaivikaṃ ceti / ātmanyadhyātmam, tatra yadbhavati tadādhyātmikam / śārīraṃ mānasaṃ ceti / tatra vātapittaśleṣmaṇāṃ vaiṣamyeṇa jvarādiduḥkham, taccharīre bhavatīti śārīram / yatkāmakrodhaśokādibhiḥ manasi duḥkhaṃ tanmānasam / yanmānuṣapaśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpasthāvarānyadhikṛtya bhavati tadādhibhautikam / yaccharīre grahāveśādīni daivānyadhikṛtya bhavati tadādhidaivikamiti / etadduḥkhatrayam / tenābhighātātpīḍanāddhetorjijñāsā jñātumicchā bhavati //
children.translated_text: 'From the affliction of the threefold suffering, the desire to know' etc. The triad of sufferings is the threefold suffering: <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), <s>ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to beings), and <s>ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to the gods). That which relates to the self (<s>adhyātma</s>), that which occurs therein is <s>ādhyātmika</s>. It is of two kinds: bodily and mental. Of these, the suffering of fever etc. arising from the imbalance of <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), which occurs in the body, is bodily. The suffering in the mind caused by desire, anger, grief, etc. is mental. That which occurs in relation to human beings, cattle, deer, birds, reptiles, and plants is <s>ādhibhautika</s>. That which occurs in the body in relation to divine [causes] such as spirit-possession etc. is <s>ādhidaivika</s>. This is the threefold suffering. From the affliction by it, from the torment caused by it, the desire to know, the wish to understand, arises.

children.text: kasmin viṣaya ityāha- 'tadavaghātake hetau'; iti / avaghātayatyapanayatītyavaghātakaḥ / tasya duḥkhatrayasyāvaghātakastadavaghātakaḥ / tṛjakābhyāṃ ṣaṣṭhīsamāsapratiṣedhaḥ, 'tatprayojako hetuśca'; iti na bhavati / kena khalvimāni duḥkhānyutpadyanta iti tadavaghātako heturjijñāsyo bhavati / duḥkhavānahametatpratīkāramanveṣayāmīti prāyovādaḥ / sa ca pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānānnānya iti manasi vartate //
children.translated_text: Regarding what subject [does this desire arise]? — he says: 'the cause that removes it.' That which removes, that is, eliminates, is the remover. That which removes the threefold suffering is the remover of that. By the rules of compounds, the formation of a genitive compound is prohibited, so 'that which causes it [to cease]' does not apply. 'By what are these sufferings produced?' — this cause of their removal is to be investigated. 'I am afflicted by suffering; I shall seek its remedy' — this is the general purport. And that [remedy] is none other than the knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> — this is what is meant.

children.text: 'dṛṣṭe sā 'pārthā cet'; iti / syādetat yadi dṛṣṭastadavaghātako heturna syāt / yāvadādhyātmikasya śārīraduḥkhasyāpanayane cikitsāśāstravihita evopāyo 'sti, mānasasyāpi saṃkhyānabalaṃ ramyāśca śabdādayo viṣayāḥ / ādhibhautikādhidaivikayorapi, avaghātaheturanuṣṭhīyamāno loka eva dṛśyate, tayoḥ satpratipakṣatvāt / tatrādhidaivikasya sāmadāmabhedadaṇḍopāyaghaṭitārambhāḥ / ādhibhautikasyāpi nipātapratipātasaṃvṛtapradeśāśrayaṇādayaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'If pointless when [a remedy] is seen' — this might be [objected]: if a seen cause for removing [suffering] exists — for removing bodily suffering of the <s>ādhyātmika</s> kind, there is indeed a remedy prescribed by the science of medicine; for mental [suffering] too, the strength of reason and pleasing sense-objects such as sound etc. [serve as remedies]. For the <s>ādhibhautika</s> and <s>ādhidaivika</s> as well, the removing cause is indeed seen being employed in the world, since effective countermeasures exist for both. For the <s>ādhidaivika</s>, there are efforts composed of the methods of conciliation, gifts, sowing dissension, and punishment. For the <s>ādhibhautika</s> as well, [there are remedies such as] taking shelter in places protected by barriers and ramparts, etc.

children.text: tataśca dṛṣṭe hetau sati jijñāsā 'smin viṣaye nirarthaketyāśaṅkyāha- 'naikāntātyantato 'bhāvāt'; iti / nā 'pārthā, sārthikaiva / kutaḥ- ekāntataḥ ekāntātyantato 'bhāvādapi / ekāntenātyantena ca duḥkhābhāvasyābhāvādityarthaḥ / dṛṣṭe hyupāye kriyamāṇe 'pi keṣāṃcidduḥkhatrayaṃ bhavatyeveti naikāntenopaśamaḥ / kathaṃcidupaśame punarutpādanāt nātyantenopaśamaḥ / tasmādaikāntikātyantikaduḥkhopaśamāya jijñāsā yukteti // 1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, with the apprehension that 'when a seen cause exists, the desire to know in this matter is pointless,' he says: 'because of the non-existence of absolute and permanent [cessation].' It is not pointless; it is meaningful indeed. Why? — because of the non-existence of the absence of suffering absolutely and permanently. The meaning is: because the absence of suffering does not exist either absolutely or permanently. For even when a seen remedy is being applied, the threefold suffering occurs for some — so there is no absolute cessation. Since after some cessation it arises again, there is no permanent cessation. Therefore the desire to know [the cause] for the absolute and permanent cessation of suffering is justified. ||1||

children.text: kārikā 2
children.translated_text: Kārikā 2

children.text: yadyevamaikāntikātyantikaduḥkhopaśamaheturvavedavihito 'sti / tathā cāha-
aṇama somamamṛtā abhūmāganma jyotiravidāma devān /
children.translated_text: 'We have drunk the <s>Soma</s>; we have become immortal; we have reached the light; we have found the gods.

children.text: kimasmān kṛṇavadarātiḥ kimu dhūrttiramṛtamartyasya // iti //
children.translated_text: What can an enemy do to us now? What can the decrepitude of a mortal [do to us]?'
If so, [one might argue:] a cause for the absolute and permanent cessation of suffering is indeed prescribed in the <s>Vedas</s>. And thus it is said—

children.text: asyāyamarthaḥ- indro devanāmapaṇḍitānāha 'divyāḥ kimanyatsukhamasti'; iti / te tamāhuḥ 'nāsti'; iti / somamapāma, somaṃ pītavanto vayam / tato 'mṛtā abhūma, vyapagatamṛtyavo jātāḥ / 'aganma jyotiḥ'; iti / jyotiḥ svargo 'yam, taṃ prāptā vayam / 'avidāma devān'; iti / iyanto devā asmin svarga iti jñātavantaḥ jñānamasmākamutpannamityarthaḥ / 'kimasmān kṛṇavat'; iti / kṛṇavanmṛtyurucyate / asmān somapānān kiṃ mṛtyuḥ kariṣyate / arātiḥ vyādhiḥ so 'pi, dhūratirjarā sāpi cāsmākaṃ kiṃ kariṣyati / 'amṛtamartyasya'; iti / tasmāt somapānādduḥkhopaśamaheturastītyasmin pūrvapakṣe -
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is: <s>Indra</s> asked the gods, the learned ones: 'Is there any other happiness than the divine?' They said to him: 'There is not.' 'We have drunk the <s>Soma</s>' — we have drunk the <s>Soma</s> [juice]. From that, 'we have become immortal' — we have become free from death. 'We have reached the light' — this light is heaven; we have attained it. 'We have found the gods' — we have come to know that there are this many gods in this heaven, meaning: knowledge has arisen in us. 'What can [it] do to us?' — the word '<s>kṛṇavat</s>' refers to death. What can death do to us who have drunk <s>Soma</s>? The 'enemy' is disease; what can that do? And '<s>dhūrti</s>' is old age — what can that do to us? 'Of the mortal who is [now] immortal.' Therefore, from drinking <s>Soma</s>, there exists a cause for the cessation of suffering — in response to this prima facie position—

children.text:
dṛṣṭavadānuśravikaḥ sa hyaviśuddhikṣayātiśayayuktaḥ
tadviparītaḥ śreyān vyaktāvyaktajñavijñānāt || 2 ||
children.translated_text: The [Vedic remedy] based on what is heard (<s>ānuśravika</s>) is like the seen [remedy], for it is attended with impurity, decay, and excess; superior to that is [the path] through the discriminative knowledge of the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>), the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), and the knower (<s>jña</s>). || 2 ||

children.text: 'dṛṣṭavadānuśravikaḥ'; ityādi / anuśrūyate pāramparyeṇetyanuśravo vedaḥ śruvaḥ 'ṛdorap'; / tatra bhavo heturānuśravikaḥ / adhyātmādiḥ / dṛṣṭena tulyo dṛṣṭavat / tasyāpi doṣadarśanāt //
children.translated_text: 'Like the seen, the one based on what is heard' etc. That which is heard through tradition is <s>anuśrava</s>, the <s>Veda</s>; from the root '<s>śru</s>' with the suffix '<s>ap</s>.' The cause that arises therein is <s>ānuśravika</s> — the <s>ādhyātmika</s> and other [remedies prescribed in the Vedas]. Like the seen — equal to the seen. Because faults are observed in that too.

children.text: yadāha - 'sa hyaviśuddhikṣayātiśayayuktaḥ'; iti / yasmādānuśraviko heturaviśuddhyādibhistribhirdoṣairyuktaḥ / tatrāgnihotrādau paśuvyāpādanāt somapānādaviśuddhiyuktaḥ / karmakṣayāt svargacyutiriti kṣayayuktaḥ / tathā cāhuḥ - 'bahūnīndrasahasrāṇi vyatītāni yuge yuge'; iti / 'sa hi deveṣvapi devo daridrāti'; iti / 'īśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā mahad duḥkhamutpadyate'; ityatiśayayuktaḥ / tathāhi- yaḥ kratuśatena yajate tasya mahadaiśvaryam, yo dvābhyāṃ tribhirvā tasyālpamiti / tasmādānuśraviko 'pi dṛṣṭavatparityājyaḥ //
children.translated_text: As he says: 'for it is attended with impurity, decay, and excess.' Since the <s>ānuśravika</s> cause is attended with three faults — impurity, etc. Of these, in the <s>agnihotra</s> and other [rituals], due to the slaughter of animals and the drinking of <s>Soma</s>, it is attended with impurity. Due to the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, there is fall from heaven — so it is attended with decay. And thus they say: 'Many thousands of <s>Indras</s> have passed away age after age.' 'He is impoverished even among the gods.' 'Seeing the supreme lord, great suffering arises' — so it is attended with excess. For one who sacrifices with a hundred rituals has great lordship, while one with two or three has little — thus there is gradation. Therefore the <s>ānuśravika</s> [remedy] too, like the seen one, is to be rejected.

children.text: kastarhi śreyānityāha- 'tadviparītaḥ śreyān'; iti / dṛṣṭānuśravikadvārā yo viparītaḥ tattvajñānākhyaḥ sa śreyān / tasya akaivalyaprāpakatvāt / tatraikāntātyantato 'bhāvāddṛṣṭācchreyān / śarīrahānāddhi śuddhaphalaḥ, prakṛtihānādakṣayaphalaḥ, anuttaratvācca niratiśayaphala ityānuśravikācchreyān //
children.translated_text: What then is superior? — he says: 'superior is the opposite of that.' That which is opposite to both the seen and the heard paths — namely, the knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> — that is superior. Because it alone leads to <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). It is superior to the seen because of the absolute and permanent non-existence [of suffering]: free from the [impurity] of bodily [involvement], its fruit is pure; free from [dependence on] <s>Prakṛti</s>, its fruit is imperishable; and being unsurpassable, its fruit is without excess — thus it is superior to the <s>ānuśravika</s>.

children.text: sa kathaṃ procyata ityatrāha 'vyaktāvyaktajñavijñānāt'; iti / rāśitrayeṇa pañcaviṃśatitattvāni kathyante / tatra mahadādibhūtaparyantaṃ trayoviṃśatiprakāraṃ vyaktamucyate, tena rūpeṇa pradhānasya vyaktatvāt / avyaktaṃ pradhānam, kenacidrūpeṇāvyaktatvāt / jānātīti jñaḥ puruṣaḥ / teṣu yadvijñānaṃ svarūpaparicchedaḥ, tasmāt prāpyata ityarthaḥ / tanvādi hi paricchidya tadabhyāsāduttarakālaṃ prakṛtipuruṣāntarajñānamutpadyate, tataśca kaivalyamiti / asyā āryāyā vakṣyamāṇā yāḥ, sarvā evārthena bhāṣyasthānīyā draṣṭavyāḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: How is that expressed? — to this he says: 'through the discriminative knowledge of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower.' The twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> are stated by means of three categories. Of these, from <s>Mahat</s> (the Great, i.e., Intellect) to the gross elements — twenty-three in kind — is called the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>), because <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primal Nature) is manifest in those forms. The unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is <s>Pradhāna</s>, because it is unmanifest in any [perceptible] form. The knower (<s>jña</s>) is <s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious self), because he knows. The discriminative knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>) regarding these — the discernment of their essential natures — [liberation] is attained from that, this is the meaning. For having discerned the material [principles] and so forth, through continued practice, in time the knowledge of the distinction between <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> arises, and from that comes <s>kaivalya</s>. All the following <s>āryā</s> verses should be regarded as being in the position of a commentary in meaning. ||2||

children.text: kārikā 3
children.translated_text: Kārikā 3

children.text: tatraiṣāṃ vyaktādīnāmutpādābhyāṃ svarūpamāha-
children.translated_text: Now he states the essential nature of these — the manifest and others — through their origination:

children.text: mūlaprakṛtiravikṛtirmahadādyāḥ prakṛtivikṛtayaḥ sapta /
children.translated_text: The root <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) is uncreated (<s>avikṛti</s>); the seven — beginning with <s>Mahat</s> — are both <s>prakṛtis</s> (sources) and <s>vikṛtis</s> (modifications);

children.text: ṣoḍaśakastu vikāro, na prakṛtirna vikṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: the group of sixteen, however, are modifications alone; <s>Puruṣa</s> is neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor <s>vikṛti</s>. || 3 ||

children.text: 'mūlaprakṛtiḥ'; ityādi / prakṛtiḥ pradhānam / prakriyata utpadyate pradhānāt asyā iti prakṛtiḥ / mūlaṃ ca tatprakṛtiśceti mūlaprakṛtiḥ / saptānāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ mūlamādyaṃ kāraṇamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Root <s>Prakṛti</s>' etc. <s>Prakṛti</s> is <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primal Nature). It is called <s>Prakṛti</s> because from <s>Pradhāna</s> production takes place. It is the 'root' — and it is <s>Prakṛti</s> — hence 'root <s>Prakṛti</s>.' [It is] the root, the primary cause of the seven <s>Prakṛtis</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: 'avikṛtiḥ'; iti / na vikriyata ityavikṛtiḥ / na kutaścidutpādyata ityarthaḥ / etatprathamaṃ tattvam //
children.translated_text: 'Uncreated (<s>avikṛti</s>)' — that which is not modified is <s>avikṛti</s>; it is not produced from anything — this is the meaning. This is the first <s>tattva</s>.

children.text: 'mahadādyāḥ prakṛtivikṛtayaḥ sapta'; iti / mahān buddhissa ādyo yāsāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ tāstathoktāḥ / prakṛtayaśca vikṛtayaśceti prakṛtivikṛtayaḥ / tatra mahānahaṅkāraṃ janayan prakṛtiḥ, mahata utpadyamāno vikṛtiḥ / tanmātrāṇi śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ pañca yathākramamākāśavāyvagnyudakapṛthivyākhyāni bhūtāni janayantaḥ prakṛtayaḥ, ahaṅkārādutpadyamānā vikṛtayaḥ / ityetāni sapta tattvāni //
children.translated_text: 'The seven — beginning with <s>Mahat</s> — are both <s>prakṛtis</s> and <s>vikṛtis</s>.' <s>Mahat</s> (the Great, i.e., Intellect) — that is the first of those <s>prakṛtis</s>; they are so called. They are both <s>prakṛtis</s> (sources) and <s>vikṛtis</s> (modifications). Of these, <s>Mahat</s>, generating <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense), is a <s>prakṛti</s>; being produced from <s>Mahat</s> [i.e., from <s>Pradhāna</s>], it is a <s>vikṛti</s>. The five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) — sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — generating respectively the five gross elements called space, wind, fire, water, and earth, are <s>prakṛtis</s>; being produced from <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, they are <s>vikṛtis</s>. Thus these are the seven <s>tattvas</s>.

children.text:
'ṣoḍaśakaśca vikāraḥ'; iti / ṣoḍaśa parimāṇamasyeti ṣoḍaśakaḥ / pañca buddhīndriyāṇi, pañca karmendriyāṇi, manaścetyekādaśendriyāṇi, pañca mahābhūtānītyayaṃ ṣoḍaśako gaṇaḥ / cakāra evakārārthaḥ / vikāro vikṛtireva / (nāsmāt kiñcidutpadyata ityarthaḥ / etāni ṣoḍaśa tattvāni) /
'na prakṛtirna vikṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ'; iti / puraṃ śarīraṃ tasmin vasatīti puruṣaḥ / nairukto 'travidhiḥ / tasmānna kiñcidutpadyata iti na prakṛtiḥ, niṣkriyatvāt / nāpyayaṃ kutaścidutpadyata iti na vikṛtiḥ, anāditvāt // 3 //
children.translated_text: 'And the group of sixteen is <s>vikāra</s> (modification).' That which has sixteen as its measure is 'the group of sixteen.' The five <s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s> (cognitive sense-organs), the five <s>karmendriyāṇi</s> (organs of action), and <s>manas</s> (mind) — these are the eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense-organs); the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) — this is the group of sixteen. The particle 'ca' (and) has the meaning of 'eva' (only). <s>Vikāra</s> (modification) means that which is only modified (nothing further arises from it — this is the meaning. These are the sixteen <s>tattvas</s>, principles). '<s>Puruṣa</s> is neither <s>Prakṛti</s> nor <s>vikṛti</s>.' <s>Puruṣa</s> — one who dwells (<s>vasati</s>) in the city (<s>pura</s>), i.e., the body — this is the etymological derivation (<s>nairukta</s>). Nothing arises from him, therefore he is not <s>Prakṛti</s> (primal nature), because of his inactivity. Nor does he arise from anything, therefore he is not <s>vikṛti</s> (modification), because of his beginninglessness. ||3||

children.text: kārikā 4
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 4

children.text: eṣāṃ vyaktādīnāṃ siddhau pramāṇānyāha-
dṛṣṭamanumānamāptavacanaṃ ca, sarvapramāṇasiddhatvāt /
children.translated_text: Perception (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and reliable testimony (<s>āptavacana</s>) — since [the <s>pramāṇas</s>] are established through all [three] means of valid knowledge,

children.text: trividhaṃ pramāṇamiṣṭaṃ, prameyasiddhiḥ pramāṇāddhi || 4 ||
children.translated_text: the threefold <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is accepted; for the establishment of what is to be known (<s>prameya</s>) is indeed from <s>pramāṇa</s>. [ISk 4]
He states the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇas</s>) for establishing these — the manifest and others—

children.text: 'dṛṣṭam'; ityādi / dṛṣṭaṃ pratyakṣam / anumīyate yena tadanumānam / āptaḥ kṣīṇadoṣastena yaducyate tadāptavacanam / āgamaḥ / etat trividhaṃ pramāṇamiṣṭam //
children.translated_text: 'Perception' (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>) etc. — <s>dṛṣṭa</s> means direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). That by which something is inferred (<s>anumīyate</s>) is <s>anumāna</s> (inference). An <s>āpta</s> (reliable authority) is one whose faults are eliminated; what is said by such a one is <s>āptavacana</s> (reliable testimony), i.e., <s>āgama</s> (scripture). This threefold <s>pramāṇa</s> is accepted.

children.text: nanu cānyānyapi pratibhādīni pramāṇāni santi tadyathā-
children.translated_text: Objection: But are there not other <s>pramāṇas</s> such as <s>pratibhā</s> (intuition) and so on? Namely—

children.text: pratibhaupamyamaitihāsamabhāvassambhavastathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Pratibhā</s> (intuition), <s>upamāna</s> (analogy), <s>aitihya</s> (tradition), <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence), <s>sambhava</s> (inclusion), and also

children.text: arthāpattiritīmāni pramāṇānyapare jaguḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — these are the <s>pramāṇas</s> stated by others.

children.text: asmin pūrvapakṣa āha- 'sarvapramāṇasiddhatvāt'; iti / sarveṣāṃ pratibhādīnāṃ pramāṇānāṃ siddhatvāt, trividha evāntarbhāvādityarthaḥ / tatra grāme nagare vā vartata iti pratibhotpannā / tatra yadā kṣīṇadoṣasya, tadābhijñaprāptatvāt pratyakṣameva / tasyākṣīṇadoṣasya vitathatvādapramāṇam / yāpyarthāvisaṃvādinī kādācitkā, sāpi kādācitkādeva nimittādutpadyamānānumānameva na pramāṇāntaram / 'gauriva gavayaḥ'; ityaupamyam / tatra gavayamajānānaḥ kaścidāptaṃ pṛcchati 'kīdṛśo gavayaḥ', iti / sa tamāha- 'yādṛśo gaustādṛśo gavayaḥ'; iti / tadetadāptavacanameva na pramāṇāntaram / yadāpi labdhopadeśo gavayaṃ paśyati, tadāpi gavi dṛṣṭenaiva viṣāṇādinā liṅgena gavayasya vyavahāraṃ pravartayatītyanumānameva na pramāṇāntaram / 'itiha vai vaiśravaṇaḥ'; ityaitihyam / etadāptavacanameva na pramāṇāntaram / 'itiha'; iti nipātasamudāya upadeśapāramparye vartete / itiha evaitihyam / svārthe yañ / 'nāstīha ghaṭo 'nupalambhāt'; ityabhāvaḥ / tatra ghaṭaśūnyapradeśa eva ghaṭābhāvaḥ, sa ca pratyakṣapramāṇasiddhatvānna pramāṇāntaram / 'māṣaḥ prastha ityukte catvāraḥ kuḍapā itīdamapi sambhavati'; ityayaṃ sambhavaḥ / tatra samudāyaliṅgāvayavaliṅginaḥ paricchedādanumānameva / avayavaissamudāyasyārabdhatvāt kāryakāraṇalakṣaṇaḥ sambandhaḥ / 'devadatto divā na bhuṅkte balavāṃścetyukta arthādrātrau bhuṅkte'; ityarthāpattiḥ / tata eva rātrau tasya pratītiranumānānna bhidyate / idameva cānyathānupapattirityucyate //
children.translated_text: To this objection, he says: 'since [they are] established through all <s>pramāṇas</s>.' Because all the [proposed] <s>pramāṇas</s> such as <s>pratibhā</s> etc. are established, i.e., included within the threefold [classification] — this is the meaning. Regarding <s>pratibhā</s> (intuition) — it arises in one dwelling in a village or city. When it belongs to one whose faults are eliminated, then, because it is attained through <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledge), it is nothing but direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). When it belongs to one whose faults are not eliminated, it is invalid because it is erroneous. That [intuition] which is occasionally consistent with its object but incidental — since it arises from an incidental cause, it is nothing but inference, not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>. '<s>Upamāna</s> (analogy): a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is like a cow.' Someone who does not know a <s>gavaya</s> asks a reliable authority: 'What does a <s>gavaya</s> look like?' He tells him: 'A <s>gavaya</s> looks like a cow.' This is nothing but reliable testimony, not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>. Even when, having received the instruction, he sees a <s>gavaya</s>, he establishes the usage for the <s>gavaya</s> by the indicative sign (<s>liṅga</s>) of horns etc. previously seen in the cow — thus it is nothing but inference, not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>. '<s>Aitihya</s> (tradition): Thus indeed <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> [spoke].' This is nothing but reliable testimony, not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>. '<s>Itiha</s>' — this group of particles applies to a chain of instruction; <s>itiha</s> itself is <s>aitihya</s>; the suffix '-ya' is in the reflexive sense. '<s>Abhāva</s> (non-existence): There is no pot here, because of non-apprehension.' The absence of the pot is just the place devoid of the pot, and since that is established by the <s>pramāṇa</s> of direct perception, it is not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>. '<s>Sambhava</s> (inclusion): When a <s>māṣa</s> (bean-measure) equals a <s>prastha</s>, this also entails four <s>kuḍapas</s>.' Since this is the determination of a part from the indicative sign of the whole, it is nothing but inference. Because the whole is constituted by its parts, the relation is one of effect and cause. '<s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption): When it is said that <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat by day and yet is stout, [it is presumed] from the meaning that he eats at night.' His cognition at night from that [premise] does not differ from inference. And this is precisely what is called 'otherwise inexplicable' (<s>anyathānupapatti</s>).

children.text: kiṃ pramāṇatrayalakṣaṇe prayojanamiti cedāha- 'prameyasiddhiḥ pramāṇāddhi'; iti / yasmāt prameyasyārthasya siddhiḥ pramāṇāt, anyathā kathaṃ tatprāptiparihārau syātām // 4 //
children.translated_text: If asked what the purpose of defining the three <s>pramāṇas</s> is, he says: 'For the establishment of what is to be known is indeed from <s>pramāṇa</s>.' Since the establishment of the object to be known (<s>prameya</s>) is from <s>pramāṇa</s> — otherwise how could its attainment and avoidance be [determined]? ||4||

children.text: kārikā 5
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 5

children.text: dṛṣṭādipramāṇānāṃ lakṣaṇamāha-
children.translated_text: He states the definition of the <s>pramāṇas</s> beginning with perception—

children.text: prativiṣayādhyavasāyo dṛṣṭaṃ, trividhamanumānamākhyātam /
children.translated_text: The determination with respect to each sense-object is perception (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>); inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is declared to be threefold,

children.text: talliṅgaliṅgipūrvakam, āptaśrutirāptavacanaṃ ca || 5 ||
children.translated_text: and it is preceded by the indicative sign (<s>liṅga</s>) and what bears the sign (<s>liṅgin</s>); reliable testimony (<s>āptavacana</s>) is the <s>śruti</s> (transmitted word) of the reliable authority. [ISk 5]

children.text: 'prativiṣayādhyavasāyaḥ'; ityādi / viṣayaṃ viṣayaṃ prativiṣayam, prativiṣayamadhyavasāyaḥ prativiṣayādhyavasāyaḥ / viṣayāḥ śabdādayaḥ, adhyavasāyo buddhiḥ / śabdasparśarūparasagandheṣu yathākramaṃ śrotratvakcakṣurjihvāghrāṇendriyadvāreṇa viśeṣāvadhāraṇapradhānā yā buddhirutpadyate tad dṛṣṭam, śuddhatvātpramāṇamaśuddhatvādapramāṇam / taccaturvidham- savyapadeśam, savikalpam, arthavyatirekīndriyavyatirekī ceti / tatra dūrāt kvacidāgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā devadattasārūpyaṃ vyapadiśati devadatto 'yamiti yā buddhirutpadyate tatsavikalpam, saṃśayitatvādapramāṇam / taimirikasya dvicandradarśanaṃ tadarthavyatireki, dvitīyacandrābhāvāt / yatsvapnadarśanaṃ tadindriyavyatireki, nidropaplutatvādindriyāṇām //
children.translated_text: 'The determination with respect to each sense-object' etc. — 'With respect to each object' (<s>prativiṣaya</s>) means 'with respect to each and every object'; the determination with respect to each object is <s>prativiṣayādhyavasāya</s>. The objects are sound etc.; the determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect/cognition). That cognition which arises through the channels of the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose organs, with respect to sound, touch, form, taste, and smell respectively, predominantly as the ascertainment of particulars — that is perception (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>); when pure, it is a valid <s>pramāṇa</s>; when impure, it is not. It is of four kinds: with designation (<s>savyapadeśa</s>), with conceptual construction (<s>savikalpa</s>), deviating from the object (<s>arthavyatirekin</s>), and deviating from the sense-organ (<s>indriyavyatirekin</s>). Among these: seeing someone approaching from afar and designating resemblance to <s>Devadatta</s> — the cognition 'This is <s>Devadatta</s>' — that is <s>savikalpa</s> (with conceptual construction), and being doubtful, it is not a valid <s>pramāṇa</s>. The vision of two moons by one with an eye-disease — that deviates from the object (<s>arthavyatirekin</s>), since there is no second moon. Dream-vision deviates from the sense-organ (<s>indriyavyatirekin</s>), since the sense-organs are overwhelmed by sleep.

children.text: 'trividhamanumānamākhyātam'; iti / ṣaṣṭitantre vyākhyātam- pūrvavat, śeṣavat, sāmānyatodṛṣṭamiti / atītānāgatavarttamānāstrayaḥ padārthāḥ / tatra bhaviṣyadarthasādhanāya pūrvavadanumānam / pūrvaṃ liṅgamasyāstīti pūrvavat / yathonnatajaladharaṃ dṛṣṭvā vṛṣṭirbhaviṣyatītyanumīyate / atītārthasādhanāya śeṣavat- śeṣaṃ liṅgamasyāstīti / yathāsyā nadyā upari vṛṣṭirbhūtā, yasyāḥ kaluṣodakaṃ śeṣaṃ liṅgamiti / varttamānārthasādhanāya sāmānyatodṛṣṭam- sāmānyena liṅgaliṅgidṛṣṭatvāt / yathā devadattasya gatipūrvikā deśāntaraprāptirdṛṣṭā, tathā sūryādīnāṃ sāmānyena deśāntaraprāptyā gatiranumīyate //
children.translated_text: 'Inference is declared to be threefold.' It is explained in the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>: <s>pūrvavat</s> (from prior), <s>śeṣavat</s> (from remainder), and <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (from general observation). The three temporal objects are past, future, and present. For establishing a future object, <s>pūrvavat</s> inference [is used] — 'that which has a prior sign' is <s>pūrvavat</s>. For example: seeing risen rain-clouds, one infers 'there will be rain.' For establishing a past object, <s>śeṣavat</s> — 'that which has a remaining sign.' For example: 'Rain has occurred upstream of this river,' because turbid water is the remaining sign. For establishing a present object, <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> — because the sign and what bears the sign are seen in general. For example: <s>Devadatta</s>'s reaching another place is seen to be preceded by movement; similarly, the movement of the sun and others is inferred in general from their reaching another place.

children.text: 'talliṅgaliṅgipūrvakam'; iti / trividhamanumānam / kadācilliṅgapūrvakaṃ kadācilliṅgipūrvakaṃ loke dṛśyate / tadyathā- śrāvyeṇa virutena kadācitkokilo 'numīyate, kadācitkokilaṃ liṅginaṃ dṛṣṭvā śrāvyeṇāpi virutenāsya bhavitavyamiti tayorgamyagamakatvaṃ sati sambandhe / sambandhāśca sapta- tatra svasvāmibhāvasambandho yathā rājapuruṣayoḥ kadācitpuruṣeṇa rājā rājñā vā puruṣaḥ / evaṃ prakṛtivikārasambandho yathā yavasaktoḥ / kāryakāraṇasambandho yathā dhenuvatsayoḥ / pātrapātrikasambandho yathā parivṛṭtriviṣṭabdhayoḥ / sāhacaryasambandho yathā cakravākayoḥ / pratidvandvisambandho yathā śītoṣṇayoḥ / tatraikasya bhāve 'nyābhāvaḥ pratīyate / nimittanaimittikasambandho yathā bhojyabhojakayoriti / ebhissambandhaistrividhamanumānaṃ pramāṇanna lupyate //
children.translated_text: 'It is preceded by the sign and what bears the sign.' Inference is threefold. Sometimes it is preceded by the sign (<s>liṅga</s>), sometimes by what bears the sign (<s>liṅgin</s>), as seen in the world. For example: sometimes the cuckoo is inferred from its sweet call; sometimes, having seen the cuckoo (the <s>liṅgin</s>), [one infers] 'it must also have a sweet call' — thus there is a relation of the knowable and the means of knowing when a connection exists. And the connections are seven: the relationship of master and servant (<s>svasvāmibhāva</s>), as between a king and his subject — sometimes the king [is inferred] from the subject, sometimes the subject from the king. Similarly, the relationship of <s>prakṛti</s> (primal nature) and <s>vikāra</s> (modification), as between barley and its flour. The relationship of effect and cause (<s>kāryakāraṇa</s>), as between a cow and her calf. The relationship of container and contained (<s>pātrapātrika</s>), as between the enclosed and the enclosing. The relationship of accompaniment (<s>sāhacarya</s>), as between <s>cakravāka</s> birds (ruddy geese). The relationship of opposition (<s>pratidvandvi</s>), as between cold and heat — from the presence of one, the absence of the other is understood. The relationship of indicator and indicated (<s>nimittanaimittika</s>), as between food and the eater. Through these connections, the threefold inference as a <s>pramāṇa</s> is not diminished.

children.text: 'āptaśrutirāptavacanaṃ ca'; iti / āptaḥ kṣīṇadoṣaḥ / yaccāhuḥ-
svakarmaṇyabhiyukto yo rāgadveṣavivarjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is devoted to his own duty, free from passion and aversion,

children.text: nirvairaḥ pūjitaḥ sadbhirāpto jñeyaḥ sa tādṛśaḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: without enmity, honored by the good — such a one is to be known as an <s>āpta</s> (reliable authority).
'Reliable testimony is the <s>śruti</s> (transmitted word) of the reliable authority.' An <s>āpta</s> (reliable authority) is one whose faults are eliminated. As they say—

children.text: āptebhyo yā śrutiparamparayā śrutirāgatā āptavacanam, tairdṛṣṭo 'numito vārthaḥ, paratra svabodhasadṛśabodhāntarotpattaye śabdenopadiśyate / yadanyavacanaṃ so na plavate (?) / caśabdo 'numānena tulyakakṣyatvakhyāpanārthaḥ / yathā trikālamaviṣayamanmānaṃ tathāptavananamapīti // 5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Āptavacana</s> (reliable testimony) is the <s>śruti</s> (transmitted word) that has come through the tradition of transmission from reliable authorities. The object seen or inferred by them is taught through words for the purpose of generating in others a cognition similar to their own. What is the speech of another [unreliable person] does not avail (?). The particle 'ca' (and) is for indicating equal status with inference. Just as inference [reaches] what is beyond the three times, so too does reliable testimony. ||5||

children.text: kārikā 6
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 6

children.text: eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ kaḥ kasya viṣaya ityata āha-
sāmānyatastu dṛṣṭādatīndriyāṇāmpratītiranumānāt /
children.translated_text: But from general observation (<s>sāmānyatas</s>), the cognition of what is beyond the senses (<s>atīndriya</s>) is from inference;

children.text: tasmādapi cāsiddhaṃ parokṣamāptāgamāt siddham || 6 ||
children.translated_text: and what is not established even thereby, being imperceptible, is established from reliable scripture (<s>āptāgama</s>). [ISk 6]
What is the scope of each of these three? To this he says—

children.text: 'sāmānyatastu'; ityādi / trividhaṃ prameyam- pratyakṣm, parokṣam, atyantaparokṣaṃ ceti / tatra yatsāmānyatodṛṣṭamanumānaṃ tasmādatīndriyāṇāṃ parokṣāṇāṃ prasiddhirasti / tanniścayaḥ, teṣāṃ pratyakṣaviṣayatvāt / pūrvavaccheṣavatostvamanumānayorbhaviṣyadbhūtārthavṛttitvādvarttamāneṣvatīndriyeṣu ca pravṛttyasambhavaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'But from general observation' etc. The knowable (<s>prameya</s>) is threefold: the perceptible (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), the imperceptible (<s>parokṣa</s>), and the utterly imperceptible (<s>atyantaparokṣa</s>). From the <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (general observation) inference, there is the establishment of things that are imperceptible, beyond the senses. That is their ascertainment, since they are objects of direct perception [in analogous cases]. But the <s>pūrvavat</s> and <s>śeṣavat</s> inferences, since they operate with respect to future and past objects, cannot function with respect to what is beyond the senses in the present.

children.text: 'tasmādapi cāsiddham'; iti / sāmānyatodṛṣṭādanumānādyadasiddhaṃ parokṣam, tadatyantaparokṣatvādāgamātsiddham / yathā svargāpavargāviti / pratyakṣe tu prameye dṛṣṭameva vyāpriyata ityarthāduktam // 6 //
children.translated_text: 'And what is not established even thereby.' That which is imperceptible and not established even by <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> inference — that, being utterly imperceptible, is established from <s>āgama</s> (scripture). For example, heaven (<s>svarga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). But regarding the perceptible object of knowledge, it is stated [implicitly] that perception alone operates. ||6||

children.text: kārikā 7
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 7

children.text: nanu ca 'vyaktāvyaktajñavijñānāt', vyaktaṃ tāvat pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ siddham, pradhānapuruṣayostu sarvadānupalambhāt kathaṃ siddhirnastayoriti nānupalabdhimātreṇāsattvam / yataścaturbhiḥ prakāraiḥ satāmapi padārthānāmupalabdhirbhavati / deśadoṣādindriyadoṣādviṣayadoṣādarthāntaradoṣācca / tāneva bhedena darśayannāha-
atidūrātsāmīpyādindriyaghātānmano 'navasthānāt /
children.translated_text: [Non-perception occurs] due to excessive distance, excessive proximity, damage to the sense organs, inattentiveness of the mind,

children.text: saukṣmyādvyavadhānādabhibhavātsamānābhihārācca || 7 ||
children.translated_text: subtlety, obstruction, suppression, and intermixture with similar things. // ISk 7 //

But [it was said] 'from the knowledge of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower.' Now, the manifest is indeed established through perception and inference. But how can <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit) be established, since they are never perceived? [One might say] 'they do not exist' — but non-existence does not follow from mere non-perception. Since even for existing things, perception fails for four reasons: due to defects of place, defects of the sense organs, defects of the object, and defects of other things. Showing these very reasons with differentiation, he says:

children.text: 'atidūrāt'; ityādi / yathā dūramutpatitasya pakṣiṇo nopalabdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Due to excessive distance' and so on. Just as a bird that has flown far away is not perceived.

children.text: 'sāmīpyāt'; iti / atiśabdo 'trāpi yojanīyaḥ / atisāmīpyāditi / yathā cakṣuḥsthasyāñjanasya / ubhayatrāpi deśadoṣakṛtānupalabdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Due to proximity.' The prefix 'ati' (excessive) should be supplied here too — that is, 'due to excessive proximity.' Just as collyrium applied to the eye [is not perceived]. In both cases, non-perception is caused by a defect of place.

children.text: 'indriyaghātāt'; iti / śrotrādīnāṃ buddhīndriyāṇāṃ doṣādyogyadeśāvasthitānāmapi śabdādīnāmanupalabdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Due to damage to the sense organs.' Due to a defect of the cognitive sense organs beginning with hearing, even sounds and other objects, though situated in an appropriate location, are not perceived.

children.text: 'mano 'navasthānāt'; iti / manaso 'navasthānamasamāhitatā, viṣayāntarapravṛttatvāt / tataścānupahatendriye 'pi sannihitaṃ viṣayaṃ nopalabhate / ubhayatrāpīndriyadoṣādanupalabdhiḥ / manaso 'pīndriyatvād bhedenopādānaṃ tu manasaḥ prādhānyārtham //
children.translated_text: 'Due to inattentiveness of the mind.' Inattentiveness of the mind is a state of being unconcentrated, due to being engaged with another object. And therefore, even when the sense organ is unimpaired, one does not perceive an object that is present. In both cases, non-perception is due to a defect of the sense organ. Although the mind too is a sense organ, its separate mention is for the purpose of emphasizing its importance.

children.text: 'saukṣmyāt'; iti / viṣayadoṣāt / viṣaya eva paramāṇvādistathā, yenāvyagramanasā 'pyanupahatendriyeṇa nopalabhyate //
children.translated_text: 'Due to subtlety.' This is due to a defect of the object. The object itself — atoms and the like — is of such a subtle nature that even with an undistracted mind and unimpaired sense organs, it is not perceived.

children.text: 'vyavadhānāt'; iti / yavanikādibhistirodhānāt sthūlā apyavikṛṣṭā ghaṭādayo nopalabhyante //
children.translated_text: 'Due to obstruction.' Due to concealment by curtains and the like, even large objects such as pots, though not far away, are not perceived.

children.text: 'abhibhavāt'; iti / ādityaprabhābhibhūtatvāt divā tārakā nopalabhyante //
children.translated_text: 'Due to suppression.' The stars are not perceived during the day due to being overpowered by the sun's radiance.

children.text: 'samānābhihārācca'; iti / sadṛśānāṃ rāśīkaraṇāt dhānyarāśau hyeko dhānyaguḍakaḥ prakṣipto na dṛśyate / triṣvapyarthāntaradoṣādanupalabdhiḥ / natveta anupalabhyamānā na santi // 7 //
children.translated_text: 'And due to intermixture with similar things.' Due to the heaping together of similar things, for a single grain thrown into a heap of grain is not seen. In all three [of the last cases], non-perception is due to a defect of other things. But these, though not perceived, do not therefore not exist. // 7 //

children.text: kārikā 8
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 8]

children.text: yadyevaṃ kena prakāreṇa satorapi pradhānapuruṣayoranupalabdhirityāha-
saukṣmyāttadanupalabdhirnābhāvāt kāryatastadupalabdheḥ /
children.translated_text: The non-perception of that [<s>Pradhāna</s>] is due to subtlety, not due to non-existence, since it is perceived through its effects.

children.text: mahadādi tacca kāryaṃ prakṛtisarūpaṃ virūpaṃ ca || 8 ||
children.translated_text: And that effect, beginning with <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One), is both similar and dissimilar to <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). // ISk 8 //
If so, by what means is there non-perception even of the existent <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>? To this he says:

children.text: 'saukṣmyāttadanupalabdhiḥ'; ityādi / prakārāntarābhāvāt sūkṣmatvātsatorapi tayoranupalabdhiḥ / nanvabhāvādeva kasmādanupalabdhirna bhavati / yathā ghaṭasyotpatteḥ prāk mṛt śarādiṣu.... tasya pradhvaṃsābhāvāt, gavi vāśvatvasyāśvatve vā gotvasyetaretarābhāvāt, vandhyāsutasya vātyantābhāvādityāha- 'nābhāvāt'; iti / caturvidhādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Due to subtlety, the non-perception of that' and so on. In the absence of any other reason, the non-perception of those two, though existent, is due to subtlety. Objection: Why is non-perception not simply due to non-existence? Just as, before the production of a pot, [there is] clay among potsherds — [one might argue for] its subsequent non-existence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>); or the mutual non-existence (<s>itaretarābhāva</s>) of horse-ness in a cow or cow-ness in a horse; or the absolute non-existence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>) of a barren woman's son. To this he says: 'Not due to non-existence' — the meaning is: not due to any of the four kinds [of non-existence].

children.text: yadyevaṃ kathaṃ tau sta iti gamyata ityāha- 'kāryatastadupalabdheḥ'; iti / yadyapyatrobhayaṃ prakrāntaṃ tathāpi tacchabdena pradhānaṃ nirdiśyate / pradhānasyāstitvapratipattiḥ kāryādityarthaḥ / puruṣasyāstitvapratipattau hetuṃ vakṣyati //
children.translated_text: If so, how are those two known to exist? To this he says: 'Since it is perceived through its effects.' Although both [<s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>] are introduced here, by the word 'tat' (that), <s>Pradhāna</s> is indicated. The meaning is: the ascertainment of <s>Pradhāna</s>'s existence comes from its effects. He will state the reason for the ascertainment of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s existence later.

children.text: kiṃ tatkāryamityāha- 'mahadādi tacca kāryam'; iti / mahān buddhiḥ sa ādiryasya tanmahadādibhūtaparyantaṃ kāryamasti / tat pradhānam, yasyedaṃ mahadādikāryaṃ vyaktam, akāraṇasya kāryasyānutpādāt //
children.translated_text: What is that effect? To this he says: 'And that effect, beginning with <s>Mahat</s>.' <s>Mahat</s> is <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect); that which has it as the beginning — the effect ranging from <s>Mahat</s> up to the gross elements — exists. That is <s>Pradhāna</s>, of which this manifest effect beginning with <s>Mahat</s> is the product, since an effect cannot be produced without a cause.

children.text: 'prakṛtisarūpaṃ virūpaṃ ca'; iti / tadvyaktaṃ prakṛteḥ pradhānasya sadṛśamasadṛśaṃ cetyarthaḥ / etaduttaratra yojayiṣyate // 8 //
children.translated_text: 'Both similar and dissimilar to <s>Prakṛti</s>.' That manifest product is both similar and dissimilar to <s>Prakṛti</s>, i.e., <s>Pradhāna</s> — this is the meaning. This will be elaborated further on. // 8 //

children.text: kārikā 9
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 9]

children.text: tatkāryaṃ kāraṇādutpadyamānaṃ sadutpadyate, kimasat, kiṃ vā sadasaditi? tatra viruddhadharmādhyāsitatvātsadasannopapadyate / asaditi vaiśeṣikāḥ / atra dūṣaṇamāha-
asadakaraṇādupādānagrahaṇāt sarvasambhavābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: The effect pre-exists [in the cause] because the non-existent cannot be produced, because of the selection of material cause, because of the impossibility of everything arising from everything,

children.text: śktasya śakyakaraṇāt, kāraṇabhāvācca satkāryam || 9 ||
children.translated_text: because the capable cause alone can produce what is possible, and because of the nature of the cause. // ISk 9 //

Does that effect, being produced from a cause, arise as existent? Or as non-existent? Or as both existent and non-existent? Of these, 'both existent and non-existent' is not possible, since contradictory properties would be superimposed. The <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> hold it to be non-existent [before production]. To refute this he says:

children.text: 'asadakaraṇāt'; ityādi / iha loke asataḥ karaṇaṃ nāsti, yathā śaśaviṣāṇādīnām / yadeva sat ghaṭādidravyaṃ tadeva mṛtpiṇḍādinā kāraṇaviśeṣeṇa kriyate, nāsat //
children.translated_text: 'Because the non-existent cannot be produced' and so on. In this world, there is no production of what is non-existent, just as there is no production of hare's horns and the like. Only that substance — a pot, etc. — which already exists [in the cause] is produced by a specific cause such as a lump of clay; not what is non-existent.

children.text: 'upādānagrahaṇāt'; iti / iha yadarthaṃ yadupādīyate tasya tadupādānaṃ kāraṇam, yathā tailasya tilāḥ, dadhnaḥ kṣīram / atra tailaṃ dadhi ca yadi na syāt kathaṃ tasyopādānasya grahaṇaṃ tadarthibhiḥ kriyate / tasmādupādānasaṃgrahāt sadeva kāryam / anyathā sikatāsalilayorapi grahaṇaṃ syāt //
children.translated_text: 'Because of the selection of material cause.' Here, that which is selected for the sake of a certain product, that material is its cause — just as sesame seeds are the cause of oil, and milk of yogurt. Here, if oil and yogurt did not already exist [in the cause], how would the selection of that material cause be made by those desiring them? Therefore, from the selection of the material cause, the effect indeed pre-exists. Otherwise, sand and water too would be selected [for oil and yogurt].

children.text: 'sarvasambhavābhāvāt'; iti / yadyasatkāryaṃ bhavet tadā sarvasya sarvatra sambhavaḥ syāt / na caivam / tasmātsadeva kāryam //
children.translated_text: 'Because of the impossibility of everything arising from everything.' If the effect were non-existent before production, then anything could arise from anything. But this is not so. Therefore, the effect indeed pre-exists.

children.text: 'śaktasya śakyakaraṇāt'; iti śaktaṃ kāraṇaṃ nāśaktamityevamapyavagantavyam / anyathopahataśaktarbījāṅkurotpattiprasaṅgaḥ / śaktaśca ko bhavitumarhati, yaḥ śaktimān / tasya śaktimataḥ śakyasya karaṇāt, śakanīyasya kāryasyotpādanādityarthaḥ / evaṃ ca tacchakanīyaṃ yadi kāraṇe śaktirūpeṇāvasthitaṃ syāt / tasmātsadevotpadyate nāsat //
children.translated_text: 'Because the capable cause alone can produce what is possible.' It should be understood that the cause is capable, not incapable. Otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence of a sprout arising from a seed whose power is destroyed. And who can be capable? One who possesses power. The meaning is: because that powerful cause produces the possible effect, the effect that is capable of being produced. And thus, that which is capable of being produced must exist in the cause in the form of power. Therefore, only what exists is produced, not what is non-existent.

children.text: 'kāraṇabhāvācca'; iti / kāraṇasya sattvādityarthaḥ / yadyasatkāryamutpadyate kimiti kāraṇabhāvena kāryasya bhāvo bhavati / bhavati ca / tasmācchaktirūpeṇāvasthitamiti gamyate / athavā- kāraṇabhāvāditi kāraṇasvabhāvāt / yatsvabhāvaṃ kāraṇaṃ tatsvabhāvaṃ kāryam, yathā snigdhasvabhāvastilebhyaḥ snigdhameva tailam, mṛto mṛtsvabhāvo ghaṭaḥ / yadyasatkāryaṃ syāt, asatsvabhāvebhyo hyutpādyetetyevaṃ sāṃkhyānāṃ sadevotpadyata iti siddhāntaḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: 'And because of the nature of the cause.' The meaning is: because of the existence of the cause. If a non-existent effect were to arise, why would the existence of the effect depend on the existence of the cause? And it does so depend. Therefore, it is understood that the effect exists in the form of power in the cause. Alternatively — 'because of the nature of the cause' means 'because of the essential nature of the cause.' The effect has the same essential nature as the cause. Just as from sesame seeds, whose nature is oily, only oily oil is produced; from clay, a pot of clay-nature is produced. If the effect were non-existent, it would be produced from things of non-existent nature — thus the established doctrine of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> is that only what exists is produced (<s>satkāryavāda</s>). // 9 //

children.text: kārikā 10
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 10]

children.text: evaṃ mahadādikāryaṃ sadevotpadyata iti vyavasthāpya prakṛtevirūpaṃ sarūpaṃ ca darśayati / tatra prakṛtervirūpamadhikṛtyāha-
children.translated_text: Having thus established that the effect beginning with <s>Mahat</s> is produced as already existent, he shows what is dissimilar and similar to <s>Prakṛti</s>. Regarding what is dissimilar to <s>Prakṛti</s>, he says:

children.text: hetumadanityamavyāpi sakriyamanekamāśritaṃ liṅgam /
children.translated_text: The manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) has a cause, is non-eternal, non-pervasive, active, manifold, dependent, inferential,

children.text: sāvayavaṃ paratantraṃ vyaktaṃ, viparītamavyaktam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: composite, and subordinate. The unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is the opposite. // ISk 10 //

children.text: 'hetumat'; ityādi / vyaktaṃ mahadādibhūtaparyantam / avyaktaṃ pradhānaṃ tatra vyaktaṃ hetumat, yathāsvaṃ kāraṇebhya utpadyamānatvāt / tatra pradhānādutpadyamāno mahān hetumān, mahato 'haṅkāro hetumān, ahaṅkārāttanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇyutpadyamānāni hetumanti ca, tanmātrebhyaśca mahābhūtāni hetumanti / viparītamavyaktamahetumadityarthaḥ, tasyānyataḥ kutaścidanutpādāt / nahi pradhānākiṃcidaparamasti yatastadutpadyate //
children.translated_text: 'Having a cause' and so on. The manifest is the products from <s>Mahat</s> to the gross elements. The unmanifest is <s>Pradhāna</s>. There, the manifest has a cause, since it is produced from its respective causes. <s>Mahat</s>, being produced from <s>Pradhāna</s>, has a cause; <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), being produced from <s>Mahat</s>, has a cause; the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) and the eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs), being produced from <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, have causes; and the <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements), being produced from the <s>tanmātras</s>, have causes. The opposite — the unmanifest is without cause, since it is not produced from anything else. For there is nothing prior to <s>Pradhāna</s> from which it would be produced.

children.text: anityaṃ vyaktam, kāraṇebhya utpannatvāt ghaṭādivat / kāraṇāni ca prāguktānyeva / viparītamavyaktaṃ nityamityarthaḥ, kutaścidanutpannatvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest is non-eternal, since it is produced from causes, like pots and the like. And the causes are those previously stated. The opposite — the unmanifest is eternal, since it is not produced from anything.

children.text:
avyāpi vyaktaṃ prādeśikamityarthaḥ / daivaṃ mānuṣaṃ tairyagyonaṃ ca, tadānīmanyatrāvartamānatvāt / sarvagataṃ viparītamavyaktaṃ vyāpītyarthaḥ, devādiṣu triṣu lokeṣu sarvadā vartamānatvāt /
'sakriyam'; iti / kriyāśabdenātra saṃsaraṇamabhipretam, na kriyāmātram / mahadādisūkṣmaparyantaṃ vyaktaṃ devādi saṃsaratītyarthaḥ / viparītamavyaktam, asaṃsāri / triṣu lokeṣu sthitatvānna saṃsarati / na punaḥ kriyaiva nāstīti niṣkriyam, tasya jagatkartṛtvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest is non-pervasive, meaning it is localized — in the divine, human, and animal realms — since at any given time it does not exist elsewhere. The opposite — the unmanifest is all-pervading, since it always exists in the three worlds — divine and others. 'Active' — by the word 'action' here, transmigration is intended, not mere activity. The meaning is: the manifest, from <s>Mahat</s> to the subtle body, transmigrates through divine and other states. The opposite — the unmanifest does not transmigrate, since it abides in all three worlds, it does not transmigrate. But it is not that it has no activity at all, since it is the creator of the world.

children.text: anekaṃ vyaktam, mahadādibhūtaparyantatāyāstrayoviṃśatiprakāratvāt / viparītaṃ vyaktam, trayāṇāṃ lokānāṃ tasyaikasya kāraṇatvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest is manifold, since from <s>Mahat</s> to the gross elements, it is of twenty-three kinds. The opposite — the unmanifest [is singular], since it alone is the cause of the three worlds.

children.text: 'āśritam'; iti / yadyasmādutpannaṃ mahadādi vyaktaṃ tadeva tadāśritaṃ nānyat / utpannamanyadāśritamiti darśanārthaṃ vacanam, anyathā hetumadityanenaivāśritaṃ siddhameva / viparītamavyaktam, anāśritam / tato 'nyasya kāraṇasyābhāvāt //
children.translated_text: 'Dependent.' The manifest — <s>Mahat</s> and the others — having been produced from something, depends on that very thing and nothing else. The statement that what is produced depends on another is for the purpose of showing [something specific]; otherwise, 'dependent' would already be established by the term 'having a cause.' The opposite — the unmanifest is independent, since there is no other cause for it.

children.text:
'liṅgam'; iti / liṅgyate 'nenāvyaktamiti liṅgam / viparītamavyaktam, na liṅgyate kiñcidaneneti / athavā layaṃ gacchatīti liṅgam /
pralayakāle hyākāśādayaḥ pañca yathākramaṃ śabdāditanmātreṣu līyante, tanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi cāhaṅkāre, ahaṅkāro mahati, mahānpradhāna iti / viparītamavyaktam, na kutracididaṃ līyate, ahetutvāt //
children.translated_text: '<s>Liṅga</s>' (mark/sign): That by which the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is inferred is the <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark). The unmanifest is the opposite — nothing is inferred by it. Or alternatively, that which dissolves (<s>laya</s>) is <s>liṅga</s>. For at the time of cosmic dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>), the five [elements] beginning with space (<s>ākāśa</s>) dissolve sequentially into their respective subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>) beginning with sound; the subtle elements and the sense organs dissolve into <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego); <s>ahaṅkāra</s> into <s>mahat</s> (cosmic intellect); and <s>mahat</s> into <s>pradhāna</s> (the primal cause). The unmanifest is the opposite — it does not dissolve anywhere, because it has no cause.

children.text: 'sāvayavam'; iti / śabdādayo 'vayavā ucyante / tairādhyātmikaṃ bāhyaṃ ca vyaktaṃ yuktam / viparītamavyaktam, tairayuktatvāt //
children.translated_text: 'Having parts' (<s>sāvayava</s>): Sound and the other [subtle elements] are called parts (<s>avayavas</s>). The manifest (<s>vyakta</s>), both internal and external, is endowed with them. The unmanifest is the opposite, because it is not endowed with them.

children.text: paratantram / na svatantram / yadasmādutpadyate tadevānuruddhya svakāryaṃ janayati na tadvyatirekeṇeti darśanārtham / anyathā hetumadityanenaiva paratantratvaṃ prasiddhameva / viparītamavyaktam, svatantraṃ na kiṃcidapekṣate // 10 //
children.translated_text: 'Dependent' (<s>paratantra</s>): Not independent. That which is produced from this [cause] generates its own effect only in conformity with [that cause], not independently of it — this is [stated] to demonstrate [dependence]. Otherwise, dependence is already well-established by the [earlier statement] 'having a cause' (<s>hetumat</s>). The unmanifest is the opposite — it is independent, not depending on anything. ||10||

children.text: kārikā 11
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 11

children.text: sārūpyamadhikṛtyāha-
children.translated_text: Regarding the similarity [between the manifest and the unmanifest], he says:

children.text: triguṇamaviveki viṣayaḥ sāmānyamacetanamprasavadharmi /
children.translated_text: The manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) has three <s>guṇas</s>, is non-discriminating, is an object [of experience], is common, is non-conscious, and is productive.

children.text: vyaktaṃ, tathā pradhānam, tadviparītastathā ca pumān || 11 ||
children.translated_text: So too is <s>pradhāna</s> (the primal cause). <s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious self) is the opposite of these, and also [different in other ways]. // ISk 11 //

children.text: 'triguṇam'; ityādi / trayassattvādayo guṇā yasya tattriguṇaṃ vyaktam / tathā pradhānamapi triguṇaṃ tatsvabhāvatvāt //
children.translated_text: 'Having three <s>guṇas</s>' (<s>triguṇa</s>): That which has the three <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the others — is called <s>triguṇa</s>; [this is] the manifest. So too is <s>pradhāna</s> <s>triguṇa</s>, because that is its essential nature.

children.text: 'aviveki'; iti / avivecanaśīlaṃ vyaktam, acetanatvāt / yadvā guṇebhyastasya pṛthaktvābhāvādaviveki / tathā pradhānamapi //
children.translated_text: 'Non-discriminating' (<s>aviveki</s>): The manifest has the character of non-discrimination, because it is non-conscious. Or, because of the absence of its separateness from the <s>guṇas</s>, it is non-discriminating. So too is <s>pradhāna</s>.

children.text: sāmānyaṃ vyaktam, sarvapuruṣopabhogyatvānmalladāsīvat / tathā pradhānamapi //
children.translated_text: 'Common' (<s>sāmānya</s>): The manifest is common, because it is to be enjoyed by all <s>puruṣas</s>, like a wrestler's female servant. So too is <s>pradhāna</s>.

children.text: acetanaṃ vyaktam, sukhaduḥkhamohānna vedayatītyarthaḥ / tathā pradhānamapi //
children.translated_text: 'Non-conscious' (<s>acetana</s>): The manifest is non-conscious — the meaning is that it does not experience pleasure, pain, or delusion. So too is <s>pradhāna</s>.

children.text: 'prasavadharmi'; iti / prasavo dharmo 'syāstīti prasavadharmi vyaktam / tathā pradhānamapi / dvayorapi prasavadharmitvam //
children.translated_text: 'Productive' (<s>prasavadharmi</s>): That which has production as its property is <s>prasavadharmi</s> — [this is] the manifest. So too is <s>pradhāna</s>. Both have the property of being productive.

children.text: tathā ca pradhānānmahān, mahato 'ṅkāra ityādinā svakāryotpādanadharmatvādyathā vyaktāvyaktayorvairūpyaṃ sārūpyaṃ ca, tathā kiṃ puruṣasya vāpītyāha- 'tadviparītastathā ca pumān'; iti / vyaktāvyaktābhyāṃ kaiściddharmairvilakṣaṇa ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And so, from <s>pradhāna</s> [arises] <s>mahat</s>, from <s>mahat</s> [arises] <s>ahaṅkāra</s> — and so on, because of the property of producing their own effects. Just as there is both difference and similarity between the manifest and the unmanifest, so what about <s>puruṣa</s>? — to this he says: '<s>Puruṣa</s> is the opposite of these, and also [different in other ways].' The meaning is that [<s>puruṣa</s>] is distinguished from both the manifest and the unmanifest by certain properties.

children.text: atra pūrvasyā āryāyā artho yojyate / hetumadvyaktam, ahetumadavyaktam / puruṣo 'pyahetumān, tasya kutaścidanutpādāt //
children.translated_text: Here the meaning of the previous <s>āryā</s> [verse] is to be connected: The manifest has a cause; the unmanifest is without cause. <s>Puruṣa</s> too is without cause, since it is not produced from anything.

children.text: anityaṃ vyaktam, nityamavyaktam / puruṣo nityaḥ, kutaścidanutpannatvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest is non-eternal; the unmanifest is eternal. <s>Puruṣa</s> is eternal, because it is not produced from anything.

children.text: avyāpi vyaktam, vyāpyavyaktam / puruṣo 'pi vyāpī yadā prakṛtyā muktaḥ / yuktaścet, vyaktena sadṛśo na pradhānena / hi sarvadā devādiṣu pravartate //
children.translated_text: The manifest is non-pervasive; the unmanifest is pervasive. <s>Puruṣa</s> too is pervasive when liberated from <s>Prakṛti</s>. But when conjoined [with <s>Prakṛti</s>], it is similar to the manifest, not to <s>pradhāna</s> — for it always operates in [forms such as] gods and others.

children.text: sakriyaṃ vyaktam, niṣkriyamavyaktam, asaṃsāritvāt / puruṣo 'pi niṣkriyaḥ, kartṛtvābhāvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest is active; the unmanifest is inactive, because of not being in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). <s>Puruṣa</s> too is inactive, because of the absence of agency.

children.text: anekaṃ vyaktam, ekamavyaktam / puruṣo 'neko bahutvāt / tasya bahutvaṃ pratipādayiṣyati / pradhānenātra vaisādṛśyaṃ tasyaikatvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest is many; the unmanifest is one. <s>Puruṣa</s> is many, because of multiplicity — he will establish its multiplicity [later]. Here there is dissimilarity with <s>pradhāna</s>, because of its [<s>pradhāna</s>'s] oneness.

children.text: āśritaṃ vyaktam, anāśritamavyaktam / puruṣo 'pyanāśritaḥ kutaścidanutpannatvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest is dependent; the unmanifest is independent. <s>Puruṣa</s> too is independent, because it is not produced from anything.

children.text: liṅgaṃ vyaktam, aliṅgamavyaktam / puruṣo 'pyaliṅgaḥ / na kiṃcidanena liṅgyate na vāyaṃ kadācillīyate 'nutpannatvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest is a <s>liṅga</s> (mark/sign); the unmanifest is without mark (<s>aliṅga</s>). <s>Puruṣa</s> too is without mark — nothing is inferred by it, nor does it ever dissolve, because it is unproduced.

children.text:
sāvayavaṃ vyaktam, niravayavamavyaktam / puruṣo 'pi niravayavaḥ śabdādibhirayuktatvāt /
paratantraṃ vyaktam, svatantramavyaktam / puruṣo 'pi svatantraḥ, kutaścidanutpannatvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest has parts; the unmanifest is without parts. <s>Puruṣa</s> too is without parts, because it is not endowed with sound and the other [elements]. The manifest is dependent; the unmanifest is independent. <s>Puruṣa</s> too is independent, because it is not produced from anything.

children.text:
dvitīyasyā āryāyā artho yojyate-
triguṇaṃ vyaktamavyaktaṃ ca / nirguṇaḥ puruṣaḥ, guṇānāṃ tatrābhāvāt //
children.translated_text: The meaning of the second <s>āryā</s> [verse] is to be connected: The manifest and the unmanifest both have three <s>guṇas</s>. <s>Puruṣa</s> is without <s>guṇas</s>, because of the absence of <s>guṇas</s> in it.

children.text: aviveki vyaktamavyaktaṃ ca / vivekī puruṣaścetanatvāt / vivikto vā nirguṇatvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest and the unmanifest are both non-discriminating. <s>Puruṣa</s> is discriminating, because of being conscious. Or [it is] distinct (<s>vivikta</s>), because of being without <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: viṣayo vyaktamavyaktaṃ ca / puruṣo nirviṣayaḥ, bhoktṛtvāt, na bhogyaḥ //
children.translated_text: The manifest and the unmanifest are both objects [of experience]. <s>Puruṣa</s> is without an object, because of being the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) — it is not something to be experienced.

children.text: sāmānyaṃ vyaktamavyaktaṃ ca / puruṣo 'sāmānyaḥ, aviṣayatvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest and the unmanifest are both common. <s>Puruṣa</s> is not common, because of not being an object [of experience].

children.text: acetanaṃ vyaktamavyaktaṃ ca / cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ sukhādivedanatvāt //
children.translated_text: The manifest and the unmanifest are both non-conscious. <s>Puruṣa</s> is conscious, because of experiencing pleasure and the rest.

children.text: prasavadharmi vyaktamavyaktaṃ ca / puruṣo 'prasavadharmī, akartṛtvāt / ityuktam // 11 //
children.translated_text: The manifest and the unmanifest are both productive. <s>Puruṣa</s> is non-productive, because of the absence of agency. Thus it has been stated. ||11||

children.text: kārikā 12
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 12

children.text: trayāṇāmapi vairūpyaṃ sārūpyaṃ ceti triguṇamityukte, ke ke trayo guṇāḥ kimātmakā ityāha-
children.translated_text: Having stated both the difference and the similarity of all three — and having said 'having three <s>guṇas</s>' — what are these three <s>guṇas</s> and what is their nature? To this he says:

children.text: prītyaprītiviṣādātmakāḥ prakāśapravṛttiniyamārthāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>guṇas</s> have the nature of pleasure, displeasure, and depression; their purposes are illumination, activity, and restraint;

children.text: anyo 'nyābhibhavāśrayajananamithunavṛttayaśca guṇāḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: they mutually overpower, support, generate, accompany, and function [together]. // ISk 12 //

children.text: 'prītyaprītiviṣādātmakāḥ'; ityādi / prītyādaya ātmāno yeṣāṃ guṇānāṃ te tathoktāḥ sattvarajastamāṃsi trayo guṇāḥ / tatra prītyātmakaṃ sukhātmakaṃ sattvam, aprītyātmakaṃ duḥkhātmakaṃ rajaḥ, viṣādātmakaṃ mohātmakaṃ tamaḥ / guṇā hyatīndriyatvātpariṇatyā sukhādinānumīyamānāstadātmakā iti vyapadiśyante //
children.translated_text: 'Having the nature of pleasure, displeasure, and depression': Those <s>guṇas</s> whose selves (essential natures) are pleasure and the rest are so called — [they are] the three <s>guṇas</s>: <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. Of these, <s>sattva</s> has the nature of pleasure (<s>prīti</s>), i.e., the nature of happiness (<s>sukha</s>); <s>rajas</s> has the nature of displeasure (<s>aprīti</s>), i.e., the nature of pain (<s>duḥkha</s>); <s>tamas</s> has the nature of depression (<s>viṣāda</s>), i.e., the nature of delusion (<s>moha</s>). Since the <s>guṇas</s> are beyond the senses, they are inferred through their transformations as pleasure etc., and are designated as having that nature.

children.text: kiṃ punareṣāṃ prayojanamityāha- 'prakāśapravṛttiniyamārthāḥ'; iti / prakāśārthaṃ sattvaṃ prakāśakatvāt, pravṛttyarthaṃ rajaścalatvāt, niyamārthaṃ tamaḥ stimitatvāt //
children.translated_text: What then is their purpose? To this he says: 'Their purposes are illumination, activity, and restraint.' <s>Sattva</s> serves the purpose of illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>), because it illuminates. <s>Rajas</s> serves the purpose of activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), because it is mobile. <s>Tamas</s> serves the purpose of restraint (<s>niyama</s>), because it is inert.

children.text: kimiti te guṇāḥ parasparasavyapekṣāḥ kiṃ vā netyāha- 'anyo 'nyābhibhavāśrayajananamithunavṛttayaśca guṇāḥ'; iti / anyo 'nyaśabdaḥ pratyekamabhisambaddhyate / abhibhavatītyabhibhavaḥ / pacādyac / anyo 'nyasyābhibhavā anyo 'nyābhibhavāḥ / tadyathā deveṣu sattvamudriktaṃ rajastamasī abhibhavati, manuṣyeṣu rajaḥ sattvatamasī, tiryakṣu (tamaḥ sattvarajasī) / āśrīyanta ityāśrayāḥ / karmaṇyaṇ / anyo 'nyasyāśrayāḥ, tridaṇḍavat / nāśrayāntarameṣām, anāśrayāśca kartāraḥ / janayantīti jananāḥ / 'kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam'; iti kartari lyuṭ / anekārthatvāt ca dhātūnāṃ bodhanārthā draṣṭavyāḥ / anyo 'nyasya prabodhakā ityarthaḥ / sarvaṃ hi vyaktamutpadyamānaṃ triguṇātmakamutpadyate / tatra yadā sattvamutkaṭaṃ tadā rajastamasī nyakkṛtaśaktike / prabodhyāyaskānto lohavaduktam (?) / satvanyatkṛtena guṇena vyaktaṃ janayati (?) evaṃ rajastamaśca yojyam / yadā guṇadvayamudbhūtaśakti tadā dvayamapītaradabhibhavati, prabodhayatītyarthaḥ / anyo 'nyamithunā iti / anyo 'nyasya sahāyā ityarthaḥ / tathā coktaṃ viṣṇugītāyām-
rajaso mithunaṃ sattvaṃ sattvasya mithunaṃ rajaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Sattva</s> is the companion of <s>rajas</s>, <s>rajas</s> is the companion of <s>sattva</s>;

children.text: ubhayoḥ sattvarajasormithunaṃ tama ucyate //
children.translated_text: and <s>tamas</s> is said to be the companion of both <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>.'

Are the <s>guṇas</s> mutually dependent or not? To this he says: 'They mutually overpower, support, generate, accompany, and function [together].' The word 'mutual' (<s>anyonya</s>) connects with each [verb] separately. 'Overpowering' (<s>abhibhava</s>) — that which overpowers. [The suffix] <s>pac</s> etc. Mutual overpowering means: among the gods, <s>sattva</s> predominates and overpowers <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>; among humans, <s>rajas</s> [overpowers] <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>; among animals, <s>tamas</s> [overpowers] <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>. 'Supports' (<s>āśraya</s>) — they are relied upon. Mutual support, like a tripod. They have no other support, and without support they are not agents. 'Generating' (<s>janana</s>) — they generate. The <s>lyuṭ</s> suffix in the agent sense, from 'the <s>lyuṭ</s> suffix after <s>kṛtya</s> is frequent.' And since verbal roots have multiple meanings, they should be understood in the sense of 'awakening.' They mutually awaken each other — this is the meaning. For every manifest thing that is produced is produced with the nature of all three <s>guṇas</s>. When <s>sattva</s> is predominant, then <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> have their powers diminished. Like a magnet awakening iron, so it is said. <s>Sattva</s>, activated by another <s>guṇa</s>, produces the manifest effect — similarly <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> should be understood. When two <s>guṇas</s> have their powers heightened, they too overpower the third and awaken [each other] — this is the meaning. 'Mutual companionship' means: they are each other's companions — this is the meaning. And so it is stated in the <s>Viṣṇu Gītā</s>:

children.text: ekasyāṃ vyaktau trayāṇāmabhibhavaprabodhanānuktau vyaktam, itare tu tau eva pravṛttiṃ janayanta iti darśayannāha- anyo 'nyavṛttaya iti / vṛttiḥ sukhādirūpeṇa pariṇatiḥ / vṛtihetutvād vṛttaya ucyante / anyonyavṛttihetava ityarthaḥ / tadyathā kācidyoṣidrūpaśīladatyantaguṇā (!) sitatvātsāttvikī sā bharttuḥ sukhamutpādayati sapatnīnāṃ kāsāṃcidduḥkhaṃ kāsāṃcidviṣādamityatra sattvamātmano dvayośca vṛttihetuḥ / kasyacitprabhoratyantaśūratvād bhṛtyā rājasāḥ, pareṣāṃ yudhyamānānāṃ prahārairduḥkhaṃ janayanti, palāyamānānāṃ viṣādam, svāminaśca tuṣṭimityatra raja ātmano dvayosca vṛttihetuḥ / meghāṃścāmbugu.....vāniṣāndhakārīkṛtyonnatatvāt (?) tāmasāḥ, te varṣantaḥ proṣitabhartṛkāṇāṃ viṣādaṃ janayanti, pathikānāṃ duḥkham kṛṣīvalānāṃ tuṣṭimityatra tama ātmano dvayośca vṛttihetuḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: When in a single manifest [entity] the overpowering and awakening of the three [<s>guṇas</s>] has been stated as the manifest, the other two produce activity — showing this, he says: 'They function mutually.' <s>Vṛtti</s> (function) means transformation into the form of pleasure etc. They are called <s>vṛttis</s> because they cause the function. 'They are mutual causes of function' — this is the meaning. For example: a certain woman of extremely beautiful form and character — being <s>sāttvika</s> due to her radiance — produces happiness for her husband, pain for some co-wives, and depression for others. Thus <s>sattva</s> is the cause of its own function and the functions of the other two. For some lord of extreme valor, his servants, being <s>rājasa</s> (of the nature of <s>rajas</s>), produce pain for enemies in battle through blows, depression for those who flee, and satisfaction for their master. Thus <s>rajas</s> is the cause of its own function and the functions of the other two. And clouds [...] making [things] dark through their height — being <s>tāmasa</s> (of the nature of <s>tamas</s>) — when they rain, they produce depression for women whose husbands are abroad, pain for travelers, and satisfaction for farmers. Thus <s>tamas</s> is the cause of its own function and the functions of the other two. ||12||

children.text: kārikā 13
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 13

children.text: eṣāṃ durlakṣaṇānāṃ lakṣaṇāntaramāha-
children.translated_text: He states another definition of these difficult-to-characterize [<s>guṇas</s>]:

children.text: sattvaṃ laghu prakāśakamupaṣṭambhakaṃ calaṃ ca rajaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> is light and illuminating; <s>rajas</s> is stimulating and mobile;

children.text: guru varaṇakameva tamaḥ, pradīpavaccārthato vṛttiḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: <s>tamas</s> is heavy and veiling. They function purposefully, like a lamp. // ISk 13 //

children.text: 'sattvam'; ityādi / iṣṭaṃ sāṃkhyācāryāṇāṃ sattvaṃ laghusvabhāvaṃ prakāśaṃ ca / yasyodrekāccharīreṃ 'śāni laghūni bhavanti, viṣayaprakāśanasamarthāni cendriyāṇi / bāhyāni ca dravyāṇi laghūni prakāśātmakāni nirmalāni bhavanti //
children.translated_text: '<s>Sattva</s>': It is the position of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers that <s>sattva</s> is light by nature and illuminating. When it predominates, the body and limbs become light, and the sense organs become capable of illuminating their objects. And external substances too become light, luminous in nature, and pure.

children.text: 'upaṣṭambhakaṃ calaṃ ca rajaḥ'; iti / upaṣṭambhayatītyupaṣṭambhakam / yasyodrekād devadatto vyavasyati, calacittaśca bhavati / bāhyāni calāni bhavantīti //
children.translated_text: 'Stimulating and moving is <s>rajas</s>' — that which stimulates is the stimulant. Through its predominance, <s>Devadatta</s> becomes resolute, and also restless-minded. External things too become moving.

children.text: 'guru varaṇakameva tamaḥ'; iti / vṛṇoti pidhatta iti / 'kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam'; iti kartari lyuṭ, karaṇe vā / paścāt svārthe kan / yasyodrekād gurūṇyaṅgāni bhavanti, indriyāṇi ca tamasaivāttāni bhavanti / bāhyāni ca gurūṇyanirmalāni ca bhavanti //
children.translated_text: 'Heavy and covering alone is <s>tamas</s>' — it covers, conceals. By the grammatical rule '<s>kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam</s>,' the suffix <s>lyuṭ</s> is in the agent or instrument sense; afterwards, the suffix <s>kan</s> in its own sense. Through its predominance, the limbs become heavy, and the senses are consumed by <s>tamas</s>. External things too become heavy and impure.

children.text: udāharaṇadigiyamanyānyapi vijñeyāni bhavanti / tathā cāhuḥ- prītiprīti(?)svābhiṣaṅgalāghavāni prasādaharṣau ca, stambhauddhatyadveṣacalanaśoṣaṇatāpabhedāśca, varaṇāpadhvaṃsanasādanagauravadainyabhītayaścaitāni sattvarajastamasāṃ krameṇa jñātavyāni liṅgāni //
children.translated_text: This is merely an indication through examples; other [signs] too should be understood. And thus they say: pleasure, delight, attachment, lightness, lucidity, and joy; immobility, agitation, hatred, motion, desiccation, heat, and splitting; covering, destruction, depression, heaviness, misery, and fear — these are the signs of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> respectively, to be known in order.

children.text: nanu caite parasparavilakṣaṇā guṇā viruddhatvāt kathaṃ sambhūyaikatra vartanta ityāha- 'pradīpavaccārthato vṛttiḥ'; iti / pradīpasyeva pradīpavat / tailavarttyagnisamudāyaḥ pradīpaḥ / yadā samudāyātma.....parasparavilakṣaṇānāmapi pradīpabhā...pravṛtiḥ, tamasi sthitā ghaṭādayo devadattasya prakāśayitavyā iti, tathā sattvarajastamasāṃ puruṣārthahetunā pravṛttiḥ, puruṣārthaśabdopalabdhiśceti // 13 //
children.translated_text: But if these <s>guṇas</s> are mutually distinct, how can they, being contradictory, function together in one entity? — he says: 'Like a lamp, their activity is purposeful.' Just as a lamp — the aggregate of oil, wick, and fire is a lamp. When the identity is collective... even those mutually distinct [elements], like the light of a lamp... activity — pots etc. situated in darkness are to be illuminated for <s>Devadatta</s> — so the activity of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> is for the sake of the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>; and the expression 'purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>' means apprehension. ||13||

children.text: kārikā 14
children.translated_text: Kārikā 14

children.text: nanu ca 'triguṇamaviveki viṣayaḥ sāmānyamacetanaṃ prasavadharmi vyaktam', tatra sukhaduḥkamohopalabdhestraiguṇyaṃ vyaktaṃ siddham, avivekyādayo dharmāḥ prasavaparyantāḥ kathaṃ siddhyantītyāha-
children.translated_text: But if 'the manifest is constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>, non-discriminating, objective, common, non-conscious, and productive,' and the three-<s>guṇa</s> nature of the manifest is established through the perception of pleasure, pain, and delusion, how are the other properties — from non-discrimination through productivity — established? To this he says—

children.text: avivekyādissiddhastraiguṇyāttadviparyayābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Non-discrimination and the other [properties] are established from the three-<s>guṇa</s> nature; from the absence of its contrary,

children.text: kāraṇaguṇātmakatvātkāryasyāvyaktamapi siddham || 14 ||
children.translated_text: and because the effect has the nature of the cause's <s>guṇas</s>, the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) too is established. || 14 ||

children.text: 'avivekyādiḥ siddhaḥ'; ityādi / guṇidvāreṇa guṇābhidhānam / avivekyādiguṇassiddhaḥ / vyakta iti vākyaśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Non-discrimination etc. is established' — etc. The <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) are stated through the <s>guṇin</s> (the entity possessing qualities). The property of non-discrimination etc. is established — 'in the manifest' is the completion of the sentence.

children.text: kutaḥ? traiguṇyāt / kathaṃ? yasmādguṇā evāvivekino bhogyāssāmānyā acetanā prasavadharmiṇaśca, te ca vyakte siddhā iti siddho guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: From what? From the three-<s>guṇa</s> nature. How? Since the <s>guṇas</s> themselves are non-discriminating, enjoyable, common, non-conscious, and productive, and since these are established in the manifest — the property is established.

children.text: 'tadviparyayābhāvāt'; iti / (traiguṇyasyābhāvāditi) / traiguṇyasyābhāve 'vivekyādayorabhāvāt / na hi nirguṇasya puruṣasyāvivekyādiḥ sambhavati / tasmāttraiguṇyādevāvivekyādissiddhaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'From the absence of its contrary' — (from the absence of the three-<s>guṇa</s> nature) — in the absence of the three-<s>guṇa</s> nature, there would be absence of non-discrimination etc. For the <s>guṇa</s>-less <s>Puruṣa</s>...

children.text: evaṃ ca sati, pradhānamapi traiguṇyāttathāvidhaṃ siddham / yadāha- 'kāraṇaguṇātmakatvātkāryasyāvyaktamapi siddham'; iti / kāraṇasya yo guṇaḥ sa ātmā svabhāvo yasya tattathoktam / tasya svabhāvastattvam / tasmādiha loke kāraṇaguṇakaṃ kāryaṃ dṛṣṭam / śuklaiḥ kṛṣṇairvā tantubhirārabdhaḥ paṭaḥ śuklaḥ kṛṣṇo vā bhavati / yadyavyaktaṃ tathāvidhaṃ na syāt, kathaṃ vyaktaṃ tathāvidhaṃ bhavet // 14 //
children.translated_text: And thus, <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primal Nature) too is established as being of such a nature through the three-<s>guṇa</s> nature. As he says: 'because the effect has the nature of the cause's <s>guṇas</s>, the unmanifest too is established' — since the <s>guṇas</s> of the effect exist in the cause...

children.text: kārikā 15
children.translated_text: Kārikā 15

children.text: nanu ca sati dharmiṇi dharmāścintyante, pradhānasyaiva dharmiṇo 'labdhasiddhitvāt kathamavivekyādītyāha-
children.translated_text: But if properties are considered only when there is a property-bearer, and since the very existence of <s>Pradhāna</s> as the property-bearer has not been established, how can there be non-discrimination etc.? — he says:

children.text: bhedānāṃ parimāṇāt samanvayācchaktitaḥ pravṛtteśca /
children.translated_text: From the finiteness of the distinctions, from the coordination, from the activity due to potency,
