children.text: kāraṇakāryavibhāgādavibhāgādvaiśvarūpyasya || 15 ||
children.translated_text: from the division of cause and effect, and from the non-separation of the variegated [world]. || 15 ||

children.text: 'bhedānām'; ityādi / kāryatastadupalabdhermahadādi tacca kāryamityanenaiva sādhite 'smin yathāvadadhigate punardārḍhyārthaṃ samanantaropādānam / bhidyanta iti bhedāḥ kāryaviśeṣāsteṣāṃ (ekassaṃsargī dṛṣṭaḥ) parimāṇācca / bhedānāṃ parimitatvādityarthaḥ / yena ca parimitāsteṣāmekaḥ saṃsargī dṛṣṭaḥ / yathā mūlāṅkurapatrakāṇḍaprasavapuṣpataṇḍulakaṇānāṃ bhedānāṃ vrīhiḥ tavibāhyādhyātmikabhedāḥ / parimitabāhyā brahmādistambaparyantāścaturdaśa / ādhyātmikāśca mahadahaṅkāratanmātrendriyabhūtākhyāstrayoviṃśatiḥ / tasmādeteṣāmekena saṃsargiṇā bhavitavyam / yatraiṣāṃ saṃsargastadavyaktaṃ kāraṇamastīti sāmānyatodṛṣṭamanumānam //
children.translated_text: 'Of the distinctions' etc. Since the effect is established through its perception — <s>Mahat</s> (Intellect) etc. — by the very argument 'that is an effect,' once this is duly understood, further arguments are for the sake of additional corroboration...

children.text:
'samanvayāt'; bhedānāmiti vartate / samanvayo 'nugamaḥ / ekajātyanugamādityarthaḥ / ya ekajātyanugatā bhedāsteṣāmekameva tathābhūtaṃ kāraṇaṃ dṛṣṭam / yathā kaṭakakeyūrādīnāṃ suvarṇapiṇḍaḥ, yathā vā śarāvādīnāṃ mṛtpiṇḍaḥ / evameṣāmapi bāhyādhyātmikānāṃ sukhaduḥkhamohānugatatvādekena tathāvidhena bhavitavyam / ya eṣāṃ samudāyastatpradhānamiti sāmānyatodṛṣṭam /
'śaktitaḥ pravṛtteśca'; iti / iha kulālādiśaktipūrvikā ghaṭādīnāṃ pravṛttirdṛṣṭā nāśaktipūrvikā / eṣāmapi bāhyādhyātmikānāṃ pravṛttirdṛśyate / tataśca prāk ca pravṛtterjanitayā śaktyā bhavitavyam / yāsau śaktiḥ saivāvyaktabhāvamāpadyata iti sāmānyatodṛṣṭam //
children.translated_text: 'From the coordination' — 'of the distinctions' continues. 'Coordination' means concomitance. 'From concomitance of one kind' — the meaning is: those distinctions that follow one kind have a single...

children.text: 'kāraṇakāryavibhāgāt'; iti / kāraṇasya pūrvabhāvitvāt pūrvanipātaḥ / alpāctarasya pūrvanipātasyānityatvam / yata utpadyate tatkāraṇam, yaccotpadyate tatkāryam / yathā mṛtpiṇḍaghaṭayorjanyajanakatvena pṛthagarthakriyākaraṇācca vibhāgo dṛṣṭaḥ / anyathā ghaṭāsyodakāharaṇakriyā yā na sā mṛtpiṇḍasya, yā mṛtpiṇḍasya na sā ghaṭasya / evaṃ vyaktasya mahadādeḥ kāryatvātpṛthagarthakriyākaraṇācca vibhāgaḥ / tasmādasya kāraṇena bhavitavyam / taccāvyaktātkimanyat syāditi //
children.translated_text: 'From the division of cause and effect' — because the cause is prior, it is placed first. The prior placement of the fewer [syllables] is not a fixed rule. Since it is produced...

children.text: asmin vyākhyāne 'kāryatastadupalabdhermahadādi tacca kāryam'; ityanenaiva siddhatvādanyairanyathā vyākhyāyate / yadupakaroti taktāraṇam, yadupakriyate tatkāryaṃ tayorvibhāgāt, upakāryopakārakabhāvādityarthaḥ / tatra kārya...vyādīni śarīrasthāni sthānasādhanā...vabhogaiḥ kāraṇānyupakurvanti / kāraṇāni ca vṛddhikṣatasaṃrohaṇapālanaiḥ kāryāṇi / bāhyāni ca kāraṇāni pṛthivyā dhṛtisaṅgrahapattivyūhanāvakāśadānaiḥ parasparamupakurvanti / tathā daivamānuṣatairyagyonāni parasparopakārīṇi / tatra daivam, yathākālaṃ śītoṣṇavarṣāgamaḥ, mānuṣatairyagyonānyupakaroti / mānuṣamijyāyāgastutibhirdaivaṃ rakṣati, poṣaṇabheṣajyaiśaaha tairyagyonamupakaroti / yathādhyātmikānāṃ bāhyānāṃ copakāryopakārakabhāvo buddhikṛta iva dṛśyate tadasya kaścidvyavasthāpitā syāt, kuto 'yaṃ vibhāga ityanyathānupapatteḥ //
children.translated_text: In this explanation, since it is already established by 'that <s>Mahat</s> etc. is the effect, established through its perception,' others explain it differently. As a subsidiary [argument]...

children.text: 'avibhāgādvaiśvarūpyasya'; iti / na vidyate vibhāgo 'syetyavibhāgaḥ / avibhaktādityarthaḥ / tasmādvaiśvarūpyasyopalabdheriti śeṣaḥ / iha loke 'vibhaktādekasmādikṣudravyādrasaphāṇitaguḍakhaṇḍaśarkarādivaiśvarūpyaṃ nānātvaṃ dṛśyate, tathaikasmāddugdhāddadhimastunavanītaghṛtādivaiśvarūpyamupalabhyate / evamādhyātmikānāṃ bāhyānāṃ ca vaiśvarūpyam / tasmādeṣāmavibhaktenaiva bhavitavyamiti sāmānyatodṛṣṭam //
children.translated_text: 'From the non-separation of the variegated' — that which has no division is <s>avibhāga</s> (non-separation); the meaning is: from the undivided. Therefore, from the perception of the variegated [world]...

children.text:
anyastvāha- 'avibhāge vaiśvarūpyasya'; iti / avibhāgo layaḥ, vaiśvarūpyaṃ jagat nānārūpatvāt / pralayakāle vaiśvarūpyaṃ kva līyate sthityutpattipralayājjagata iti / na ceśvare layanaṃ sambhavati, tasya nirguṇatvenābhyupagamāt / tasmādanyathānupapattyāsti tadekamiti / tathā cāhuḥ-
pradhānādānupūrvyeṇa sṛṣṭirlokasya saṃsaraḥ /
pra....prātilomyena punastatraiva sañcaraḥ // iti // 15 //
children.translated_text: Another says: 'from the non-separation of the variegated' — '<s>avibhāga</s>' means dissolution; 'variegated' (<s>vaiśvarūpya</s>) means the world, from its having manifold forms. At the time of <s>pralaya</s> (cosmic dissolution), the variegated [world]...

children.text: kārikā 16
children.translated_text: Kārikā 16

children.text: eṣāṃ hetūnāṃ pravartanārthamāha-
children.translated_text: He states the purpose of the operation of these causes:

children.text: kāraṇamastyavyaktam, pravartate triguṇataḥ samudayācca /
children.translated_text: There exists the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) cause; it operates due to its three-<s>guṇa</s> nature and combination,

children.text: pariṇāmataḥ salilavat, pratipratiguṇāśrayaviśeṣāt || 16 ||
children.translated_text: transforming like water, according to the specific substrate of each <s>guṇa</s>. || 16 ||

children.text: 'kāraṇamasti'; ityādi //
children.translated_text: 'There exists a cause' — etc.

children.text: yadi kāraṇamastyavyaktaṃ tatkathaṃ pravartata ityāha- 'triguṇatassamudayācca'; iti / yadā prakṛtisthā guṇāssāmyena pravartante tadā (trīnevādhikṛtya pravarante naikaikamityarthaḥ / yadā vaiṣamyeṇa pravartante tadā) kāryaṃ kāraṇārabdhatvāt samudayāt pravartate / samantādudayo yasya guṇasya tamadhikṛtyetyarthaḥ, śeṣanyakkṛtaśaktikatvāt / yadi samudayādavyaktaṃ pravartate tasmādutpannaṃ tadavya...smānna bhavati //
children.translated_text: If the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) exists as the cause, then how does it operate? He says: 'From the conjunction of the three <s>guṇas</s>.' When the <s>guṇas</s> established in <s>Prakṛti</s> operate in equilibrium, then (they operate with reference to all three together, not to each one individually — this is the meaning. When they operate in disequilibrium, then) the effect operates from their conjunction, since it is initiated by the cause. The meaning is: that <s>guṇa</s> whose emergence is complete (<s>samudaya</s>) — with reference to that [the operation occurs], because the power of the remaining [<s>guṇas</s>] is subdued. If the unmanifest operates from conjunction, then what arises from it is not different from it.

children.text:
śuklebhyaḥ kṛṣṇebhyo vā tantubhyaḥ śuklaḥ kṛṣṇo vā paṭo bhavatītyāha-
'pariṇāmataḥ'; ityādi / pūrvasyāmavasthāyāmavasthāntaraṃ pariṇāmaḥ, tasmāddhetoḥ pravartate / yathā kaṇikāyāḥ sūkṣmāyā mūlakaḥ śākhāpraśākhādipravṛddho mahānvanaspatirvyakto bhavati, evamavyaktādvyaktaṃ pariṇamati //
children.translated_text: Just as from white or black threads a white or black cloth comes into being, he says: 'From transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>)' etc. The transition to another state from a prior state is <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation); from that cause [the effect] operates. Just as from a tiny seed, a large tree with roots, branches, and sub-branches becomes manifest, so from the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) transforms.

children.text: yadyevamekarūpādutpannasya trailokyasya kathamanekarūpatvamityāha- 'salilavatpratipratiguṇāśrayaviśeṣāt'; iti / salilena tulyaṃ vartata iti salilavat / ekaikaṃ prati guṇāḥ pratipratiguṇāḥ / ta evāśrayāsteṣāṃ yo viśeṣastasmāddhetoḥ pravartante / yathā salilamantarikṣādekarasamapi tadekasya kaṭvamlāderguṇasyāśrayabhūtasya viśeṣānnānārasaṃ vartate evamavyaktamapīti guṇātmakatvādekaikaguṇāśrayaviśeṣānnānārūpaṃ pravartate / tatra sattvasya kṛterāśrayasya viśeṣāddevabhāvena vartanam, rajasa āśrayasya viśeṣānmānuṣabhāvena, tamasa āśrayasya viśeṣāttiryagyonibhāveneti // 16 //
children.translated_text: If so, how does the three-world system arising from a single form have manifold forms? He says: 'Like water, due to the distinction of the substrate of each and every <s>guṇa</s>.' 'Like water' means 'operating in the same manner as water.' '<s>Pratipratiguṇa</s>' means 'the <s>guṇas</s> with respect to each one individually.' Those themselves are the substrates; from the distinction among them, [the effects] operate. Just as water falling from the sky, though of a single taste, becomes of various tastes due to the distinction of the substrate of a particular quality such as pungency, sourness, etc. — so too the unmanifest, being of the nature of the <s>guṇas</s>, produces manifold forms due to the distinction of the substrate of each individual <s>guṇa</s>. There, from the distinction of the substrate of <s>sattva</s>, [there is] existence in the divine state; from the distinction of the substrate of <s>rajas</s>, in the human state; from the distinction of the substrate of <s>tamas</s>, in the state of animal birth. ||16||

children.text: kārikā 17
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 17

children.text: evamavyaktasyāstitvaṃ pravṛttiṃ ca prasādhya puruṣāstitvaṃ prasādhayitumāha-
children.translated_text: Having thus established the existence and operation of the unmanifest, he says, in order to establish the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s>—

children.text: saṃghātaparārthatvāt triguṇādiviparyayādadhiṣṭhānāt /
children.translated_text: Because composites serve another's purpose; because [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is the reverse of the three <s>guṇas</s> etc.; because of the [need for a] presider;

children.text: puruṣo 'sti bhoktṛbhāvātkaivalyārthaṃ pravṛtteśca || 17 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> exists — because of the nature of being an experiencer, and because activity is for the purpose of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation/liberation). [ISk 17]

children.text: 'saṃghātaparārthatvāt'; ityādi / saṃhanyata iti saṃghātaḥ / saṃghātaścāsau parārthaśceti saṃghātaparārthaḥ / saṃghātatvaṃ hetuḥ parārthatvaṃ sādhyam / iha loke saṃghātabāhyāḥ śayanāsanādayo ye te parārthā dṛṣṭāḥ / te hi devadattasya parasyārthaṃ kurvanti na svārtham / ete 'pyādhyātmikā mahadādayaḥ śarīrasaṃjñakāḥ saṃghātāḥ, taiḥ parārthairbhavitavyam / na ca puruṣavyatirikto 'nyaḥ paro 'sti, puruṣa eva para i....nyatodṛṣṭam //
children.translated_text: 'Because composites serve another's purpose' etc. That which is compounded together is a composite (<s>saṃghāta</s>). It is both a composite and serves another's purpose — thus 'composite serving another's purpose.' Being a composite is the reason (<s>hetu</s>); serving another's purpose is what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>). In this world, external composites such as beds, seats, etc. are seen to serve another's purpose. For they serve the purpose of another, namely <s>Devadatta</s>, not their own purpose. These internal ones too — <s>mahat</s> (great principle) etc., designated as the body — are composites; they too must serve another's purpose. And there is no other apart from <s>Puruṣa</s> who is that 'other' — <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is the other. [This is established by] <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (general observation).

children.text: nanu mahadādibhūtaparyantaṃ śarīrameva puruṣo nānyaḥ kaścidityatrāha- 'triguṇādiviparyayāt'; iti / ādiśabdenāvivekyādayaḥ pañca dharmā dṛśyante / tathā hi tadviparītaḥ pumānityuktam / tataśca tadviparītatvātpuṃsaḥ kathaṃ mahadādimātrameva puruṣaḥ / tasmādvyatiriktaḥ puruṣo yasyārthakā ime saṃghātāḥ //
children.translated_text: Objection: The body alone, from <s>mahat</s> to the elements, is <s>Puruṣa</s>; there is no one else. To this he says: 'Because of being the reverse of the three <s>guṇas</s> etc.' By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), the five properties beginning with non-discrimination (<s>aviveka</s>) are indicated. For it was stated: '<s>Puruṣa</s> is the opposite of that.' Therefore, because of being opposite to that, how can <s>Puruṣa</s> be nothing more than <s>mahat</s> and the rest? Therefore <s>Puruṣa</s> is distinct — for whose purpose these composites exist.

children.text: 'adhiṣṭhānāt'; iti / adhitiṣṭhatyasminnityadhiṣṭhānam / mahadādibhūtaparyantaṃ śarīramiha loke yadadhiṣṭhānaṃ tatparādhiṣṭhitaṃ dṛṣṭam, yathā rathādi / dṛśyate cādhiṣṭhānaṃ śarīram / tasmādasyādhiṣṭhātrā bhavitavyam / yo 'sāvadhiṣṭhātā sa puruṣaḥ, nāntaḥkaraṇamadhiṣṭhātṛ, tasyācetanatvāditi sāmānyatodṛṣṭam //
children.translated_text: 'Because of the [need for a] presider.' That in which [something] presides is the seat of presiding (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>). In this world, the body — from <s>mahat</s> to the elements — which is a seat of presiding, is seen to be presided over by another, like a chariot etc. And the body is seen to be a seat of presiding. Therefore there must be a presider for it. That presider is <s>Puruṣa</s>, not the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), because it is insentient. [This is established by] <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (general observation).

children.text: 'bhoktṛbhāvāt'; iti / bhoktṛtvādityarthaḥ / iha loke bhogyaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhoktānumīyate / dṛśyate mahadādiparyantaṃ bhogyam, tasmādasyāpi bhoktrā bhavitavyamiti sāmānyatodṛṣṭam / na cāntaḥkaraṇaṃ bhoktṛ, tasyācetanatvādbhogyatvācca / yaśca bhoktā sa eva puruṣaḥ sātmakaṃ jīvaccharīraṃ prāṇādimattvāt / asmin dedhe yo 'yamātmā samānajātīyānekavastvantarasahāyaḥ, pratiniyatairjanmādibhiryujyamānatvāt manovat //
children.translated_text: 'Because of the nature of being an experiencer.' The meaning is: because of experiencer-hood. In this world, seeing what is to be experienced, an experiencer is inferred. From <s>mahat</s> onward, what is to be experienced is seen. Therefore there must be an experiencer for this too. [This is established by] <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (general observation). The inner organ is not the experiencer, because of its insentiency and because it is itself what is to be experienced. And the one who is the experiencer — that is <s>Puruṣa</s>. The embodied being possessing a self (<s>sātmaka</s>) is the living body, because of possessing vital breath etc. In this body, this self, accompanied by many other entities of the same class, because of being subject to specific births etc., is like the mind.

children.text: 'kaivalyārthaṃ pravṛtteśca'; iti / kaivalyaṃ mokṣaḥ / tadanyārthapradhānasyaiṣā pravṛttiḥ / tathāhi- pradhānaṃ buddhyātmanā pariṇamati / buddheścāṣṭādaśāni / teṣu ca jñānaṃ kaivalyam / tatra yadi puruṣo na syāttadā tadarthā pravṛttirna bhavet / tasmādanyathānupapattyā puruṣo 'sti //
children.translated_text: 'And because activity is for the purpose of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation).' <s>Kaivalya</s> is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). This activity is primarily for the purpose of something other [than itself]. Thus: <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature) transforms in the form of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). And <s>buddhi</s> has eighteen [modifications]. Among these, knowledge is <s>kaivalya</s>. If <s>Puruṣa</s> did not exist, then that purposeful activity would not take place. Therefore, by the reasoning of 'otherwise unexplained' (<s>anyathānupapatti</s>), <s>Puruṣa</s> exists.

children.text: tatra siddhe puṃsi vivādāḥ / eka evāyaṃ puruṣaḥ sarvaśarīreṣu sthita ityeke / sarve kāya upanatānekātmānassātmakatvāt, yogiśarīravṛṃda.. pratiśarīramanekaḥ puruṣa ityapare / eka eva purāṇaḥ puruṣaḥ, tasmādagnesa..viṣphuliṅgāḥ pratiśarīraṃ puruṣā ābirbhūtā iti vedāntavādinaḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: Regarding the established existence of <s>Puruṣa</s>, there are disputes. Some [say]: this <s>Puruṣa</s> is one alone, situated in all bodies. Others [say]: All bodies are endowed with multiple selves, because of being ensouled... <s>Puruṣa</s> is multiple, one per body. The <s>Vedānta</s> adherents [say]: There is one primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>; from him, like sparks from a fire, <s>Puruṣas</s> have manifested, one per body. ||17||

children.text:
kārikā 18
atrāha-
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 18. To this he says—

children.text: jananamaraṇakaraṇānāṃ pratiniyamādayugapatpravṛtteśca /
children.translated_text: Because of the specific allotment of birth, death, and sense-organs; and because of the non-simultaneous activity;

children.text: puruṣabahutvaṃ siddhaṃ traiguṇyaviparyayāccaiva || 18 ||
children.translated_text: the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> is established; and also because of the contrariety of the three <s>guṇas</s>. [ISk 18]

children.text: 'jananamaraṇakaraṇānām'; ityādi / karaṇaṃ cakṣurādīndriyam dehendriyāderadhiṣṭhānasyotpattivināśau / tadyogātpuruṣaḥ jananamaraṇe 'pi vyavasthāpyete / svataḥ puruṣasya te na sambhavataḥ / kutaḥ ? - nityatāt tatra yadyekaḥ puruṣaḥ syāttadaikasmin jāyamāne mriyamāṇe vā sarveṣāṃ jananamaraṇe syātām / tathaikasmiṃścakṣuṣmati śrotravati vā sarve 'ndhā (badhirā vā, paśyeyuḥ śruṇuyurvā / ekasminnandhe) badhire vā tathā syuḥ / na caivam, jananādīnāṃ pratiniyamāt / tasmādanyathānupapattyā puruṣabahutvaṃ siddham //
children.translated_text: 'Because of the specific allotment of birth, death, and sense-organs' etc. '<s>Karaṇa</s>' (organ) means the sense-organ of the eye, etc. — the arising and destruction of the seat of presiding consisting of body and sense-organs. Through their connection, <s>Puruṣa</s> too is associated with birth and death. By his own nature, these do not belong to <s>Puruṣa</s>. Why? — Because of his eternality. If there were a single <s>Puruṣa</s>, then when one is born or dies, all would be born or die. Similarly, when one has eyes or ears, all would be blind (or deaf, or would see or hear. When one is blind) or deaf, all would be so. But this is not the case, because of the specific allotment of birth, etc. Therefore, by the reasoning of 'otherwise unexplained,' the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> is established.

children.text: 'ayugapatpravṛtteśca'; iti / yadyekaḥ puruṣaḥ syāttadaikenādhiṣṭhātrā tiṣṭhati dehe, dharmādharmayorarthānarthayoḥ sukhaduḥkhayorvā pravṛtte, sarva eva yugapatpravartteran / na caivamityanyathānupapattiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'And because of non-simultaneous activity.' If there were a single <s>Puruṣa</s>, then, with a single presider standing in the body, when <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, benefit and harm, pleasure and pain arise, all would arise simultaneously. But this is not the case — thus [this is established by] the reasoning of 'otherwise unexplained.'

children.text: 'traiguṇyaviparyayācca'; iti / traya eva guṇāstraiguṇyam / tad viparyayo 'nyathātvam / adhiṣṭhānasya triguṇātmakatvāttadyogātpuruṣo 'pi triguṇātmaka ityucyate / tatra yadyekaḥ puruṣaḥ syāttadaikasmin sāttvike rājase tāmase vā, sarva eva tathāvidhāḥ syuḥ / na caivam, guṇānaṃ viparyayadarśanadityanyathānupapattiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'And because of the contrariety of the three <s>guṇas</s>.' The three <s>guṇas</s> alone constitute '<s>traiguṇya</s>.' Its 'contrariety' means 'being otherwise,' [i.e., variation]. Because the seat of presiding is constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>, through its connection, <s>Puruṣa</s> too is said to be constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>. If there were a single <s>Puruṣa</s>, then when one is <s>sāttvika</s>, <s>rājasa</s>, or <s>tāmasa</s>, all would be of the same kind. But this is not the case, because of the observed contrariety of the <s>guṇas</s> — thus [this is established by] the reasoning of 'otherwise unexplained.'

children.text: purāṇapuruṣādagneriva viṣphuliṅgāḥ pratiśarīraṃ puruṣā ityasminnapi darśane puruṣabahutvamastyeva / teṣāṃ parasparavilakṣaṇatvāt te purāṇapuruṣādabhinnā bhinnā veti darśanadvayam / tadanyatra vivāritatvādiha granthagauravabhayānnopanyastamasmābhiriti // 18 //
children.translated_text: Even in the view that '<s>Puruṣas</s> have manifested from the primordial <s>Puruṣa</s> like sparks from a fire, one per body' — plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> does exist. Since they are mutually different from each other, whether they are different or non-different from the primordial <s>Puruṣa</s> — these are two views. Since this has been discussed elsewhere, it is not presented here by us for fear of prolixity of the text. ||18||

children.text:
kārikā 19
evaṃ puruṣabahutvaṃ prasāddhya taddharmān kathayitumāha-
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 19. Having thus established the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s>, he says, in order to describe their properties—

children.text: tasmācca viparyāsātsiddhaṃ sākṣitvamasya puruṣasya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the reverse [of the <s>guṇas</s>], the witness-hood (<s>sākṣitva</s>) of this <s>Puruṣa</s> is established;

children.text: kaivalyammādhyasthaṃ draṣṭṛtvamakartṛbhāvaśca || 19 ||
children.translated_text: [as well as] isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>), neutrality (<s>mādhyasthya</s>), seer-hood (<s>draṣṭṛtva</s>), and the state of being a non-doer (<s>akartṛbhāva</s>). [ISk 19]

children.text: 'tasmācca viparyāsāt'; ityādi / yaḥ prāgukto viparyayaḥ- triguṇamaviveki viṣayaḥ - ityādinā, tasmātsākṣitvādayo dharmāḥ puruṣasya siddhāḥ / tatra nirguṇasya puruṣasyāprasavadharmitvādakartṛtvam / yaścākartā sa bhavatyudāsīnaḥ / saptavidhaṃ cāsyaudāsīnyam / tathā coktam -
paśyati śṛṇoti sarvama karoti sthitiṃ prasaṅgaṃ ca nāpi /
children.translated_text: He sees, he hears, all this he does, and yet remains in stillness; neither by proximity nor

children.text: svato na parato...nobhayataścāpyudāsīnaḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: by his own [effort], nor by another's, nor by both — he is indifferent.

'Therefore, from the reverse' etc. The previously stated reverse — 'constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>, non-discriminating, object' etc. — from that, the properties of <s>Puruṣa</s> such as witness-hood etc. are established. Among these: the non-doership of <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is without <s>guṇas</s>, [follows] from his being of the nature of non-production. And one who is a non-doer is indifferent (<s>udāsīna</s>). And his indifference is sevenfold. Thus it is said—

children.text: yaścodāsīnaḥ sa sākṣyapi bhavati pradhānasambandhinaḥ kriyākalāpasya nirguṇatvāt //
children.translated_text: And one who is indifferent is also a witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) of the entire set of activities belonging to <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature), because of being without <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: kaivalyaṃ kevalabhāvāt cetanatvācca draṣṭṛtvamiti //
children.translated_text: <s>Kaivalya</s> (isolation) is from the state of being alone (<s>kevalabhāva</s>); and seer-hood (<s>draṣṭṛtva</s>) is from consciousness (<s>cetanatva</s>).

children.text: nanu ca yadyakartā tatkathaṃ- bhoktṛbhāvādasti puruṣaḥ- ? tathā cāhuḥ-
children.translated_text: Objection: If [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is a non-doer, then how [can it be said that] '<s>Puruṣa</s> exists because of the nature of being an experiencer'? And thus they say—

children.text: bālahutāśanataravaḥ svayamakṛtānāṃ yathā hi bhoktāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as children, fire, and trees are experiencers of what they themselves have not produced,

children.text: puruṣo 'pi viṣayaphalānāṃ svayamakṛtānāṃ tathāpi bhoktā // iti //
children.translated_text: so too <s>Puruṣa</s> is the experiencer of the fruits of sense-objects that he himself has not produced.

children.text: ityuktamakarturapi bhoktṛtvamasyeti // 19 //
children.translated_text: Thus it has been stated that even a non-doer can be an experiencer. ||19||

children.text: kārikā 20
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 20

children.text: nanu ca yadyacetanamavyaktaṃ kathaṃ dehendriyasaṃjñamadhiṣṭhānaṃ dharmādharmādiṣu pravarttate, tasyācetanatvādityāha-
children.translated_text: Objection: If the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is insentient, how does the seat of presiding designated as body and sense-organs operate in <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, etc., given its insentiency? To this he says—

children.text: tasmāttatsaṃyogādacetanaṃ cetanāvadiva liṅgam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the conjunction with that [<s>puruṣa</s>], the non-conscious [<s>prakṛti</s>] appears as if conscious, like the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body).

children.text: guṇakartṛtve 'pi tathā karteva bhavatyudāsīnaḥ || 20 ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, though the agency belongs to the <s>guṇas</s>, the indifferent [<s>puruṣa</s>] appears as if it were the agent. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 20)

children.text: 'tasmāttatsaṃyogāt'; ityādi / tena puruṣeṇa yaḥ saṃyogastasmādacetanaṃ cetanāvadiva bhavati / yathāgnisaṃyogāllohamaṇirityucyate / liṅgaṃ mahadādisūkṣmaparyantaṃ vakṣyati //
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, from the conjunction with that' — and so forth. From the conjunction with that <s>puruṣa</s>, the non-conscious appears as if conscious. Just as iron appears [to be magnetic] through contact with a magnet. The <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) — from <s>mahat</s> (the great) down to the subtle [elements] — he will explain.

children.text:
yadi tadeva triguṇātmakaṃ kartṛ na pumān, kathaṃ puruṣo gacchatītyucyata ityāha- 'guṇakartṛtve 'pi tathā karteva bhavatyudāsīnaḥ'; iti / guṇānāṃ kartṛtvaṃ na puruṣasya / yathā puruṣasaṃyogādacetanaṃ liṅgaṃ cetanāvadiva bhavati, tathā guṇātmakaliṅgasaṃyogādakartāpi san karteva bhavati / udāsīnaḥ / yathā svāmī svayamayoddhāpi yaudhabhṛtyasaṃyogād yoddheti vyapadiśyate, tathā puruṣo 'pyupacāreṇa karteti /
tathā coktam -
pravarttamānān prakṛterimān guṇāṃstamo 'bhibhūto viparītadarśanaḥ /
ahaṃ karomītyabudho 'bhimanyate tṛṇasya kubjīkaraṇe 'pyanīśvaraḥ // iti // 20 //
children.translated_text: If the three-<s>guṇa</s>-natured [<s>prakṛti</s>] alone is the agent and not <s>puruṣa</s>, how then is it said that '<s>puruṣa</s> goes'? To this he replies: 'Though the agency belongs to the <s>guṇas</s>, the indifferent [<s>puruṣa</s>] appears as if it were the agent.' The agency belongs to the <s>guṇas</s>, not to <s>puruṣa</s>. Just as, through conjunction with <s>puruṣa</s>, the non-conscious [<s>prakṛti</s> appears conscious] —

children.text: kārikā 21
children.translated_text: (Kārikā 21)

children.text: nanu pradhānapuruṣayoḥ kiṃ (kartṛtvaṃ) caitanyārthameva saṃyogaḥ, kiṃ vānyārthamapītyāha-
puruṣasya darśanārthaṃ kaivalyārthaṃ tathā pradhānasya /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of the seeing (<s>darśana</s>) of <s>puruṣa</s>, and for the purpose of the isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) of <s>pradhāna</s> likewise —

children.text: paṃgvandhavadubhayorapi saṃyogastatkṛtaḥ sargaḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: the conjunction of both is like that of the lame and the blind; from that [conjunction] is produced creation (<s>sarga</s>). (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 21)
Now, is the conjunction of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter) and <s>puruṣa</s> solely for the purpose of consciousness, or for some other purpose as well? To this he says:

children.text: 'puruṣasya'; ityādi / puruṣasyārtho dvividhaḥ, viṣayopabhogaḥ kaivalyaṃ ca / tadubhayaṃ pradhānena sampādyam / viṣayopabhogaśca pradhānavibhūtimantareṇa na sambhavati, iti darśanārthaṃ puruṣaḥ pradhānena saṃyujyate / mānaṃ svāṃ vibhūtiṃ darśayitumasamarthātpuruṣeṇa saṃyujyate (?) / dṛṣṭvā sa sarvāṃ vibhūtimanubhūya virasatvād viraktaḥ puruṣaḥ pradhānena tyajyate / tyaktasya kaivalyamityato darśanārthaṃ kaivalyārthaṃ ca dvayorapi saṃyogo matsyodakavadudumbaramaśakaśca //
children.translated_text: 'Of <s>puruṣa</s>' — and so forth. The purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> is twofold: the experience of objects (<s>viṣayopabhoga</s>) and isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>). Both of these are to be accomplished by <s>pradhāna</s>. The experience of objects is not possible without the manifestation of <s>pradhāna</s>; therefore <s>puruṣa</s> [conjoins with] <s>pradhāna</s> for the purpose of seeing.

children.text: 'paṃgvandhavat'; iti / dṛṣṭāntaḥ / paṅguḥ sacakṣuḥ paśyati panthānaṃ na saṃcarati, andho 'pi saṃcarati na paśyati panthānam / tayoḥ svārthabhraṣṭayorgrāmaprāptyarthaḥ sambandho bhūtaḥ / tatra paṅgurandhaskandhamāruhya gatimān, andho 'pi draṣṭradhiṣṭhānāddṛṣṭimān jātaḥ / grāmaprāptayośca tayorviyogaḥ / evaṃ puruṣo niṣkriyaḥ pradhānena saṃyujya tadvibhūtidarśanāya devādiṣu saṃcarati / pradhānaṃ niścetanamapi puruṣādhiṣṭhānāccetanāvadiva dvayamapi sampādayati / tasmātpaṃgvandhavadubhayorapi saṃyogaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Like the lame and the blind' — this is an illustration. The lame man has sight — he sees the path but cannot walk; the blind man walks but does not see the path. When both have failed in their own purposes, a connection arises for the sake of reaching the village. There the lame man [mounts the blind man's shoulders] —

children.text: nanu ca saṃyogamātreṇa kathaṃ darśanaṃ kaivalyaṃ cetyāha- 'tatkṛtaḥ sargaḥ'; iti / saṃyogakṛto mahadādigrāmotpāda ityarthaḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: Now, how can mere conjunction [produce] seeing and isolation? To this he says: 'From that is produced creation.' The meaning is: the production of the group [of evolutes] beginning with <s>mahat</s> is brought about by the conjunction. (21)

children.text: kārikā 22
children.translated_text: (Kārikā 22)

children.text: tameva darśayannāha-
children.translated_text: Showing that very [creation], he says:

children.text: prakṛtermahāṃstato 'haṅkārastasmādgaṇaśca ṣoḍaśakaḥ /
children.translated_text: From <s>prakṛti</s> [arises] <s>mahat</s> (the great); from that, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle); from that, the group of sixteen.

children.text: tasmādapi ṣoḍaśakātpañcabhyaḥ pañca bhūtāni || 22 ||
children.translated_text: And from five of that group of sixteen [arise] the five gross elements (<s>bhūta</s>). (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 22)

children.text: 'prakṛtermahān'; ityādi / prakṛtiḥ pradhānaṃ kāraṇamavyaktaṃ guṇasāmyaṃ tamobahulamavyākṛtamiti prakṛtiparyāyāḥ / tato mahānutpadyate sa tu tamobahulaḥ / mahān buddhirmatiḥ pratyaya upalabdhiriti buddhiparyāyāḥ / tato 'haṅkāra utpadyate / sa tu rajastamobahulaḥ / ahaṅkāraḥ suparṇapaṇi(!)statpuruṣa ityahaṅkāraparyāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'From <s>prakṛti</s>, <s>mahat</s>' — and so forth. <s>Prakṛti</s> [is synonymous with] <s>pradhāna</s>, cause, unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), the equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s>, predominantly <s>tamas</s>, undifferentiated — these are the synonyms of <s>prakṛti</s>. From that, <s>mahat</s> is produced; and it is predominantly <s>tamas</s>. <s>Mahat</s>, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>mati</s>, <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition), <s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension) — these are synonyms of <s>buddhi</s>.

children.text: 'tasmādgaṇaśca ṣoḍaśakaḥ'; iti / tasmādahaṅkārāt ṣoḍaśako gaṇa utpadyate / ekādaśendriyāṇi pañca tanmātrāṇītyarthaḥ / tāni hṛṣīkāṇīndriyāṇīti paryāyāḥ / sūkṣmā atiśayā aṇavaḥ (viṣā) iti tanmātraparyāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'From that, the group of sixteen' — from that <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, the group of sixteen is produced: the eleven sense-faculties and five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) — this is the meaning. <s>Hṛṣīka</s> and <s>indriya</s> are synonyms [for sense-faculties]. Subtle (<s>sūkṣma</s>), exceedingly fine (<s>atiśaya</s>), atoms (<s>aṇu</s>) — these are synonyms of <s>tanmātra</s>.

children.text: 'tasmādapi ṣoḍaśakāt pañcabhyaḥ pañca bhūtāni'; iti / ṣoḍaśād gaṇādyāni pañca tanmātrāṇi tebhya ekottaravṛddhyā pañca mahābhūtāni bhavanti / tatra śabdatanmātrādākāśamekaguṇam / śabdatanmātrapratisaṃhitāt sparśatanmātrāddviguṇo vāyuḥ / tābhyāṃ pratisaṃhitādrūpatanmātrāt triguṇaṃ tejaḥ / taiḥ pratisaṃhitādrasatanmātrāt caturguṇā āpaḥ / caturbhiḥ pratisaṃhitādgandhatanmātrāt pañcaguṇā pṛthivīti / etairekādaśādayaḥ sthūlā viśeṣā ucyante, yeṣvavasitāni caturviṃśatitattvāni // 22 //
children.translated_text: 'And from five of that group of sixteen, the five gross elements' — from the group of sixteen, those which are the five <s>tanmātras</s>, from them, by progressive increment of one [quality], the five great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>) arise. Among these: from the sound-<s>tanmātra</s>, space (<s>ākāśa</s>) with one quality; from the compounding of the sound-<s>tanmātra</s> [with touch] —

children.text: kārikā 23
children.translated_text: (Kārikā 23)

children.text: buddherlakṣaṇamāha-
children.translated_text: He states the characteristic of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect):

children.text: adhyavasāyo buddhirdharmo jñānaṃ virāga aiśvaryam /
children.translated_text: Determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) is <s>buddhi</s>. <s>Dharma</s> (virtue), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), dispassion (<s>virāga</s>), and sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) —

children.text: sāttvikametadrūpaṃ tāmasamasmādviparyastam || 23 ||
children.translated_text: these are its <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) forms; the <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) [forms] are the reverse of these. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 23)

children.text: 'adhyavasāyaḥ'; ityādi / śabdādiṣu viṣaye 'dhyavasāyaśabdo 'yaṃ yāvat gandho 'yamiti subuddherlakṣaṇam (?) / tasyāścāṣṭau rūpāṇi //
children.translated_text: 'Determination' — and so forth. The word 'determination' refers to the ascertainment regarding objects such as sound and the like — 'this is a smell' — this is the characteristic of <s>buddhi</s>. And its forms are eight.

children.text:
'dharmo jñānaṃ virāga aiśvaryam'; iti / tatra yo 'yamaniviṣayamanuṣṭhānātmako 'dhavasāyassa dharmaḥ / yamāḥ pañca niyamāśca / yathoktaṃ sāṃkhyapravacane 'ahiṃsāsatyāsteyabrahmacaryāparigrahā yamāḥ'; / 'śaucasantoṣatapassvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni niyamāḥ'; iti / tatra santoṣassanihitasādhanābhyāśādadhikasyānupāditsā / tapo jighatsāpipāsāśītoṣṇasthānasādhanājayaḥ kāṣṭhamaunākāramaune, vratāni ca kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādīni / svādhyāyo mokṣaśāstrādhyayanaṃ praṇavajapo vā / īśvarapraṇidhānaṃ viśiṣṭadevatārādhanam / asaṃsāribhistulyavṛttitvāditi / tadviparītānuṣṭhānamadharmaḥ / pañcaviṃśatitattvānāṃ svasaṃjñālākṣaṇyakatvaprayojanāvadhāraṇaṃ jñānam, guṇapuruṣāntarajñānam / śeṣamajñānam / viṣayaśarīrendriyebhyo doṣadarśanādvaimukhyaṃ virāgaḥ / teṣvabhilāṣo rāgaḥ / aiśvaryamaṣṭaguṇam- aṇimā, mahimā, laghimā, prāptiḥ, prākāmyam, īśitvaṃ, vaśitvam, yatrakāmāvasāyitvaṃ ceti / tatrāṇimāṇutvam, yena guṇena sūkṣmo bhūtvā vicarati / kārye kāraṇopacārādaṇimetyucyate / uttaratrāpyevaṃ yojyam / laghimā laghutvam, yena vāyuvallaghutaro bhavati / mahimā mahattvam, yena bhuvaneṣu dharmādiprāptiḥ, yena guṇeneṣitasya prāpaṇam / prākāmyaṃ pracurakāmitā yenaikamanekaṃ prākāmyate 'nekaṃ caikam / īśitvaṃ prabhutā (yena sthāvarādīni bhūtāni sandeśakārīṇi bhavanti / vaśitvaṃ vaśitā) yena svatantraścarati / yatrakāmāvaśāyitvaṃ (kāmenecchayāvaśetuṃ śīlaṃ yasya sa yatrakāmāvaśāyī / tasya bhāvaḥ yatrakāmāvaśāyitvam) / anekārthatvāddhātūnāṃ 'śī'; tiṣṭhatau varttate / yena guṇena divyantarikṣe bhūmau vāvasthāyitvamityarthaḥ /
'sāttvikametadrūpam'; iti / sattvatamobahulatvāt / buddheryadā sattvamutkaṭaṃ bhavati tadaitaccatuṣṭayaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
'tāmasamasmādviparyastam'; iti / utkaṭalakṣaṇāt dharmādicatuṣṭayādviparītaṃ tamasyudrikte bhavatītyarthaḥ / adharmo 'jñānamavairāgyamanaiśvaryaṃ ceti // 23 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, sovereignty' — among these, that determination which consists of practice directed toward non-sensory [goals] is <s>dharma</s>. The five <s>yamas</s> (restraints) and the <s>niyamas</s> (observances). As stated in the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacana</s>: 'Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possessiveness are the <s>yamas</s>.'

children.text: kārikā 24
children.translated_text: (Kārikā 24)

children.text: ahaṅkāralakṣaṇamāha-
abhimāno 'haṅkāraḥ, tasmāddvividhaḥ pravarttate sargaḥ /
children.translated_text: Self-attribution (<s>abhimāna</s>) is <s>ahaṅkāra</s>. From it proceeds a twofold creation:

children.text: ekādaśaśca gaṇastanmātrapañcakaścaiva || 24 ||
children.translated_text: the group of eleven and the set of five <s>tanmātras</s>. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 24)
He states the characteristic of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle):

children.text: 'abhimānaḥ'; ityādi / abhimatirabhimānaḥ / rūpādiṣu viṣayeṣvabhimāno rūpavānaham, mamaite viṣayāḥ, ityahyaṅkāralakṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: 'Self-attribution' — and so forth. Self-regarding thought (<s>abhimati</s>) is self-attribution. The self-attribution regarding objects such as form and the like — 'I have form,' 'these objects are mine' — this is the characteristic of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>.

children.text: tasmādabhimānalakṣaṇādahaṅkārāt 'dvividhaḥ pravarttate sargaḥ'; iti / sṛjyata iti sargaḥ //
children.translated_text: From that <s>ahaṅkāra</s> characterized by self-attribution, 'a twofold creation proceeds.' What is created (<s>sṛjyate</s>) is creation (<s>sarga</s>).

children.text: tameva dvividhaṃ darśayitumāha- 'ekādaśakaśca gaṇaḥ'; iti / ekādaśa parimāṇamasyetyekādaśaḥ śrotrādirgaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: To show that very twofold [creation], he says: 'the group of eleven' — that whose measure is eleven — [namely] the group [of sense-faculties] beginning with the ear.

children.text: 'tanmātrāpañcakaṃ ca'; iti / tanmātraśabdādisvarūpamātra ityarthaḥ / tanmātrāṇi śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ / mātrāgrahaṇaṃ bhūtasaṃśleṣanivṛttyartham / bhūteṣvapi śabdādisambhavāt // 24 //
children.translated_text: And 'the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements)'; thus. The word <s>tanmātra</s> means merely the essential nature of sound and so forth. The <s>tanmātras</s> are sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. The word 'mātra' (merely) is used to distinguish them from the combination with gross elements, since sound and the rest are found in the gross elements as well. // 24 //

children.text: kārikā 25
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 25

children.text: sa cāhaṅkārastrividha iti darśayannāha-
sāttvika ekādaśakaḥ pravarttate vaikṛtādahaṅkārāt /
children.translated_text: From the <s>vaikṛta</s> (modified) <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, the <s>sāttvika</s> group of eleven proceeds;

children.text: bhūtādestanmātraḥ sa tāmasaḥ, taijasādubhayam || 25 ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>bhūtādi</s> (source of elements), the <s>tanmātras</s> — that is <s>tāmasa</s> (dominated by <s>tamas</s>); from the <s>taijasa</s> (dominated by <s>rajas</s>), both. // <s>ISk</s>_25 //
Showing that this <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) is threefold, he says—

children.text: 'sāttvikaḥ'; ityādi / yadā sattvamudriktaṃ tadāhaṅkāro vaikṛtābhimāno bhavati, rajaścodriktaṃ taijasaḥ, tamaścodriktaṃ bhūtādiriti / tatra vaikṛtādekādaśako gaṇaḥ pravarttate / sa ca sāttvikaḥ sattvabahulaḥ, svaviṣayagrahaṇatvāt //
children.translated_text: '<s>Sāttvika</s>' and so forth. When <s>sattva</s> predominates, then <s>ahaṅkāra</s> becomes the <s>vaikṛta</s> (modified) self-identification; when <s>rajas</s> predominates, it is <s>taijasa</s>; when <s>tamas</s> predominates, it is <s>bhūtādi</s>. Among these, from the <s>vaikṛta</s>, the group of eleven proceeds. And that is <s>sāttvika</s>, predominating in <s>sattva</s>, because it has the nature of apprehending its own objects.

children.text: bhūtādestāmasādahaṅkārāttanmātraḥ sa tāmasaḥ, tamobahulatvāt / tatastāmasāttanmātrāt gaṇāt tāmaso bhūtagaṇaḥ pravarttate //
children.translated_text: From the <s>bhūtādi</s>, the <s>tāmasa</s> <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, the <s>tanmātras</s> proceed — that is <s>tāmasa</s>, because of the predominance of <s>tamas</s>. Then from the <s>tāmasa</s> group of <s>tanmātras</s>, the <s>tāmasa</s> group of gross elements proceeds.

children.text: ('taijasādubhayam'; iti / etadāśayaḥ- pañcakañcaitadubhayamapi pravarttate) / ādikāla ubhayatrāpyasya sahāyatvāt / vaikṛtabhūtādi dvāvapi prakāśasthitiśīlatvāt na kriyāśīle / tatastaijasamahaṅkāraṃ kriyāśīlaṃ sahāyamapekṣyaikādaśakaṃ pañcakaṃ ca malājanayata (?) iti // 25 //
children.translated_text: 'From the <s>taijasa</s>, both'; thus. The intention is this — both the group of five and both groups proceed. Because at the initial time, it serves as an auxiliary to both. The <s>vaikṛta</s> and <s>bhūtādi</s>, both being of the nature of illumination and stability, are not of the nature of activity. Therefore, requiring the <s>taijasa</s> <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, which is of the nature of activity, as an auxiliary, it produced the group of eleven and the group of five. // 25 //

children.text: kārikā 26
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 26

children.text: kaḥ punarekādaśa ityāha-
children.translated_text: What then are the eleven? He says—

children.text: buddhīndriyāṇi cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇarasanatvagākhyāni /
children.translated_text: The <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (cognitive sense organs) are called sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch;

children.text: vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthān karmendriyāṇyāhuḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: Speech, hands, feet, anus, and generative organ — these they call the <s>karmendriyas</s> (organs of action). // <s>ISk</s>_26 //

children.text: 'buddhīndriyāṇi'; ityādi / dvividhamindriyam / tatra cakṣuryena dṛśyate / śrotraṃ yena śrūyate / tvagyayā spṛśyate / rasanaṃ yena rasyate / nāsikā yayā ghrāyate / tā ākhyā yeṣāmindriyāṇāmiti śabdapradhāno nirdeśaḥ / tāni cakṣuḥśrotratvagrasanānāsikākhyāni pañca / buddhipūrvakaparyālocanamiti buddhīndriyāṇyāhuḥ sāṃkhyācāryāḥ / śabdavaśādatrākramaḥ kṛtaḥ / kramastu śrotratvakcakṣuriti //
children.translated_text: '<s>Buddhīndriyas</s>' and so forth. The <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) are of two kinds. Among them: the eye is that by which one sees; the ear is that by which one hears; the skin is that by which one touches; the tongue is that by which one tastes; the nose is that by which one smells. These are the names of the <s>indriyas</s> — thus the designation is based on the predominance of the term. These five are called by the names eye, ear, skin, tongue, and nose. They are called <s>buddhīndriyas</s> by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers because their operation is preceded by <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). The order here is irregular due to metrical requirements. The proper order is ear, skin, eye, and so forth.

children.text: 'vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthān'; iti / karmendriyāṇi karmābhinirvartanāt / asmādeva prayogādupasthaśabdaḥ puṃliṅgo 'pyastīti jñāyate / sa ca straiṇaḥ pauruṣeyaśca / tatra vāgindriyaṃ kaṇṭhastham / anyāni prasiddhānyeva // 26 //
children.translated_text: 'Speech, hands, feet, anus, and generative organ'; thus. The <s>karmendriyas</s> (organs of action) are so called because they bring about action. From this very usage it is known that the word <s>upastha</s> (generative organ) also has a masculine form. And it applies to both female and male. Among these, the organ of speech is situated in the throat. The others are well known. // 26 //

children.text: kārikā 27
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 27

children.text: ekādaśakamindriyaṃ darśayannāha-
children.translated_text: Showing the group of eleven <s>indriyas</s>, he says—

children.text: ubhayātmakamatra manaḥ, saṅkalpakamindriyaṃ ca sādharmyāt /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>manas</s> (mind) is of the nature of both; it is the deliberative one, and it is an <s>indriya</s> because of its similarity;

children.text: guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣānnānātvaṃ bāhyabhedāśca || 27 ||
children.translated_text: The diversity arises from the specific modifications of the <s>guṇas</s>, and so do the external differences. // <s>ISk</s>_27 //

children.text: 'ubhayātmakamatra manaḥ'; ityādi / atretyasminnindriyavaśe mana ubhayātmakamubhayasvabhāvam / buddhīndriyāṇāṃ karmendriyāṇāṃ ca svasvaviṣayagrahaṇakāle buddhīndriyaṃ karmendriyaṃ cetyarthaḥ / ubhayatrāpyasya vyāpārāditi lakṣaṇaṃ tadityāha- saṅkalpayatīti saṅkalpakam, idaṃ nedamiti //
children.translated_text: 'Here, <s>manas</s> is of the nature of both'; and so forth. 'Here' means in this domain of the <s>indriyas</s>. <s>Manas</s> is of the nature of both, having the nature of both. At the time of apprehending their respective objects by the <s>buddhīndriyas</s> and <s>karmendriyas</s>, it functions as both a <s>buddhīndriya</s> and a <s>karmendriya</s> — this is the meaning. Because it operates in both domains, its characteristic definition is stated thus — it deliberates, hence it is the 'deliberative one' (<s>saṅkalpaka</s>), thinking 'this, not that.'

children.text: kathamindriyamityāha- 'indriyaṃ ca sādharmyāt'; ityādi / indriyaistulyatvādityarthaḥ / yathānyadindraliṅgaṃ tathā mano 'pītyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: How is it an <s>indriya</s>? He says — 'It is an <s>indriya</s> because of its similarity'; and so forth. Because it is similar to the <s>indriyas</s> — this is the meaning. Just as the other organs bear the mark of <s>Indra</s> (the lord, i.e., <s>Puruṣa</s>), so too does <s>manas</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: tatraikasmādahaṅkārādutpannānāṃ kathaṃ svarūpabhedaḥ ? / yacchrotrādibuddhīndriyam, tat pratiniyataviṣayaṃ netaraviṣayamapi / yadyāgādi karmendriyaṃ tat pratiniyatakarma, netarakarmāpi / manaścobhayātmakam, naikātmakamityāha- 'guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣānnānātvam'; iti / ahaṅkārasthā ye guṇāḥ sattvādayasteṣāmanyo 'nyābhibhavāśrayā (dvidvāreṇa yaḥ pariṇāmaviśeṣastata evaiṣāṃ nānātvam / ta eva hi guṇāḥ pari)ṇāmaviśiṣṭā indriyavyapadeśabhājo nānāviṣayā bhavanti / kathaṃ deśaniyamo vṛttiniyamaśca ? tatra tvagindriyaṃ sarvaśarīrasthitabāhyābhyantaravṛtti, cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇarasanāni śirasi bahiḥ pṛthak pṛthagavasthitāni bāhyavṛttīni / vāgāsye sthitā / pāṇyādayaśca bāhoradhastāt pṛthak pṛthagavasthitā bahiḥkarmaviṣayāḥ //
children.translated_text: Now, when they arise from a single <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, how is there difference in their essential nature? That which is a <s>buddhīndriya</s> such as the ear and so forth is restricted to its own specific object and does not apprehend the objects of the others. That which is a <s>karmendriya</s> such as speech and so forth is restricted to its own specific action and does not perform the actions of the others. And <s>manas</s> is of the nature of both, not of one only. He says — 'The diversity arises from the specific modifications of the <s>guṇas</s>'; thus. The <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the rest — residing in <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, through the mutual predominance and subordination of one over another, undergo specific modifications, and from that alone arises their diversity. For it is these very <s>guṇas</s>, when specifically modified, that become designated as <s>indriyas</s> and have diverse objects. How is there restriction of location and restriction of function? The organ of touch (<s>tvagindriya</s>) is situated throughout the entire body and functions both externally and internally. The eye, ear, nose, and tongue are situated separately in the head and function externally. Speech is situated in the mouth. The hands and the rest are situated separately below the arms and have external actions as their objects.

children.text: ityatāha- 'bāhyabhedāśca'; iti / ye cānye viṣayabhedā deśaniyamavṛtiniyamābhyāṃ te 'pi guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣādeva / nātrāntarā kāraṇamasti // 27 //
children.translated_text: Therefore he says — 'And the external differences'; thus. Whatever other differences of objects arise through restriction of location and restriction of function, they too are solely due to the specific modifications of the <s>guṇas</s>. There is no other cause here. // 27 //

children.text: kārikā 28
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 28

children.text: eṣāmindriyāṇāṃ kasya kā vṛttirityāha-
children.translated_text: What is the function of each of these <s>indriyas</s>? He says—

children.text: śabdādiṣu pañcānāmālocanamātramiṣyate vṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: The function of the five [<s>buddhīndriyas</s>] with regard to sound and the rest is held to be mere apprehension;

children.text: vacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandāśca pañcānām || 28 ||
children.translated_text: Speaking, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure are the [functions] of the five [<s>karmendriyas</s>]. // <s>ISk</s>_28 //

children.text: 'śabdādiṣu'; ityādi / ādiśabdena śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ / teṣu yathākramaṃ pañcānāṃ śrotrādīnāṃ buddhīndriyāṇāmālocanamātraṃ vṛttiriṣyate sāṃkhyācāryaiḥ / śrotrādīni hi viṣayasya prakāśanamātraṃ kurvanti, niścayaṃ tu buddhiḥ / tathā hi buddhyavasitamarthaṃ puruṣaḥ cetayata iti siddhāntaḥ / karmendriyāṇāmapi vāgādīnāṃ yathākramaṃ vasanādānādīni vṛttayaḥ karmāṇi / tatra vāgindriyasya nānāvidhavarṇoccāraṇaṃ karma, ādeyasyādānaṃ pāṇyoḥ, viharaṇaṃ deśāntaragamanaṃ pādayoḥ, utsarga āhāramalasyotsarjanaṃ pāyoḥ, ānandanamānado hlādaḥ śukravisṛṣṭisaṃsṛṣṭisukhaṃ tadupasthendriyavṛttiḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: 'With regard to sound and the rest'; and so forth. By the word 'ādi' (and the rest), sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are meant. With regard to these, in their respective order, the function of the five <s>buddhīndriyas</s> — ear and the rest — is held by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers to be mere apprehension. For the ear and the rest merely illuminate the object; determination, however, belongs to <s>buddhi</s>. For the established doctrine is that <s>Puruṣa</s> becomes aware of what has been determined by <s>buddhi</s>. The functions of the <s>karmendriyas</s> — speech and the rest — are, in their respective order, speaking, grasping, and so forth. Among these: the function of the organ of speech is the utterance of various kinds of syllables; grasping of what is to be taken belongs to the hands; locomotion, meaning going to another place, belongs to the feet; excretion, meaning the evacuation of food-waste, belongs to the anus; and pleasure — meaning delight, joy, the happiness of the emission and union of semen — that is the function of the <s>upastha</s> (generative organ). // 28 //

children.text: kārikā 29
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 29

children.text: buddhyahaṅkāramanasāṃ kā vṛttirityāha-
children.translated_text: What is the function of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>? He says—

children.text: svālakṣaṇyaṃ vṛttistrayasya saiṣā bhavatyasāmānyā /
children.translated_text: The function of the three is their own distinctive characteristic — this is non-common;

children.text: sāmānyakaraṇavṛtiḥ prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañca || 29 ||
children.translated_text: The common function of the instruments is the five breaths beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>. // <s>ISk</s>_29 //

children.text: 'svālakṣaṇyaṃ vṛttiḥ'; ityādi / svātmīyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yasya tat svalakṣaṇam / tasya bhāvaḥ svālakṣaṇyam / tadeva vṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'The function is their own distinctive characteristic'; and so forth. That which has its own characteristic is called <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (having its own defining mark). Its state is <s>svālakṣaṇya</s> (possessing one's own distinctive characteristic). That itself is its function.

children.text: 'trayasya'; iti / buddhyahaṅkāramanasāmityarthaḥ / adhyavasāyo buddheḥ, abhimāno 'haṅkārasya, saṅkalpo manasaḥ / ta evādhyavasāyābhimānasaṅkalpāstrayasya vṛttiḥ / eṣāṃ ca buddhyādīnāṃ trayodaśānāṃ caturvidhā vṛttiḥ, asāmānyāyugapatkramaśceti (?) //
children.translated_text: 'Of the three'; thus. This means of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>. <s>Adhyavasāya</s> (determination) belongs to <s>buddhi</s>; <s>abhimāna</s> (self-identification) belongs to <s>ahaṅkāra</s>; <s>saṅkalpa</s> (deliberation) belongs to <s>manas</s>. These very functions — <s>adhyavasāya</s>, <s>abhimāna</s>, and <s>saṅkalpa</s> — are the function of the three. And the function of these thirteen, beginning with <s>buddhi</s>, is fourfold: non-common, simultaneous, and sequential.

children.text: tatra sāmānyāṃ darśayitumāha- 'saiṣā'; iti / yeyamuktā vṛttiḥ saiṣā bhavatyasāmānyā / yā yasya sā tasyaiva nānyeṣāmapītyarthaḥ / śrotrasya yacchabdaprakāśanaṃ tacchrotrasyaiva, nānyeṣāṃ tvagādīnāṃ dvādaśānām / evaṃ sarvatra yojyam //
children.translated_text: To show the common function, he says — 'This'; thus. The function that has been stated — this is the non-common function. That which belongs to one belongs to that one alone and not to the others — this is the meaning. The illumination of sound that belongs to the ear belongs to the ear alone, and not to the other twelve such as the skin and so forth. The same should be applied in all cases.

children.text: sāmānyāmāha- 'sāmānyakaraṇavṛttiḥ'; iti sāmānyā cāsau karaṇavṛttiśceti sāmānyakaraṇavṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: He states the common function — 'The common function of the instruments'; thus. It is common and it is the function of the instruments, hence 'common function of the instruments.'

children.text: 'prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañca'; iti / prāṇā ādyā yeṣāṃ vāyūnāṃ te prāṇādyāḥ / prāṇāpānavyānodānasamānā iti pañca vāyavaḥ / tatra prāṇo yo mukhanāsikābhyāṃ nirgacchati / yo nābheradhaḥ sthitaḥ so 'pānaḥ / yena kāye 'gnirdīpita āhāraṃ ca pacati sa samānaḥ / yo nābhideśādudyataśirogatirnādaṃ janayati sa udānaḥ / yaḥ sarvaśarīraṃ vyāpya sthitaṃ sa vyānaḥ / ete trayodaśānāmapi karaṇānāṃ sāmānyavṛttiḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: 'The five breaths beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>'; thus. Those breaths of which <s>prāṇa</s> is the first are called 'beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>.' The five breaths are <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>vyāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>samāna</s>. Among these: <s>prāṇa</s> is that which goes out through the mouth and nostrils; that which is situated below the navel is <s>apāna</s>; that by which the fire in the body is kindled and food is digested is <s>samāna</s>; that which, rising from the region of the navel, moves upward toward the head and produces sound is <s>udāna</s>; that which pervades the entire body and remains stationed is <s>vyāna</s>. These are the common function of all thirteen instruments. // 29 //

children.text: kārikā 30
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 30

children.text: karaṇaprabhāvikatvādvāyūnāṃ yugapatkramaśo vṛttimāha-
children.translated_text: Because the breaths are produced by the instruments, he states their simultaneous and sequential function—

children.text: yugapaccatuṣṭayasya tu vṛttiḥ kramaśaśca nirdiṣṭā /
children.translated_text: The function of the four is simultaneous and also described as sequential;

children.text: dṛṣṭe tathāpyadṛṣṭe trayasya tatpūrvikā vṛttiḥ || 30 ||
children.translated_text: In the seen and likewise in the unseen, the function of the three is preceded by that [of the fourth]. // <s>ISk</s>_30 //

children.text: 'yugapat'; ityādi / 'catuṣṭayasya tu'; iti / tuśabdo viśeṣaṇārthaḥ / buddhirahaṅkāro manaścakṣurityetasya catuṣṭayasyaikasmin rūpe yugapadvṛttiḥ / yathāndhakāre vidyutsaṃpāte kṛṣṇasarpasandarśane yugapadālocanādhyavasāyābhimānasaṅkalpanāni bhavanti / tathā hi cakṣuṣālocitaṃ buddhyādhyavasitamahaṅkāreṇātmīkṛtaṃ manasā saṅkalpitamiti //
children.translated_text: 'Simultaneous'; and so forth. 'Of the four'; thus. The word 'tu' (but) serves the purpose of specification. <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, <s>manas</s>, and the eye — the function of these four with respect to a single form is simultaneous. Just as when lightning flashes in the darkness and one sees a black serpent, apprehension, determination, self-identification, and deliberation occur simultaneously. For what is apprehended by the eye is determined by <s>buddhi</s>, appropriated by <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and deliberated upon by <s>manas</s>.

children.text: 'kramaśaśca tasya'; iti / catuṣṭasyasya krameṇa kadācidvṛttiriṣṭā / mandaprakāśe sthāṇupuruṣocitāmūrdhvatāṃ dṛṣṭavataḥ kiṃ sthāṇuḥ puruṣa iti vikalpaḥ / tatrākuñcapanaprasāraṇāt puruṣa ityadhyavasāyaḥ / tata ātmīkaraṇādabhimāna iti //
children.translated_text: 'And sequentially of that [four]'; thus. Sometimes the function of these four is sequential. When one sees an upright shape resembling either a post or a person in dim light, the doubt arises: 'Is it a post or a person?' Then, from the bending and stretching [of the figure], comes the determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>): 'It is a person.' Then from the appropriation comes self-identification (<s>abhimāna</s>).

children.text: yeya(mubhaya)thāvṛttiḥ sā kasmin viṣaya ityāha - 'dṛṣṭe'; iti / adṛṣṭe tarha nāstītyāha - 'tathāpyadṛṣṭe'; iti / tathā...ṣṭe dṛṣṭe 'pi vṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: This twofold function — in what domain does it occur? To this he says: 'In the seen (perceptible).' 'Then it does not occur in the unseen?' To this he says: 'Likewise in the unseen.' Thus, the function occurs in both the seen and the unseen.

children.text: kintu na catuṣṭayasya tarhītyāha- 'trayasya'; iti / buddhyahaṅkāramanasāmityarthaḥ / tatrāpi tatpūrvikā śrotrādipūrviketyarthaḥ / yathā smartavyamanusmarataḥ saṅkalpābhimānādhyavasāyā bhavanti // 30 //
children.translated_text: 'But not of all four?' To this he says: 'Of three' — the meaning is: of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), and <s>manas</s> (mind). And even there, [the function] is preceded by that, preceded by the ear etc. — this is the meaning. Just as when one remembers what is to be remembered, conceptualization, self-assertion, and determination occur. // 30 //

children.text: kārikā 31
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 31]

children.text: atha yadetaccatuṣṭayaṃ tatkiṃ yugapat parasparasavyapekṣaṃ svāṃ svāṃ vṛtiṃ pratipadyate kiṃ vā nirapekṣamityāha-
svāṃ svāṃ pratipadyante parasparākūtahaitukīṃ vṛttim /
children.translated_text: They engage in their respective functions, which are caused by each other's intention.

children.text: puruṣārtha eva heturna kenacitkāryate karaṇam || 31 ||
children.translated_text: The purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is the motive; no one makes the instrument act. // ISk 31 //
Now, do these four [organs] simultaneously, depending on each other, engage in their respective functions, or independently? To this he says:

children.text: 'svāṃ svām'; ityādi / ātmīyātmīyāṃ vṛttim //
children.translated_text: 'Their respective' and so on — each its own function.

children.text: 'parasparākūtahaitukīm'; iti / parasparasya yadākūtaṃ svavṛttibhogastadeva hetuḥ / tatra bhūtāṃ parasparākūtahaitukīṃ vṛttiṃ catvāri karaṇāni pratipadyante / tatra cakṣurbuddhyāditrayasyākūtaṃ jñātvā prakāśanaṃ pratipadyate / evaṃ buddhirahaṅkāro manaśca trayāṇāmākūtaṃ jñātvā 'dhyavasāyamabhimānaṃ saṅkalpanaṃ ca pratipadyante / kramaśaśca parasparākūtahaitukīm / kintu pūrvapūrvahaitukī draṣṭavyā / yathā kasyacidupanimantraṇaṃ śrutavataḥ śrotravṛttiṃ jñātvā, buddhirgamanāyādhyavasitā / tadvṛttiṃ jñātvā 'haṅkāro modakānahaṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmīti manyate / tadvṛttiṃ jñātvā manaḥ, pracuraṃ ghṛtaṃ prāpayiṣyāmīti kiṃ stokamiti, saṅkalpayatīti / evaṃ bāhyānyapi karaṇāni svāṃ svāṃ vṛttiṃ parasparākūtahaitukīṃ pratipadyante //
children.translated_text: 'Caused by each other's intention.' Whatever is the intention of each toward the other — the experience of its own function — that alone is the cause. There, the four instruments engage in the function caused by each other's intention. The eye, knowing the intention of the three [inner organs] beginning with <s>buddhi</s>, engages in illumination. Similarly, <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>, knowing the intention of the three others, engage in determination, self-assertion, and conceptualization respectively. And [this is] successively caused by each other's intention; but it should be understood as caused by the preceding one. For example: when one who has heard an invitation — knowing the ear's function — <s>buddhi</s> determines to go. Knowing that function, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> thinks 'I shall eat the sweets.' Knowing that function, <s>manas</s> conceptualizes: 'Shall I procure much ghee, or little?' Thus the external instruments too engage in their respective functions caused by each other's intention.

children.text: etāni kimātmārthaṃ svāṃ svāṃ vṛttiṃ pratipadyante, kimanyārthamityāha- 'puruṣārtha eva hetuḥ'; iti / puruṣasyārtho viṣayopabhogaḥ kaivalyaṃ ca, sa vṛttihetuḥ //
children.translated_text: Do these engage in their respective functions for their own sake or for another's? To this he says: 'The purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is the motive.' <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose is the enjoyment of objects and <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation); that is the motive for their function.

children.text:
nanvīśvaraḥ kartā jagataḥ, sa eva buddhyādikalāpaṃ sṛṣṭavān yena puruṣasyārthaḥ sampadyate / tathā coktam-
'īśvaraprerito gacchetsvargaṃ vā śvabhrameva vā'; / iti
tatrāha - 'na kenacitkāryate karaṇam'; iti / pradhānavyatirekeṇa na kaścidbuddhyādikaraṇaṃ svāṃ svāṃ vṛttiṃ kārayatītyarthaḥ / yadi kartā syāt, kimiti prakṛtimapekṣate / nāpi seśvaravādinā prakṛtirabhyupagataiva, niścetanatvāt prakṛteḥ sacetano 'dhiṣṭhātā kartā 'paro gaveṣyata iti cet, puruṣa evādhiṣṭhātā / acetanā prakṛtiḥ / etaduktameva prāk // 31 //
children.translated_text: Objection: <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is the creator of the world. He alone created the aggregate of <s>buddhi</s> and others, by which <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose is fulfilled. As it is said: 'Impelled by <s>Īśvara</s>, one goes to heaven or to a dog's hole.' To this he says: 'No one makes the instrument act.' The meaning is: apart from <s>Pradhāna</s>, no one makes the instruments of <s>buddhi</s> etc. engage in their respective functions. If there were a creator, why would he need <s>Prakṛti</s>? Nor has <s>Prakṛti</s> been accepted by those who posit <s>Īśvara</s>. If one says: because <s>Prakṛti</s> is insentient, a sentient presider and creator other than her must be sought — [we reply:] <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is the presider. <s>Prakṛti</s> is insentient. This has already been stated before. // 31 //

children.text: kārikā 32
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 32]

children.text: katividhamantaḥkaraṇamityāha-
children.translated_text: How many kinds of inner organ are there? To this he says:

children.text: karaṇaṃ trayodaśavidham, tadāharaṇadhāraṇaprakāśakaram /
children.translated_text: The instrument is of thirteen kinds; it accomplishes gathering, holding, and illuminating.

children.text: kāryaṃ ca tasya daśadhā, hāryaṃ dhāryaṃ prakāśyaṃ ca || 32 ||
children.translated_text: Its object is tenfold: what is to be gathered, what is to be held, and what is to be illuminated. // ISk 32 //

children.text: 'karaṇaṃ trayodaśavidham'; ityādi / pañca buddhīndriyāṇi, pañca karmendriyāṇi, buddhyahaṅkāramanāṃsi ca trīṇi / etat trayodaśavidham / karaṇaṃ karotīti / 'kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam'; iti kartari lyuṭ //
children.translated_text: 'The instrument is of thirteen kinds' and so on. Five cognitive sense organs (<s>buddhīndriya</s>), five action organs (<s>karmendriya</s>), and three — <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>. This makes thirteen kinds. 'Instrument' — because it acts (<s>karoti</s>). The <s>lyuṭ</s> suffix is in the agent sense, [per the rule] 'the <s>lyuṭ</s> suffix after <s>kṛtya</s> is frequent.'

children.text: tatra kasya kā kriyā yadapekṣayā karaṇamityāha- 'tadāharaṇadhāraṇaprakāśakaram'; / iti tatkaraṇamāharaṇādīni karotīti / tatra karmendriyāṇyāharaṇaṃ kurvanti, buddhyahaṅkāramanāṃsi dhāraṇam, buddhīndriyāṇi prakāśamiti //
children.translated_text: What is the function of which, such that it is [called] an instrument? To this he says: 'It accomplishes gathering, holding, and illuminating.' That instrument performs gathering etc. There, the action organs accomplish gathering, <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> accomplish holding, and the cognitive sense organs accomplish illuminating.

children.text: kiṃ tatkāryaṃ yasyāharaṇaṃ kurvantītyāha- 'kāryam'; iti / tasya karaṇasya daśavidhaṃ kāryam / tatra śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ pañca vacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandāḥ pañceti daśadhā / pūrve dvividhāḥ- sūkṣmāstanmātralakṣaṇāḥ sukhaikasvabhāvatvāddivyāḥ, sthūlā ākāśādayaḥ sukhaduḥkhamohatmakatvādadivyā iti / etatkāryaṃ buddhīndriyāṇāṃ prakāśyam / vāgādīnāmuktyādānādikarmakartṛtvāt kāryam (?) / tatra vācā śabdasya, pāṇibhyāmādeyasyāhriyamāṇatvādubhayamapyāhāryam // vihāryaṃ viharaṇasthānam, pūrvāvayavanyāsenottarāvayavākramaṇena ca pādābhyāmāhriyamāṇatvādāhāryam / anyathā kathamutsargānandau syātām / ubhayamapi karmendriyāviṣayam / buddhyahaṅkāramanasāṃ dhāryam, tairantaḥ svavṛttyāvadhāryamāṇatvāt // 32 //
children.translated_text: What is that object for which they accomplish gathering? To this he says: 'Its object' — the object of that instrument is tenfold. Of these, sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are five; speech, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure are five — making ten. The former are twofold: the subtle ones, characterized as <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), being of the nature of pleasure alone, are divine; the gross ones — space and the rest — being of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, are non-divine. This tenfold object is what the cognitive sense organs illuminate. For the speech organ and the rest, being agents of the actions of speaking, grasping, etc., [the objects constitute] their product. There, by speech, sound is [expressed], and by the hands, what is to be grasped is brought — thus both are what is to be gathered. Locomotion-space is a place of movement; since it is brought by the feet through the arrangement of prior limbs and the stepping of subsequent limbs, it too is what is to be gathered. Otherwise, how would excretion and pleasure be [accounted for]? Both are objects of the action organs. For <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>, [the objects are] what is to be held, since they are internally grasped by their own function. // 32 //

children.text: kārikā 33
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 33]

children.text: tadeva trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇaṃ bāhyāntarabhedāddvividhamiti darśayannāha-
children.translated_text: Showing that this very thirteenfold instrument is twofold, being divided into external and internal, he says:

children.text: antaḥkaraṇaṃ trividhaṃ daśadhā bāhyaṃ trayasya viṣayākhyam /
children.translated_text: The internal organ is threefold; the external is tenfold. The object of the three [internal organs] is named 'external.'

children.text: sāmpratakālaṃ bāhyaṃ trikālamābhyantaraṃ karaṇam || 33 ||
children.translated_text: The external [organ operates in] the present time; the internal organ operates in all three times. // ISk 33 //

children.text: 'antaḥkaraṇam'; ityādi / karaṇaṃ dvividham- bāhyamābhyantaraṃ ca / tatra śarīrasyāntaḥsthitatvādantaḥkaraṇaṃ trividham- buddhirahaṅkāromanaśceti //
children.translated_text: 'The internal organ' and so on. The instrument is twofold: external and internal. Of these, the internal organ is threefold — <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> — because of being situated within the body.

children.text: 'daśadhā bāhyam'; iti / daśaprakāram / pañca buddhīndriyāṇi, pañca karmendiyāṇi / tadbuddhirbhavati //
children.translated_text: 'The external is tenfold' — of ten kinds: five cognitive sense organs and five action organs. Such is the understanding.

children.text: tadbāhyaṃ 'trayasya viṣayākhyam'; iti / tryavayavasyāntaḥkaraṇasya bāhyaṃ viṣaya ityākhyāyate, taddvāreṇa viṣayāvagāhanāt / tenāntaḥkaraṇasya dvividho viṣayaḥ- dvāraṃ bhogyaṃ ceti / catuṣṭayasya dṛṣṭervartamāne trayasyādṛṣṭe vṛttiruktā //
children.translated_text: That external [organ is] 'named the object of the three' — the external [organ] is designated as the 'object' of the three-parted internal organ, since through it [as a door], the internal organ apprehends objects. Thus the internal organ has a twofold object: the door [i.e., the external organs] and what is to be enjoyed. The function of the four [organs] in the seen and of the three [inner organs] in the unseen has been stated.

children.text: tatrātītānāgatayorapi viṣayayoḥ kiṃ vṛttirasti, netyāha- 'sāmpratakālaṃ bāhyam'; iti / kalyata iti kālaḥ viṣaya evātīto 'nāgato vartamānoścocyate / na tadvyatirekeṇa kālo 'sti / mā bhūt ṣaḍviṃśatitattvaprasaṅga iti / tatra sāmprato vartamānaḥ kālo yasya bāhyasya taddhi bāhyam / śrotrādi vartamānameva śabdādikaṃ prakāśayati, nātītānāgate / vāgādi ca vartamānamevoktyādānaviharaṇotsargānandān karoti, nātītānāgatān //
children.translated_text: Does the function extend to past and future objects as well, or not? To this he says: 'The external [operates in] the present time.' Time is called <s>kāla</s> ('that which is reckoned') — it is the object itself that is called past, future, or present. There is no time apart from that, lest there be the absurd consequence of a twenty-sixth <s>tattva</s> (principle). There, the external [organ] whose time is the present — the ear and others illuminate only present sounds and the like, not past or future ones. And the speech organ and others perform only present speaking, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure, not past or future ones.

children.text: 'trikālamābhyantaram'; iti / trayaḥ kālā yasya tat trikālam / yathā buddhirvartamānamadhyavasyati / tathātītānāgatāvapi / māndhātāsīt kalkī rājā bhaviṣyatīti / yathāhaṅkāro vartamānamabhimanyate tathātītānāgatāvapi / mamaivamāsīt, mamaivaṃ bhaviṣyatīti / yathā ca mano vartamānaṃ saṅkalpayatīti tathātītānāgatāvapi / tatra kimidaṃ bhūtaṃ syāt, na mameti / kimidaṃ bhaviṣyati, netīti // 33 //
children.translated_text: 'The internal [operates in] all three times.' That which has three times is 'trikāla' (of three times). Just as <s>buddhi</s> determines what is present, so too the past and the future — '<s>Māndhātā</s> existed; King <s>Kalki</s> will come into being.' Just as <s>ahaṅkāra</s> claims the present as its own, so too the past and the future — 'Thus it was mine; thus it will be mine.' And just as <s>manas</s> conceptualizes about the present, so too about the past and the future — 'What could this have been? Not mine.' 'What will this become? Not [mine].' // 33 //

children.text: kārikā 34
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 34]

children.text: nanu ca yadi sthūlāḥ pṛthivyādayaste viśeṣāḥ / bāhyaṃ bāhyakaraṇaṃ svaviṣayaṃ pratipadyate / pṛthivyādayastarhi bhedena pratipattavyā ityāha-
children.translated_text: But if the gross elements — earth and the rest — are the specific [objects], and the external organ apprehends its own specific object, then earth and the rest should be apprehended distinctly. To this he says:

children.text: buddhīndriyāṇi teṣāṃ pañca viśeṣāviśeṣaviṣayīṇi /
children.translated_text: The cognitive sense organs — five of them — have both specific and non-specific objects.

children.text: vāgbhavati śabdaviṣayā śeṣāṇi tu pañcaviṣayīṇi || 34 ||
children.translated_text: Speech has sound as its object; the remaining [action organs] have all five objects. // ISk 34 //

children.text: 'buddhīndriyāṇi'; ityādi / teṣāmapi trayodaśānāṃ karaṇānāṃ yāni pañca buddhīndriyāṇi, tāni viśeṣāviśeṣaviṣayīṇi / śabdādayaḥ pañca viṣayā dvividhāḥ - viśeṣā aviśeṣāśca / tatra ye sūkṣmāstanmātralakṣaṇāste 'viśeṣāḥ / ye sthūlāḥ pṛthivyādayaste viśeṣāḥ / viśeṣāścāviśeṣāśceti dvaṃdvaḥ / ta eva viṣayā vidyante yeṣāmiti matvarthopaḥ / viśiṣṭānaviśiṣṭāṃśca viṣayān gṛhyantītyarthaḥ / tatra śrotraṃ sthūlān nānāśabdānavikalān gṛhṇāti, śabdatanmātraṃ ca / nāsikā sthūlān surabhyādigandhān, tanmātraṃ ca gṛhṇātīti //
children.translated_text: 'The cognitive sense organs' and so on. Among the thirteen instruments, the five cognitive sense organs have both specific and non-specific objects. The five objects — sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — are twofold: specific (<s>viśeṣa</s>) and non-specific (<s>aviśeṣa</s>). Of these, the subtle ones characterized as <s>tanmātras</s> are the non-specific. The gross ones — earth and the rest — are the specific. 'Specific and non-specific' is a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound). 'Those in which these very objects exist' — [this is] a possessive suffix (<s>matvartha</s>). The meaning is: they grasp both specific and non-specific objects. There, the ear grasps gross and varied sounds without distinction, as well as the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> (subtle element of sound). The nose grasps gross fragrances such as pleasant ones, as well as the <s>tanmātra</s> [of smell].

children.text: 'vāgbhavati'; / kevalaḥ śabdo viṣayo yasyāḥ, na viṣayāntaramityarthaḥ // śeṣāṇi pāṇyādīni catvāri, pañca viṣayīṇi / pañca viṣayā eṣāmiti / tatra pāṇiḥ śabdasparśarūparasavantaṃ ghaṭādikamādatte / pādau śabdādimatyāṃ bhūmau viharataḥ / pāyurupasthaśca śabdādimadeva malaṃ śukraṃ ca visṛjati / anena dvāreṇa tu sarvaṃ bāhyaṃ karaṇaṃ pañcaviṣayameva draṣṭavyam / yaṃ hi yadevamāśritya (?) sphītaṃ tasya śabdasparśarūparasagandhavattvāt, 'bāhyaṃ trayasya viṣayākhyam'; ityuktam // 34 //
children.translated_text: Speech arises; sound alone is the object of which [speech], not any other object — this is the meaning. The remaining four, beginning with hands, have five objects — five objects belong to these. Among them, the hand grasps a pot and so forth which possess sound, touch, form, and taste; the feet move about on the earth which possesses sound and the rest; the organ of excretion and the generative organ discharge waste and semen which likewise possess sound and the rest. By this approach, however, all external <s>karaṇas</s> (instruments) should be understood as having five objects indeed. For whatever is abundantly supported by whatever [element], that possesses sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — thus it was stated: 'the external [instruments] of the three are called objects of the senses.' // 34 //

children.text: kārikā 35
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 35

children.text: tatkathaṃ tasya viṣaya ityāha-
sāntaḥkaraṇā buddhiḥ sarvaṃ viṣayamavagāhate yasmāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), together with the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner instrument), apprehends all objects;

children.text: tasmāt trividhaṃ karaṇaṃ dvāri, dvārāṇi śeṣāṇi || 35 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the threefold <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument) is the doorkeeper, and the rest are the doors. // <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 35 //
Then how is that its object? To this he says —

children.text: 'sāntaḥkaraṇā'; ityādi / buddherupāttatvāccheṣamahaṅkāro manaścāntaḥkaraṇam / tābhyāṃ yuktā buddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Together with the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner instrument)' and so on. Since the rest are subordinate to <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) and <s>manas</s> (mind) constitute the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner instrument). <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) is endowed with these two.

children.text: 'sarvam'; iti / triṣvapi kāleṣu vyavasthitaṃ viṣayamavagāhate gṛhṇāti yasmāt , tasmāt trividhamantaḥkaraṇaṃ buddhyādi dvāri bhavati / dvārāṇyasya santīti kṛtvā / śeṣāṇi tu buddhīyakarmendriyāṇi (?) dvārāṇi / ebhirdvārabhūtairantaḥkaraṇaṃ viṣayān gṛhṇāti // 35 //
children.translated_text: 'All' — it apprehends, grasps the objects established in all three times. Since [<s>buddhi</s> does this], therefore the threefold <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner instrument) beginning with <s>buddhi</s> serves as the doorkeeper — because it possesses the doors. The remaining sense organs and action organs belonging to <s>buddhi</s> are the doors. Through these, which serve as doors, the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner instrument) grasps the objects. // 35 //

children.text: kārikā 36
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 36

children.text: nanu ca yadyantaḥkaraṇaṃ bāhyakaraṇadvāreṇa sarvaṃ viṣayamavagāhate, tasmin kiṃ lakṣaṇamityāha-
children.translated_text: Now, if the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner instrument) apprehends all objects through the external instruments, what is its distinguishing characteristic? To this he says —

children.text: ete pradīpakalpāḥ parasparavilakṣaṇā guṇaviśeṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: These, resembling lamps, mutually distinct, are modifications of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities);

children.text: kṛtsnaṃ puruṣasyārthaṃ prakāśya buddhau prayacchanti || 36 ||
children.translated_text: Having illuminated the entire purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness), they present it to <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). // <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 36 //

children.text: 'ete'; ityādi / śrotrādayo vāgādayo buddhyādayaścetyete trayodaśa guṇaviśeṣāḥ, traya eva guṇā anyo 'nyābhibhavadvāreṇa pariṇatāḥ śrotrādivyapadeśabhāja ityarthaḥ / pradīpakalpāḥ, svavṛttyā viṣayasya prakāśakatvāt / parasparavilakṣaṇāḥ / ekasya yā vṛttiḥ svarūpaṃ ca, na taditareṣāmapi yadi syādetenaiva viṣayāvagāhanaṃ siddhaṃ kimanyena //
children.translated_text: 'These' and so on. The auditory organ and the rest, speech and the rest, <s>buddhi</s> and the rest — these thirteen are modifications of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), meaning the three <s>guṇas</s> alone, having undergone transformation through mutual predominance, come to be designated as the auditory organ and so forth. They resemble lamps, because they illuminate their objects through their own activity. They are mutually distinct — the function and nature of one does not belong to the others, for if it did, apprehension of objects would be accomplished by that one alone, and what need would there be of the others?

children.text: 'kṛtsnam'; iti / trailokyagataṃ puruṣasyārthaṃ sūkṣmasthūlaviṣayalakṣaṇaṃ prakāśyābhivyaktiṃ nītvā paścādahaṅkārādayo dvādaśa buddhau prayacchanti, sthāpayantītyarthaḥ / avagāhanaphalametat / tasyāṃ ca viṣayopadhānoparaktyāṃ buddhau puruṣa upalabhate / tatredamucyate - buddhyādhyavasitamarthaṃ puruṣa...ta iti // 36 //
children.translated_text: 'The entire' — the object of <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness), characterized by subtle and gross objects extending through the three worlds, having illuminated it, having brought it to manifestation, thereafter the twelve beginning with <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) present it to <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), place it there — this is the meaning. This is the fruit of apprehension. And when objects are thus deposited in <s>buddhi</s>, which serves as the receptacle, <s>Puruṣa</s> perceives them. Here it is said — <s>Puruṣa</s> [perceives] the object determined by <s>buddhi</s>... // 36 //

children.text: kārikā 37
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 37

children.text: nanu ca tulye karaṇatve kimityahaṅkārādayo buddhau prayacchanti / prādhānyāttadeva darśayannāha -
children.translated_text: Now, since all are equally instruments, why do <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) and the rest present [objects] to <s>buddhi</s> (intellect)? Showing that very thing due to its preeminence, he says —

children.text: sarvaṃ pratyupabhogaṃ yasmātpuruṣasya sādhayati buddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) accomplishes all enjoyment for <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness);

children.text: saiva ca viśinaṣṭi punaḥ pradhānapuruṣāntaraṃ sūkṣmam || 37 ||
children.translated_text: And she alone again discriminates the subtle difference between <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness). // <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 37 //

children.text: 'sarvam'; ityādi / upabhogamupabhogaṃ prati pratyupabhogam / devamanuṣyatiryagyoniśu yo viṣayasyopabhogastaṃ prati sarvaṃ trailokyagataviṣayaṃ puruṣasya sādhayati, sampādayati / yasmādbuddhiḥ pradhānabhūtā satī nānyaḥ kaścit, tasmāt tāni karaṇāni buddhau prayacchanti / (yathā grāme hiraṇyādipratyayaṃ kuṭumbinaḥ pradhānāya prayacchanti) / pradhāno 'pyāsannavarttitvādbhogapataya iti //
children.translated_text: 'All' and so on. With respect to each enjoyment — the enjoyment of objects in the wombs of gods, humans, and animals — <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) accomplishes all objects extending through the three worlds for <s>Puruṣa</s>. Since <s>buddhi</s>, being the principal [instrument], and no other, [does this], therefore those instruments present [objects] to <s>buddhi</s>. Just as in a village, householders present their revenues of gold and such to the chief. And the chief too, being in close proximity, [delivers them] to the lord of enjoyment.

children.text: 'saiva ca viśinaṣṭi'; iti / yadā tamasvatī buddhirbhavati tadā sarvamupanītaṃ sampādayati / yadā sattvādhikā buddhirbhavati, tadā jñānasaṅgatā pradhānapuruṣāntaraṃ viśinaṣṭi / pradhānapuruṣayorvibhāgaṃ karotītyarthaḥ / anyat pradhānamanyaḥ puruṣa iti //
children.translated_text: 'And she alone discriminates' — when <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is predominated by <s>tamas</s> (darkness), then she accomplishes all that is brought to her.
