When <s>buddhi</s> is predominated by <s>sattva</s> (purity), then, being associated with knowledge, she discriminates the difference between <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness) — she makes the distinction between <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, this is the meaning. <s>Pradhāna</s> is one thing, <s>Puruṣa</s> is another.

children.text: 'sūkṣmam'; / sāṃsārikajñānasyāviṣayatvāt // 37 //
children.translated_text: 'Subtle' — because it is beyond the reach of worldly knowledge. // 37 //

children.text: kārikā 38
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 38

children.text: viśeṣāviśeṣaviṣayiṇītyuktam, tatra ke viśeṣāḥ ke 'viśeṣāścetyatrāha-
children.translated_text: It was stated that [<s>buddhi</s>] has both <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific) and <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specific) as objects. Now, what are the <s>viśeṣas</s> and what are the <s>aviśeṣas</s>? To this he says —

children.text: tanmātrāṇyaviśeṣāḥ, tebhyo bhūtāni pañca pañcabhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) are the <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specific); from them arise the five <s>bhūtas</s> (elements) from the five [<s>tanmātras</s>];

children.text: ete smṛtā viśeṣāḥ, śāntā ghorāśca mūḍhāśca || 38 ||
children.translated_text: These are known as the <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific), and they are <s>śānta</s> (tranquil), <s>ghora</s> (fierce), and <s>mūḍha</s> (dull). // <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 38 //

children.text: 'tanmātrāṇi'; ityādi / sūkṣmaviṣayāstanmātrāṇītyucyante / tairna kaścidviśiṣyata ityaviśeṣāḥ / yathā sūkṣmatṛṇāgrāvasthitaṃ tejo na lakṣyate, na ca kiñcit prakāśayati, tadvat te 'pyaviśeṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: '<s>Tanmātras</s> (subtle elements)' and so on. The subtle objects are called <s>tanmātras</s>. By them no one is particularized, hence they are <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specific). Just as fire resting on the tip of a subtle blade of grass is not perceived and does not illuminate anything, likewise they too are <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specific).

children.text: 'tebhyo bhūtāni pañca pañcabhyaḥ'; iti / tanmātrebhyaḥ pañca mahābhūtānyutpadyante //
children.translated_text: 'From them arise the five <s>bhūtas</s> (elements) from the five' — from the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) are produced.

children.text: 'ete smṛtā viśeṣāḥ'; iti / śabdatanmātrādekaguṇamākāśamutpadyate / evaṃ sparśāditanmātrād dvitricatuḥpañcaguṇā vāyvādaya utpadyante / taiśca tanmātrāṇi / viśiṣyanta iti viśeṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'These are known as <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific)' — from the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> (sound-potential) arises <s>ākāśa</s> (space) possessing one quality. Likewise, from the <s>sparśa-tanmātra</s> (touch-potential) and the rest arise <s>vāyu</s> (air) and the others possessing two, three, four, and five qualities respectively. And by these the <s>tanmātras</s> are particularized — hence they are <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific).

children.text: te ca kiṃsvarūpā ityāha- 'śāntā ghorāśca mūḍhāśca'; iti / śāntāḥ sukhapradāha ghorā duḥkhapradāḥ, mūḍhā mohapradā iti // 38 //
children.translated_text: What is their nature? To this he says — '<s>śānta</s> (tranquil), <s>ghora</s> (fierce), and <s>mūḍha</s> (dull).' <s>Śānta</s> means pleasure-giving, <s>ghora</s> means pain-giving, <s>mūḍha</s> means delusion-producing. // 38 //

children.text: kārikā 39
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 39

children.text: kimetāvanta eva viṣeṣā utānye 'pītyāha-
children.translated_text: Are only these many <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific), or are there others as well? To this he says —

children.text: sūkṣmā mātāpitṛjāḥ, saha prabhūtaistridhā viśeṣāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: The subtle [bodies], those born of mother and father, together with the gross elements — the <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific) are of three kinds;

children.text: sūkṣmāsteṣāṃ niyatā, mātāpitṛjā nivartante || 39 ||
children.translated_text: The subtle among them are permanent, while those born of mother and father perish. // <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 39 //

children.text: 'sūkṣmāḥ'; ityādi / ye sūkṣmāstanmātralakṣaṇāḥ saṃsāriṇaḥ śarīrasyāśrayatāṃ gatāste 'pi viśeṣāḥ, sūkṣmaśarīrasyārabdhatvāt //
children.translated_text: 'The subtle' and so on. Those which are subtle, characterized by the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), having become the basis of the transmigrating body — they too are <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific), because the <s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s> (subtle body) is constituted by them.

children.text: 'mātāpitṛjāḥ'; iti / mātāpitṛjāḥ ṣaṭ / tatra mātṛto lomalohitamāṃsāni pitṛtaḥ snāyvasthimajjānaḥ / te 'pi viśeṣāḥ, taiḥ sthūlaśarīrasya ṣaṭkośikasyārabdhatvāt / ete dvividhā viśeṣā ādhyātmikāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Born of mother and father' — those born of mother and father are six. Among them, from the mother come hair, blood, and flesh; from the father come sinew, bone, and marrow. They too are <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific), because the gross body consisting of six sheaths is constituted by them. These two kinds of <s>viśeṣas</s> are <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self).

children.text: 'sahaprabhūtaiḥ'; iti / yāni mahābhūtāni bāhyāni śāntaghoramūḍhānyuktāni tāni sthūlaśarīrasyāvakāśavyūhanapattikledanadhāraṇakartṛtvena prakṛṣṭabhūtānyucynte / taiḥ saha trayo viśeṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Together with the gross elements' — the <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) which are external, described as <s>śānta</s> (tranquil), <s>ghora</s> (fierce), and <s>mūḍha</s> (dull), are called 'predominant elements' because they serve as the cause of providing space, arrangement, moisture, cohesion, and support for the gross body. Together with them, the <s>viśeṣas</s> are of three kinds.

children.text: 'sūkṣmāsteṣāṃ niyatā mātāpitṛjā nivartante'; iti / sūkṣmaśarīraniyataṃ jñānaprāpteḥ prāk, tasya sāṃsarikatvāt / sthūlaśarīraniyataṃ tu nivartate, tasya pratimaraṇaṃ patitasya rasabhasmaniṣṭhāntatvāt // 39 //
children.translated_text: 'The subtle among them are permanent, while those born of mother and father perish' — that which is fixed in the <s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s> (subtle body) [persists] until the attainment of knowledge, because it is the transmigrating [entity]. But that which is fixed in the gross body perishes, because at each death, when fallen, it ends in fluid and ash. // 39 //

children.text: kārikā 40
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 40

children.text: yadetat sūkṣmaśarīraṃ tatkathamutpannamityāha-
children.translated_text: This <s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s> (subtle body) — how did it originate? To this he says —

children.text: pūrvotpannamasaktaṃ niyatammahadādisūkṣmaparyantam /
children.translated_text: Previously originated, unobstructed, permanent, [extending] from <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) down to the subtle [elements],

children.text: saṃsarati nirupabhogaṃ bhāvairadhivāsitaṃ liṅgam || 40 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) transmigrates, without [capacity for] experience, imbued with <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions). // <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 40 //

children.text: 'pūrvotpannam'; ityādi / pradhānenādisarge pratipuruṣamutpāditatvāt pūrvotpannam / asaktamapyāha / tanna kvacidvihanyate, parvatamapi bhittvā gacchati //
children.translated_text: 'Previously originated' and so on. Because it was produced by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature) for each <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness) at the first creation, it is 'previously originated.' It is also said to be 'unobstructed' — it is not impeded anywhere; it passes even through a mountain.

children.text: 'niyatam'; / nityam, jñānotpatteḥ prāgityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Permanent' — eternal, meaning until the arising of knowledge.

children.text: kiṃparimāṇamidamityāha- 'mahadādisūkṣmaparyantam'; iti / buddhirādiryasya tat, mahadādisūkṣmaviṣayāstanmātralakṣaṇāḥ paryantaṃ yasya tat sūkṣmaparyantam / buddhirahaṅkāra ekādaśendriyāṇi pañca tanmātrāṇītyetatparimāṇamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: What is its measure? To this he says — 'from <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) down to the subtle [elements].' That of which <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is the beginning is '<s>mahat</s>-ādi'; that of which the subtle objects characterized by the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) are the end is 'ending with the subtle.' <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), the eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense and action organs), and the five <s>tanmātras</s> — this is its measure, this is the meaning.

children.text: 'saṃsarati'; / triṣu lokeṣu //
children.translated_text: 'Transmigrates' — through the three worlds.

children.text: 'nirupabhogam'; iti / bāhyena sthūlaśarīreṇa vikalatvādviṣayabhogasamarthaṃ na bhavatītyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Without experience' — because it is incomplete without the external gross body, it is not capable of the enjoyment of objects, this is the meaning.

children.text: 'bhāvairadhivāsitam'; iti / dharmādibhiruparaktamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Imbued with <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions)' — meaning colored by <s>dharma</s> (merit) and the rest.

children.text: 'liṅgam'; itu / pralayakāle layaṃ gacchatīti kṛtvā // 40 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Liṅga</s>' (subtle body) — because at the time of <s>pralaya</s> (dissolution) it dissolves. // 40 //

children.text: kārikā 41
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 41

children.text: nanu karaṇamātrameva saṃsarati, kiṃ sūkṣmaśarīreṇetyāha-
children.translated_text: Now, the instruments alone transmigrate — what need is there for a <s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s> (subtle body)? To this he says —

children.text: citraṃ yathāśrayamṛte sthāṇvādibhyo vinā yathā cchāyā /
children.translated_text: Just as a painting without a support, just as a shadow without posts and the like,

children.text: tadvadvinā 'viśeṣairna tiṣṭhati nirāśrayaṃ liṅgam || 41 ||
children.translated_text: Likewise without <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specific elements), the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) does not stand unsupported. // <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 41 //

children.text: 'citram'; ityādi / yathā kuḍyādikamāśrayamṛte citraṃ na tiṣṭhati //
children.translated_text: 'A painting' and so on. Just as a painting does not stand without a support such as a wall and the like,

children.text: 'sthāṇvādibhyaḥ'; iti / ādiśabdena vṛkṣastambādayaḥ / 'pṛthagvinānānābhistṛtīyānyatarasyām'; iti pañcamyapi bhavati / tairvinā yathā cchāyā snigdhā paruṣā vā na tiṣṭhati //
children.translated_text: 'Without posts and the like' — by the word 'ādi' (and the like) are meant trees, pillars, and so forth. According to the grammatical rule '<s>pṛthag vinā nānābhis tṛtīyā anyatarasyām</s>' (the fifth case also occurs [with these words]), the ablative is also used. Without these, a shadow, whether smooth or rough, does not stand.

children.text: 'tadvadvinā 'viśeṣairna tiṣṭhati nirāśrayaṃ liṅgam'; iti / aviśeṣāstanmātrāṇi / liṅgaṃ trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇamiha gṛhyate / na tiṣṭhati nirāśrayatvāt / (tairhi sūkṣmaśarīramārabdham, tadabhāvāttadapi nāstīti nirāśrayatvāt) / na saṃsarati / na ca nirādhāreṇa karaṇena puruṣasya saṃyogaḥ sambhavati / puruṣo 'pi niṣkriyatvānna saṃsarati // 41 //
children.translated_text: 'Similarly, without the <s>aviśeṣas</s> (unspecified elements), the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) does not persist, being without support.' The <s>aviśeṣas</s> are the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). '<s>Liṅga</s>' here refers to the thirteen-fold instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). It does not persist because of being without support. (For the subtle body is constituted by them; in their absence, it too would not exist — because of being without support.) It does not transmigrate. Nor is a conjunction of <s>Puruṣa</s> with an unsupported instrument possible. <s>Puruṣa</s> too does not transmigrate, because of being inactive. ||41||

children.text: kārikā 42
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 42

children.text: tadeva sūkṣmaśarīraṃ kimarthaṃ saṃsaratītyāha-
children.translated_text: What purpose does that very subtle body transmigrate for? To this he says—

children.text: puruṣārthahetukamidaṃ nimittanaimittikaprasaṅgena /
children.translated_text: This [subtle body], motivated by the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, through the connection of cause and effect,

children.text: prakṛtervibhutvayogānnaṭavadvyavatiṣṭhate liṅgam || 42 ||
children.translated_text: persists like an actor, due to its connection with the all-pervasiveness of <s>Prakṛti</s>. // ISk 42 //

children.text: 'puruṣārthahetukam'; ityādi / puruṣārtho dvividha uktaḥ / sa heturyasyeti / samāsāntaḥ kap //
children.translated_text: 'Motivated by the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>' etc. The twofold purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> has been stated. That is the cause of which — [such is this subtle body]. The compound-final suffix is <s>kap</s>.

children.text: 'idam'; iti / mahadādi sūkṣmaparyantaṃ liṅgamuktam, tannaṭavadavatiṣṭhate / yathaika eva naṭastaṃ taṃ viśeṣamāsthāya yavanikānto nirgatya rājāmātyaviduṣakādibhāvenānuviddho 'vatiṣṭhate, tathā liṅgamapi taṃ taṃ dehamāsthāya devamanuṣyatiryagbhāvena vyavatiṣṭhate //
children.translated_text: 'This' — the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) that has been described as [consisting of] <s>mahat</s> and the rest up to the subtle [elements] persists like an actor. Just as a single actor, assuming this or that particular [role], comes out from behind the curtain and presents himself in the guise of a king, minister, jester, etc., so too the <s>liṅga</s>, assuming this or that body, persists in the form of gods, humans, and animals.

children.text: tadeva kathaṃ bhavatītyāha- 'nimittanaimittikaprasaṅgena'; iti / nimittaṃ dharmādharmādi, naimittikamūrdhvādhogamanādi / vakṣyati ca / tayoḥ prasaṅgeneti //
children.translated_text: How does this come about? He says: 'Through the connection of cause and effect.' The cause (<s>nimitta</s>) is <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, etc.; the effect (<s>naimittika</s>) is upward movement, downward movement, etc. And he will state this [later]. Through the connection of these two.

children.text: kimetatsarvamīśvarāt kiṃ vā svabhāvādityatrāha- 'prakṛteḥ vibhutvayogāt'; iti / prakṛtiḥ pradhānam, tasyā vibhutvaṃ jagatkartṛtvam / tadyogāt naṭavadvyavatiṣṭhate / pradhānenaiva hi puruṣasyārthaḥ kartavya iti mahadādisūkṣmaparyantaṃ liṅgamutpādya dharmādibhiradhivāsayati / tadadhivāsitaṃ ca naṭavat vyavatiṣṭhate / neśvarānna svabhāvāditi bhāvairadhivāsitamityuktam // 42 //
children.translated_text: Is all this from God (<s>Īśvara</s>), or from inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>)? To this he says: 'Due to its connection with the all-pervasiveness of <s>Prakṛti</s>.' <s>Prakṛti</s> is <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature); its all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>) is its capacity to create the world. Due to that connection, [the subtle body] persists like an actor. For it is by <s>Pradhāna</s> alone that the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is to be accomplished — thus, having produced the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) consisting of <s>mahat</s> and the rest up to the subtle [elements], it perfumes it with <s>dharma</s> and the other [dispositions]. And that which is so perfumed persists like an actor. Not from God, not from inherent nature — rather, 'perfumed by dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>)' is what has been stated. ||42||

children.text: kārikā 43
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 43

children.text: te punaḥ kiyantaḥ kimāśritā ityāha-
children.translated_text: How many are those [dispositions], and what do they depend on? He says—

children.text: sāṃsiddhikāśca bhāvāḥ prākṛtikā vaikṛtāśca dharmādyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>) — <s>dharma</s> and the rest — are innate (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>) and natural (<s>prākṛtika</s>), or acquired (<s>vaikṛta</s>);

children.text: dṛṣṭā karaṇāśrayiṇaḥ kāryāśrayiṇaḥ kalalādyāḥ || 43 ||
children.translated_text: they are seen as depending on the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), and those beginning with the embryo (<s>kalala</s>) depend on the effect (<s>kārya</s>). // ISk 43 //

children.text: 'sāṃsiddhikāśca'; ityādi / ye prākṛtasvabhāvāste sāṃsiddhikā ucyante / te ca kapilasyaiva mahāmunernānyasya / tasya hyutpadyamānasyaivādisarge sahotpannā dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryasaṃjñakāścatvāro bhāvāḥ / ye tvādisargāduttarakālamutpannakāryakāraṇānāmasmadvidhānāṃ prayatnapūrvakā utpadyante, te vaikṛtāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Innate' etc. Those that are of natural (<s>prākṛta</s>) character are called <s>sāṃsiddhika</s> (innate). And these belong only to <s>Kapila</s>, the great sage, and to no other. For when he was being born at the beginning of creation, the four dispositions designated as <s>dharma</s>, <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty) arose simultaneously with him. But those that arise for beings like ourselves, who are produced by causes and effects after the initial creation, and that arise through effort — those are <s>vaikṛta</s> (acquired).

children.text: te ca dvividhāḥ / yadāha- 'dharmādyā dṛṣṭāḥ karaṇāśrayiṇaḥ kāryāśrayiṇaśca kalalādyāḥ'; iti / dharmādayaścatvāraḥ, viparītāścādharmādayaścatvāra ityaṣṭau / ete trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇamāśritya pravartante / kāryaṃ pañca, kukṣisthasyāsya nicchuritasya tu kaumārayauvanavārddhakāni trayaḥ, ityaṣṭau bhāvāḥ / tatra vaikṛte dharmādibhiradhivāsitaṃ saṃsaratīti jñeyam // 43 //
children.translated_text: And these are of two kinds. As he says: '<s>Dharma</s> and the rest are seen as depending on the instrument, and those beginning with the embryo depend on the effect.' The four beginning with <s>dharma</s>, and the four opposites beginning with <s>adharma</s> — these are eight. These operate depending on the thirteen-fold instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). The effects (<s>kārya</s>) are five [i.e., the five embryonic stages]; for one situated in the womb there are three [stages]: childhood, youth, and old age — thus eight dispositions. Among these, in the acquired [type], the subtle body transmigrates perfumed by <s>dharma</s> and the other [dispositions] — this should be understood. ||43||

children.text: kārikā 44
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 44

children.text: nimittanaimittikaprasaṅgenetyuktam / tadubhayamapi darśayitumāha-
children.translated_text: It was stated 'through the connection of cause and effect.' To demonstrate both [cause and effect], he says—

children.text: dharmeṇa gamanamūrdhvaṃ, gamanamadhastādbhavatyadharmeṇa /
children.translated_text: By <s>dharma</s> there is upward movement; by <s>adharma</s> there is downward movement;

children.text: jñānena cāpavargo, viparyayādiṣyate bandhaḥ || 44 ||
children.translated_text: by knowledge there is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>); from the opposite [of knowledge], bondage is obtained. // ISk 44 //

children.text: 'dharmeṇa'; ityādi / dharmādinimittamūrdhvagamanādi naimittikam / tatra dharmeṇa yamaniyamalakṣaṇena gamanamūrdhvamiti, sūkṣmaśarīrasya devādivyavasthitirityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'By <s>dharma</s>' etc. <s>Dharma</s> and the other [dispositions] are the cause (<s>nimitta</s>); upward movement and the rest are the effect (<s>naimittika</s>). Among these, by <s>dharma</s> characterized by <s>yama</s> (restraints) and <s>niyama</s> (observances), there is upward movement — the meaning is: the subtle body becomes established in the state of gods and the like.

children.text: 'gamanamadhastādbhavayadharmeṇa'; iti / tiryagyoniṣu sthitiḥ / miśrānmanuṣyaloke sthitirityarthoktam //
children.translated_text: 'By <s>adharma</s> there is downward movement' — [this means] existence in animal births. From a mixture [of dharma and adharma], existence in the human world — this meaning has been stated.

children.text: 'jñānena cāpavargaḥ'; iti / pradhānapuruṣāntarajñānākhyena jñānena liṅgaṃ nivartate / tataḥ kevalaḥ puruṣo bhavati //
children.translated_text: 'By knowledge there is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>)' — by the knowledge called the discriminative knowledge of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) ceases. Then <s>Puruṣa</s> becomes isolated (<s>kevala</s>).

children.text: 'viparyayādiṣyate bandhaḥ'; iti / jñānaviparyayādajñānāt saṃsāracakrabandhaḥ, punaḥ punarāvartanam / sa ca triprakāraḥ - prakṛtibandhaḥ, dakṣiṇābandhaḥ, vikārabandhaśceti / yeṣāṃ prakṛtireva paratattvaṃ nānyat, teṣāṃ prakṛtivādināṃ prākṛtiko bandhaḥ / yeṣāmiṣṭāpūrtabhāvina eva divyādivyamānuṣabhogāḥ puruṣārtha iti, teṣāṃ karmavādināṃ dakṣiṇābandhaḥ / iṣṭāpūrtaṃ dakṣiṇeti / tathā coktam-
agnihotraṃ tapaḥ satyaṃ devānāṃ paripālanam /
children.translated_text: The fire-offering (<s>agnihotra</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), truthfulness, the worship of the gods,

children.text: atithirvaiśvadevaṃ ca iṣṭamityabhidhīyate //
children.translated_text: hospitality, and the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offering — these are called <s>iṣṭa</s> (Vedic rites).

'From the opposite [of knowledge], bondage is obtained' — from the opposite of knowledge, i.e., from ignorance, there is the bondage of the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), meaning repeated return. And this [bondage] is of three kinds: bondage of <s>Prakṛti</s> (<s>prakṛtibandha</s>), bondage of merit (<s>dakṣiṇābandha</s>), and bondage of modification (<s>vikārabandha</s>). For those for whom <s>Prakṛti</s> alone is the highest reality and nothing else — for those advocates of <s>Prakṛti</s>, there is the bondage of <s>Prakṛti</s>. For those for whom the divine, semi-divine, and human enjoyments produced by <s>iṣṭā</s> (Vedic rites) and <s>pūrta</s> (meritorious works) alone constitute the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> — for those advocates of ritual action, there is the bondage of merit. <s>Iṣṭāpūrta</s> is [called] <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). And thus it is stated—

children.text: puṣkariṇyaḥ sabhā vāpyo devatāyatanāni ca /
children.translated_text: Tanks, assembly halls, wells, temples of deities,

children.text: annapradānamārāmaḥ pūrtamityabhidhīyate //
children.translated_text: the giving of food, and groves — these are called <s>pūrta</s> (meritorious works).

children.text: yeṣāṃ vikāra evaiśvaryalakṣaṇaḥ puruṣārtha iti, teṣāṃ vikāratvavādināṃ vaikāriko bandhaḥ // 44 //
children.translated_text: For those for whom modification alone, characterized by sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), constitutes the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> — for those advocates of modification, there is the bondage of modification. ||44||

children.text: kārikā 45
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 45

children.text: vairāgyāt prakṛtilayaḥ, saṃsāro bhavati rājasādrāgāt /
children.translated_text: From dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s>; from passionate attachment (<s>rāga</s>) born of <s>rajas</s>, <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) comes about;

children.text: aiśvaryādavighāto viparyayāttadviparyāsaḥ || 45 ||
children.translated_text: from sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), non-obstruction; from the opposite of that, its reverse. // ISk 45 //

children.text: 'vairāgyāt" ityādi / yo viṣayādidarśanādvirakto yamaniyamaparisthito na jñānaṃ paryeṣate, tasya mṛtasya vairāgyādaṣṭāsyu prakṛtiṣu pradhānāditanmātraparyantāsu layaḥ, sthūlaśarīreṇa viṣayopabhoganimittena yogaḥ / tallīnaścātmānaṃ muktamiva manyate na tu muktam, sargakāle punaḥ saṃsaraṇāt / yadā tu jñānaṃ paryeṣyate tadā mucyata eva / tathā coktam-
jñānādatha virāgācca tathā kṛtsnasya saṃkṣayāt /
children.translated_text: 'From knowledge, and from dispassion, and from the complete dissolution of all —

children.text: ityevaṃ jāyate mokṣo mukta ātmastha ucyate // iti //
children.translated_text: thus liberation arises; one who is liberated is said to be self-abiding.'

'From dispassion' etc. One who, from seeing the defects of sense-objects, becomes dispassionate and is established in <s>yama</s> (restraints) and <s>niyama</s> (observances) but does not seek knowledge — for him, upon death, from dispassion there is dissolution (<s>laya</s>) in the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (primary principles), from <s>Pradhāna</s> through the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements); [he has] connection with enjoyment of sense-objects through the gross body. And one dissolved [in <s>Prakṛti</s>] considers himself as if liberated, but is not [actually] liberated, because of transmigrating again at the time of [a new] creation. But when he seeks knowledge, then he is indeed liberated. And thus it is stated—

children.text: 'saṃsāro bhavati rājasādrāgāt'; iti / vairāgyaviṣayo 'śubhaviṣayābhiṣvaṅgo rājaso rāgaḥ, tasya śubhāśubhakarmākṣepakatvāt / tasmāddevādiṣvayaṃ janādyajibhāvena (?) saṃsarati //
children.translated_text: 'From passionate attachment born of <s>rajas</s>, <s>saṃsāra</s> comes about' — the <s>rājasa</s> (born of <s>rajas</s>) attachment, whose object is the impure attraction to [unwholesome] sense-objects, propels wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>. From that, this [being] transmigrates through [births] among gods and others, in the manner of birth and the like.

children.text: 'aiśvaryādavighātaḥ'; iti / anaiśvaryāttadviparyāsa iti / avighātaviparyāso vighātaḥ, prārthitānāmaprāptirityarthaha / muktistu durotsāritaiva // 45 //
children.translated_text: 'From sovereignty, non-obstruction' — from non-sovereignty, the reverse of that. The reverse of non-obstruction is obstruction — meaning the non-attainment of what is desired. But liberation is set aside entirely. ||45||

children.text: kārikā 46
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 46

children.text: eṣāmaṣṭānāṃ buddhirūpāṇāmekena mokṣaḥ saptabhirbandhaḥ saṃsāra iti yadetannimittanaimittikaṃ ṣoḍaśamuktaṃ tatsaṃkṣepeṇa caturvidhamāha -
children.translated_text: Among these eight [dispositions] in the form of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), by one [i.e., knowledge] there is liberation, and by the [other] seven there is bondage and <s>saṃsāra</s> — this cause-and-effect system that has been described as sixteenfold, he now states in summary as fourfold—

children.text: eṣa pratyayasargo viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhyākhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the intellectual creation (<s>pratyayasarga</s>), called error (<s>viparyaya</s>), incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>), contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), and attainment (<s>siddhi</s>);

children.text: guṇavaiṣamyavimardena tasya bhedāstu pañcāśat || 46 ||
children.translated_text: its subdivisions are fifty, due to the conflict of the imbalance of the <s>guṇas</s>. // ISk 46 //

children.text: 'eṣaḥ'; ityādi / pratyayaśabdena buddhirucyate / tasya sargo yaḥ ṣoḍaśavidha uktaḥ, eṣa viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhyākhyaḥ / viparyayādīnāmākhyā yasya pratyayasargasya sa tathoktaḥ / tatra viparyayamajñānam, aśaktirjñānādhigamāsāmarthyaṃ satyāmapyadhijigāṃsāyām, tuṣṭirmokṣopāyeṣu vaimukhyam, siddhirjñānaprāptiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'This' etc. By the word <s>pratyaya</s>, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is meant. Its creation, which has been described as sixteenfold, is this — called error, incapacity, contentment, and attainment. That intellectual creation which has the designation of <s>viparyaya</s> and the rest is so called. Among these: <s>viparyaya</s> (error) is ignorance; <s>aśakti</s> (incapacity) is the inability to attain knowledge even when there is the desire to know; <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) is aversion toward the means of liberation; <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) is the acquisition of knowledge.

children.text: tasya catuvidhasya punaḥ pañcāśat bhedā bhavanti / kena prakāreṇetyāha- 'guṇavaiṣamyavimardena'; ityādi / sattvarajastamasāmanyo 'nyābhibhavadvāreṇa vaiṣamyaṃ viṣamabhāvaḥ, ekasya dvayorvādhikye 'nyasyānādhikyam / ekadvitriyogena ṣaḍvidhaṃ vaiṣamyam / tena dvayorvimardaḥ parasparakṣobhaḥ / tena hetunā bhavatītyarthaḥ // 46 //
children.translated_text: The subdivisions of this fourfold [creation] are again fifty. By what means? He says: 'Due to the conflict of the imbalance of the <s>guṇas</s>' etc. The imbalance (<s>vaiṣamya</s>) of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — the state of inequality through the overpowering of one by the others — [means] the predominance of one or two and the non-predominance of the other. Through the combination of one, two, or three, the imbalance is sixfold. Through the mutual agitation (<s>vimarda</s>) of [any] two [of these], the fifty subdivisions arise — this is the meaning. ||46||

children.text: kārikā 47
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 47

children.text: tān bhedān darśayannāha-
children.translated_text: Displaying those subdivisions, he says—

children.text: pañca viparyayabhedā bhavantyaśaktiśca karaṇavaikalyāt /
children.translated_text: The subdivisions of error (<s>viparyaya</s>) are five; and incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>), due to the deficiency of the instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>),

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśatibhedā tuṣṭirnavadhā 'ṣṭadhāsiddhiḥ || 47 ||
children.translated_text: has twenty-eight subdivisions; contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) is ninefold; attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) is eightfold. // ISk 47 //

children.text: 'pañca viparyayabhedāḥ'; ityādi / ajñānākhyasya sargasya bhedāḥ pañca- tamo moho mahāmohastāmisro 'ndhatāmisraśceti / ata eva sāṃkhyapravacane kleśā ucyante / 'avidyāsmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśāḥ kleśāḥ'; iti / tatrāvidyākṣetramuttareṣām //
children.translated_text: 'Five subdivisions of error' etc. The subdivisions of the creation called ignorance are five: <s>tamas</s> (darkness), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom), and <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness). For this very reason, in the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacana</s>, they are called <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). '<s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>asmitā</s> (ego-sense), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life) are the <s>kleśas</s>.' Among these, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the field of the subsequent ones.

children.text: 'aśaktiśca'; iti / aśaktyākhyaḥ sargaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'And incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>)' — the creation called <s>aśakti</s>.

children.text: 'karaṇavaikalyāt'; iti / karaṇaṃ bāhyamābhyantaraṃ ca / tayorvaikalyādaṣṭāviṃśatibhedā yasyāḥ aśakteḥ sā bhavatīti vibhaktipariṇāmena yojyam / karaṇavaikalyaṃ ca guṇavaiṣamyavimardena bhavati //
children.translated_text: 'Due to the deficiency of the instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>)' — the instrument is both external and internal. Due to the deficiency of both, [incapacity] has twenty-eight subdivisions — this should be construed with a change of case ending. And the deficiency of the instruments arises due to the conflict of the imbalance of the <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: 'tuṣṭirnavadhā 'ṣṭadhā siddhiḥ'; / iti tuṣṭisargo navaprakāraḥ, siddhisargo 'ṣṭaprakāro bhavatītyarthaḥ / etaiḥ samudāyena pañcāśadbhedā iti // 47 //
children.translated_text: 'Contentment is ninefold, attainment is eightfold' — thus the creation of contentment is of nine kinds, and the creation of attainment is of eight kinds — this is the meaning. By these collectively, there are fifty varieties. ||47||

children.text: kārikā 48
children.translated_text: Kārikā 48

children.text: tānavāntarabhedasahitān darśayannāha-
children.translated_text: Showing those together with their sub-varieties, he says—

children.text: bhedastamaso 'ṣṭavidho mohasya ca, daśavidho mahāmohaḥ /
children.translated_text: The variety of <s>tamas</s> is eightfold; and of <s>moha</s> [it is eightfold too]; <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion) is tenfold;

children.text: tāmisro 'ṣṭādaśadhā, tathā bhavatyandhatāmisraḥ || 48 ||
children.translated_text: <s>tāmisra</s> is eighteenfold; and likewise is <s>andhatāmisra</s>. || 48 ||

children.text: 'bhedastamasaḥ'; ityādi / tama ityavidyocyate / sā cottareṣāṃ prasavabhūmiḥ / sā ca prakṛtiḥ / tattvavedināṃ satyapi vairāgye nāpavarga iti, jñānasyābhāvāt / tataśca teṣāmaṣṭāsveva prakṛtiṣu layo bhavatīti aṣṭavidhā avidyā, viṣayasyāṣṭavidhatvāt //
children.translated_text: 'The variety of <s>tamas</s>' etc. '<s>Tamas</s>' refers to ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). And that is the ground of production for the subsequent [varieties]. And that is <s>Prakṛti</s>. For the knowers of <s>tattvas</s>, even when there is dispassion, there is no liberation — because of the absence of knowledge. And thus their dissolution occurs in the eight <s>Prakṛtis</s> alone — so ignorance is eightfold, because the object [of dissolution] is eightfold.

children.text: mohasya cetiśabdenāṣṭavidho bheda ityanuvartate / moha ityasmitocyate / devā api vināśino 'pi, aṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryamāśritā ātmānamavināśinaṃ manyante / tataśca teṣāmaṣṭavidho mohaḥ, aiśvaryasyāṣṭavidhatvāt //
children.translated_text: 'And of <s>moha</s>' — by the word 'ca' (and), 'eightfold variety' continues [from the previous]. '<s>Moha</s>' refers to egoism (<s>asmitā</s>). Even the gods, though perishable, having resorted to the eightfold sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), consider themselves imperishable. And thus their delusion is eightfold, because sovereignty is eightfold.

children.text: 'daśavidho mahāmohaḥ'; iti sukhānuśayo rāgo mahāmoha ityucyate / sa ca divyādivyaviṣayeṣu vartamāno daśavidho bhavati / tatra sūkṣmāstanmātralakṣaṇāḥ pañca, sukhaikasvabhāvatvāddvivyāḥ / sthūlāḥ pṛthivyādayaḥ pañca, sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatvādadivyāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Tenfold is <s>mahāmoha</s>' — the latent tendency toward pleasure, namely attachment (<s>rāga</s>), is called great delusion (<s>mahāmoha</s>). Operating in both divine and non-divine objects, it becomes tenfold. Of these, the subtle ones, characterized as the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), are divine, because their nature is exclusively pleasurable. The gross ones, namely the five beginning with earth, are non-divine, because their nature consists of pleasure, pain, and delusion.

children.text: 'tāmisro 'ṣṭādaśadhā'; iti / duḥkhānuśayo dveṣastāmisra ityucyate / sa cāṣṭaguṇaiśvarye daśavidhe ca viṣaye pratibhavatītyaṣṭādaśavidhaḥ //
children.translated_text: '<s>Tāmisra</s> is eighteenfold' — the latent tendency toward pain, namely aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), is called <s>tāmisra</s>. It operates with respect to the eightfold sovereignty and the tenfold objects — hence it is eighteenfold.

children.text: 'tathā bhavatyandhatāmisraḥ'; iti / yathā tāmisro 'ṣṭādaśadhā tathā 'yamapītyarthaḥ / maraṇatrāso 'ndhatāmisra ucyate / sa cāṣṭaguṇaiśvarye daśavidhe ca viṣaye pratibhavatītyaṣṭādaśavidhaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Likewise is <s>andhatāmisra</s>' — just as <s>tāmisra</s> is eighteenfold, so too is this one — this is the meaning. The fear of death is called <s>andhatāmisra</s>. It operates with respect to the eightfold sovereignty and the tenfold objects — hence it is eighteenfold.

children.text: 'tathā bhavatyandhatāmisraḥ'; iti / yathā tāmisro 'ṣṭādaśadhā tathā 'yamapītyarthaḥ / maraṇatrāso 'ndhatāmisra ucyate / sa cāṣṭaguṇaiśvarye daśavidhe viṣaya eva bhavatīti / evaṃ dviṣaṣṭibhedamajñānamuktam // 48 //
children.translated_text: 'Likewise is <s>andhatāmisra</s>' — just as <s>tāmisra</s> is eighteenfold, so too is this one — this is the meaning. The fear of death is called <s>andhatāmisra</s>. It operates only with respect to the eightfold sovereignty and the tenfold objects. Thus, ignorance with its sixty-two varieties has been stated. ||48||

children.text: kārikā 49
children.translated_text: Kārikā 49

children.text: aśaktiḥ karaṇavaikalyādityuktam, tasyā bhedān darśayitumāha-
children.translated_text: It was stated that incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>) is due to the deficiency of the organs; to show its varieties, he says—

children.text: ekādaśendriyavadhaḥ saha buddhivadhairaśaktirupadiṣṭā /
children.translated_text: The impairment of the eleven sense-organs, together with the impairments of the intellect, has been taught as incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>);

children.text: saptadaśadhā ca buddherviparyayāstuṣṭisiddhinām || 49 ||
children.translated_text: and the reversals of contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) and attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) belonging to the intellect are seventeenfold. || 49 ||

children.text: 'ekādaśa'; ityādi / ekādaśānāmindriyāṇāmekādaśaivopaghātāḥ / śrotracakṣurghrāṇānāṃ bādhiryāndhatvāghrātṛtvāni, vāco mūkatvam, jihvāyā jāḍyam, manasa unmādaḥ, pāṇipādopasthānāṃ kauṇyapaṅgutvaklaibyāni, tvagindriyasya kuṣṭhaḥ, pāyorudāvarta iti /
bādhiryamāndhyāghrātṛtve mūkatā jaḍatā tathā /
children.translated_text: Deafness, blindness, loss of smell, muteness, torpidity, likewise

children.text: unmādakauṇyakuṣṭhāni klaibyodāvartapaṅgutāḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: madness, being maimed, leprosy, impotence, intestinal disorder, and lameness.

'Eleven' etc. The impairments of the eleven sense-organs are exactly eleven. Of the ear, eye, and nose: deafness, blindness, and loss of smell. Of speech: muteness. Of the tongue: torpidity. Of the mind: madness. Of the hands, feet, and reproductive organ: being maimed, lameness, and impotence. Of the skin-organ: leprosy. Of the excretory organ: intestinal disorder.

children.text: ata indriyavadhā aśaktirityupadiṣṭāḥ sāṃkhyācāryaiḥ //
children.translated_text: Hence, the impairments of the sense-organs have been taught by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> masters as incapacity.

children.text: 'saha buddhivadhaiḥ'; iti / buddherapi vadhā aśaktirupadiṣṭā // te kiyanta ityāha- 'saptadaśadhā ca buddhervupayayāstuṣṭisiddhīnām'; iti / tuṣṭayo nava, siddhayaścāṣṭau / vakṣyamāṇāmbhasāṃ ye viparyayāste saptadaśavidhā buddherjñeyāḥ / evamaśaktiraṣṭāviṃśatibhedā yayā kramasvaśakto bhavati //
children.translated_text: 'Together with the impairments of the intellect' — the impairments of the intellect too have been taught as incapacity. How many are they? He says: 'and the reversals of contentment and attainment belonging to the intellect are seventeenfold.' The contentments are nine, and the attainments are eight. The reversals of these — which will be described as 'waters' — should be understood as the seventeen varieties belonging to the intellect. Thus incapacity has twenty-eight varieties, by which one becomes progressively incapable.

children.text: nanu pratyayasarga ityuktam, nāyamindriyavadhaḥ pratyayasargaḥ kiñcidahaṅkārasarga iti satyam, ahaṅkārasya pratyayasargatvāt tatsargo 'pi pratyayasarga ucyate / dharmo vā pratyayaḥ sargaḥ // 49 //
children.translated_text: Objection: It was said [this is] the intellectual creation (<s>pratyayasarga</s>), but this impairment of the sense-organs is not the intellectual creation — rather it is the creation of the ego-sense (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>). True, but since the ego-sense itself belongs to the intellectual creation, its creation too is called the intellectual creation. Or, the property (<s>dharma</s>) is the basis of the creation. ||49||

children.text: kārikā 50
children.translated_text: Kārikā 50

children.text: tuṣṭibhedānāha-
children.translated_text: He states the varieties of contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>)—

children.text: ādhyātmikāścatasraḥ prakṛtyupādānakālabhāgyākhyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The internal ones are four, called <s>prakṛti</s>, <s>upādāna</s>, <s>kāla</s>, and <s>bhāgya</s>;

children.text: bāhyā viṣayoparamāt pañca, nava tuṣṭayo 'bhimatāḥ || 50 ||
children.translated_text: the external ones are five, from withdrawal from sense-objects; thus nine contentments are recognized. || 50 ||

children.text: 'ādhyātmikāḥ'; ityādinā / prakṛtyādīnyākhyā yāsāṃ tuṣṭīnāṃ tāstathoktāḥ / tatra prakṛtiḥ pradhānam / saiva vyaktātmanā pariṇamya bandhamokṣau kuruta ityetāvanmātropadeśāt tuṣṭo bhavati yastasya prakṛtyākhyā tuṣṭirambha ityucyate //
children.translated_text: 'Internal' etc. Those contentments whose names are <s>prakṛti</s> and so forth are so designated. Of these, '<s>prakṛti</s>' is <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primal Nature). He who becomes satisfied merely from the teaching that '<s>Pradhāna</s> itself, having transformed into manifest form, produces bondage and liberation' — his contentment named after <s>prakṛti</s> is called '<s>ambhas</s>' (water).

children.text: upādīyate prāpyate mokṣo 'nenetyupādānam / pravrajyāliṅgaṃ cātra daṇḍādi / na prakṛtijñānamātreṇa muktiḥ / 'upādānena cāpare'; ityasmādadvitīyādupadeśādihaiva muktiḥ prāptavyeti parituṣṭaḥ pravrajito 'yaṃ tasya dvitīyā upādānākhyā tuṣṭiḥ salilamucyate //
children.translated_text: '<s>Upādāna</s>' is that by which liberation is attained — that is, the insignia of renunciation (<s>pravrajyā</s>) such as the staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>) etc. Liberation does not come from mere knowledge of <s>Prakṛti</s>. He who, from this second teaching — 'and others through means (<s>upādāna</s>)' — becomes fully satisfied that liberation is to be attained in this very [life through renunciation], and has gone forth — his second contentment named <s>upādāna</s> is called '<s>salila</s>' (water).

children.text: kalyata iti kālā / mahadādisūkṣmaparyantena liṅgena saṃsaratā 'pareṇa mokṣo na prakṛtyupādānamātrādihaiva janmanīti tasmāttṛtīyādupadeśāt tuṣṭo yaḥ kālāpekṣī sthitastasya kālākhyā tuṣṭirodha ityucyate //
children.translated_text: '<s>Kāla</s>' — [time] is that which is reckoned. He who, transmigrating by means of the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) from <s>Mahat</s> through to the subtle [elements], [reasons that] liberation [will come] through another [way], not merely through <s>prakṛti</s> or <s>upādāna</s> in this very birth — he who remains waiting upon time from this third teaching, his contentment named <s>kāla</s> is called '<s>ogha</s>' (flood).

children.text: yasyāparaṃ bhāgyamasti tasya mokṣaḥ, prakṛtyupādānakālamātreṇa na, kaścidviparītabhāgadheyo 'stīti tasmāccaturthādupadeśāt tuṣṭo yo bhāgyāpekṣī sthitastasya caturthī vṛṣṭirityucyate / etāścatasra ātmānamadhikṛtya bhavantītyādhyātmikāḥ ātmanā moktavyamiti kṛtvā //
children.translated_text: He whose extraordinary fortune (<s>bhāgya</s>) exists — for him is liberation, not merely through <s>prakṛti</s>, <s>upādāna</s>, or <s>kāla</s>; [but] some have an adverse destiny — he who from this fourth teaching remains waiting upon fortune, his fourth [contentment] is called '<s>vṛṣṭi</s>' (rain). These four are internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) because they arise with reference to the self, having concluded 'one must be liberated by oneself.'

children.text: 'bāhyaviṣayoparamācca'; iti / śabdādibhyo vyāvṛttiruparamaṇaṃ pañcadhā bhavati / ārjanarakṣaṇakṣayasaṅgahiṃsādoṣadarśanāt / tatra viṣayārjane mahadduḥkhaṃ tadalpaviṣayebhya ityārjanadoṣadarśanānnivṛttasya tuṣṭiriyaṃ pañcamī sutāramityucyate //
children.translated_text: 'And from withdrawal from external objects' — withdrawal from sound and other [sense-objects] is fivefold, because of seeing the faults of acquisition (<s>ārjana</s>), preservation (<s>rakṣaṇa</s>), loss (<s>kṣaya</s>), attachment (<s>saṅga</s>), and injury (<s>hiṃsā</s>). Of these, [seeing that] there is great suffering in acquiring sense-objects — 'that is [to be gained] from a few objects' — the contentment of one who has desisted from seeing the fault of acquisition, this fifth one, is called '<s>sutāra</s>.'

children.text: viṣayā ārjituṃ śakyāḥ, rakṣaṇaṃ tu duḥkhaṃ bahubhiḥ tajjanyamānānāṃ (?) syāditi rakṣaṇadarśanānnivṛtasya tuṣṭiriyaṃ ṣaṣṭhī supāramityucyate //
children.translated_text: Objects can be acquired, but their preservation is painful for those who have produced many [possessions] — from seeing [the fault of] preservation, the contentment of one who has desisted, this sixth one, is called '<s>supāra</s>.'

children.text: viṣayā ārjituṃ rakṣituṃ kṣaye ca pratividhātuṃ śakyāḥ, kintūpabhujyamānā mahatīmātmasaktiṃ kurvanti, tadaprāptau ca mahadduḥkhamiti saṅgadoṣadarśanāduparastasyāṣṭamī tuṣṭiranuttamāmbha ityucyate //
children.translated_text: Objects can be acquired, preserved, and measures against loss can be taken; but when being enjoyed, they create great attachment to oneself, and from not attaining that, great suffering arises — from seeing the fault of attachment (<s>saṅga</s>), the contentment of one who has desisted, this eighth one, is called '<s>anuttamāmbhas</s>.'

children.text: sarvaṃ śakyaṃ kintvanupahatya bhūtāni na bhogaḥ sambhavati / bhūtopaghātānmahadaniṣṭaphalamiti hiṃsādoṣadarśanāduparatasya tuṣṭiriyaṃ navamī uttamāmbha ityucyate / etāḥ pañca viṣayadvāreṇeti bhavantīti bāhyāḥ / tatpūrvikāścādhyātmikāḥ, viṣaye tatparasyādhyātmikatuṣṭyasambhavāt //
children.translated_text: All [the above] is possible, but enjoyment does not occur without harming beings. From the injury to beings, there is a great undesirable consequence — from seeing the fault of injury (<s>hiṃsā</s>), the contentment of one who has desisted, this ninth one, is called '<s>uttamāmbhas</s>.' These five arise through the doorway of sense-objects, hence they are external. And the [first four] are preceded by those [considerations], hence they are internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>), because one who is devoted to sense-objects cannot have internal contentment.

children.text: tatra prakṛtyupādānakālā na mokṣopāyā ityupadiṣṭamapi yo vaimukhyānna pratipadyate tasyādhyātmikāścatasraḥ, viṣayoparamācca bāhyāḥ pañceti nava tuṣṭayaḥ / tā buddhivadhā ityucante / teṣāṃ śakterantarbhavati [?] / tāsāṃ catuṣṣaṣṭīnāṃ mahatprabhṛtayo viparyayeṇa saṃjñā / tadubhayamapi buddhāvantarbhūtaṃ tatsargatvāt // 50 //
children.translated_text: Thus, although it has been taught that <s>prakṛti</s>, <s>upādāna</s>, and <s>kāla</s> are not means to liberation, he who through aversion does not accept [this] — for him the four are internal, and from withdrawal from sense-objects, the five are external — thus nine contentments. They are called impairments of the intellect. Their power is subsumed within [the intellect]. The names of those sixty-four, beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, are given in reverse order. Both of these [groups] are subsumed within the intellect, because they belong to its creation. ||50||

children.text: kārikā 51
children.translated_text: Kārikā 51

children.text: katibhedā jñānājñānalakṣaṇā siddhirityāha-
children.translated_text: He says [how many] are the varieties of attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) characterized as knowledge and non-knowledge—

children.text: ūhaḥ śabdo 'dhyayanaṃ duḥkhavighātāstrayaḥ suhṛtprāptiḥ /
children.translated_text: Reasoning (<s>ūha</s>), verbal instruction (<s>śabda</s>), study (<s>adhyayana</s>), the three [arising from] removal of suffering, attainment through a friend (<s>suhṛtprāpti</s>),

children.text: dānaṃ ca siddhayo 'ṣṭau, siddheḥ pūrvo 'ṅkuśastrividhaḥ || 51 ||
children.translated_text: and giving (<s>dāna</s>) — these are the eight attainments; the prior impediment (<s>aṅkuśa</s>) to attainment is threefold. || 51 ||

children.text: 'ūhaḥ śabdo 'dhyayanam'; ityādi / siddhirjñānaprāptiḥ, tasyā bhedā upāyabhedāt / ūha iti / janmāntarasaṃskṛtadhiyo yasya bandhamokṣakāraṇamutprekṣamāṇasya pradhānapuruṣāntarajñānamutpadyate tasya siddhirūhahetukā prathamā tāramityucyate //
children.translated_text: 'Reasoning, verbal instruction, study' etc. Attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) is the obtaining of knowledge; its varieties arise from the difference of means. '<s>Ūha</s>' (reasoning) — for one whose intellect has been refined in a previous birth, who, contemplating the cause of bondage and liberation, gains the knowledge of the distinction between <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — his attainment, caused by reasoning, the first one, is called '<s>tāra</s>.'

children.text: yasya sāṃkhyaśāstrapāṭhamanyadīyamākarṇya tattvajñānamutpadyate, sā siddhiḥ śabdahetukā dvitīyā sutāramityucyate //
children.translated_text: For one in whom knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> arises from hearing the recitation of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> scripture from another — that attainment, caused by verbal instruction (<s>śabda</s>), the second one, is called '<s>sutāra</s>.'

children.text: yasya śiṣyācāryasambandhena sāṃkhyaśāstraṃ śabdato 'rthataścādhītya jñānamutpadyate, tasyādhyayanahetukā / adhyayanena hi tatparijñānāt / eṣā tṛtīyā tāravi ityucyate //
children.translated_text: For one in whom knowledge arises from studying the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> scripture both in its words and meaning through the pupil-teacher relationship — his [attainment] is caused by study (<s>adhyayana</s>). For through study comes complete understanding of that. This third one is called '<s>tāratāra</s>.'

children.text: 'duḥkhavighātāstrayaḥ'; iti / yo 'pyādhyātmikenādhibhautikenādhidaivikena vā bhāvitastadvighātārthaṃ jñānaṃ paryeṣyati, ūhena śabdenādhyayanena vā, tasya tadvighātahetukāḥ pramādapramuditamodanākhyāstisraḥ, upāyasya tritvāditi / pūrvā yāstisraḥ siddhyayastā na duḥkhahetukā iti boddhavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'The three from the removal of suffering' — he who, being affected by <s>ādhyātmika</s>, <s>ādhibhautika</s>, or <s>ādhidaivika</s> [suffering], will seek knowledge for the removal of that, through reasoning, verbal instruction, or study — for him, the three [attainments] caused by that removal are called '<s>pramoda</s>,' '<s>pramudita</s>,' and '<s>modamāna</s>,' because the means are threefold. The first three attainments should be understood as not caused by suffering.

children.text: 'suhṛtprāptiḥ'; iti / yo 'dhigatatattvaḥ suhṛdaṃ prāpya jñānamadhigacchati, tasya suhṛtprāptipūrvikā / mitraṃ hi snehāt jñānaṃ prakāśayati / iyaṃ saptamī ramyakamityucyate //
children.translated_text: 'Attainment through a friend (<s>suhṛtprāpti</s>)' — one who, having understood the truth, obtains knowledge by reaching a friend, for him [siddhi] is preceded by the attainment of a friend. For a friend, out of affection, reveals knowledge. This seventh [siddhi] is called <s>Ramyaka</s>.

children.text: dānaṃ ca siddhihetuḥ / dānena hyārādhito jñānī jñānaṃ prayacchati / iyamaṣṭamī sadāpramuditamityucyate //
children.translated_text: Giving (<s>dāna</s>) too is a cause of attainment. For a knower, propitiated by giving, bestows knowledge. This eighth [siddhi] is called <s>Sadāpramudita</s> (ever-delighted).

children.text: tadviparītā asiddhayaḥ / mandabuddhitvānnohate yastasyānūhahetukā asiddhiḥ / yaḥ śakto 'pi sāṃkhyaśāstraṃ śṛṇvannapi buddhidaurbalyānna buddhyati tasya śabdahetukā asiddhiḥ / buddhidoṣa evāyam / yasya gurupūrvakaṃ nādhyayanaṃ buddhidoṣādeva tasyānadhyayanahetukā asiddhiḥ / na yatra mitrasaṃgraho na ca dānamityaṣṭāvasiddhayo buddhivadhā aśaktāvantarbhūtāḥ / tāsāṃ cāsiddhīnāṃ moṣamuṣṇāmānoramityādyāḥ [?] saṃjñāḥ / buddhāvantarbhūtaṃ tatsargatvāt //
children.translated_text: The opposites of these are the non-attainments (<s>asiddhis</s>). For one whose intellect is dull and who cannot reason, [there is] non-attainment caused by lack of reasoning (<s>anūha</s>). For one who, though capable, while hearing the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> treatise, does not understand due to weakness of intellect, [there is] non-attainment caused by verbal instruction (<s>śabda</s>) — this is itself a defect of intellect. For one who, due to a defect of intellect, does not undertake study preceded by a teacher, [there is] non-attainment caused by lack of study (<s>anadhyayana</s>). Where there is no friendship and no giving — these eight non-attainments, which are destructions of intellect, are included within incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>). And the names of these non-attainments are <s>Moṣamuṣṇā</s>, <s>Mānorama</s>, etc. These are included within <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), because of being its creation.

children.text: 'siddheḥ pūrvo 'ṅkuśastrividhaḥ'; iti / tasyā aṣṭavidhāyāḥ siddheryaḥ pūrvo viparyayāśaktituṣṭyākhyastrividha uktaḥ so 'ṅkuśa ivetyaṅkuśa uktaḥ / tena hyasvatantrīkṛto lokaḥ saṃsāracakre 'vatiṣṭhate / tatra viparyayādiṣyate bandha iti vacanāt pañcavidhamajñānamaṅkuśaḥ / aśaktiḥ karaṇavaikalyam, tato hi jñānāprāptirityaṅkuśaḥ / tuṣṭirapyaṅkuśaḥ / tadā prakṛtyupādānakālabhāgyā mokṣopāyā iti, viṣayoparamācca mukta ityetāvanmātrādupadeśāt tuṣṭo na jñānaṃ paryeṣyati / yadā tu paryeṣyati tadā 'naṅkuśa ityarthaḥ / ete pratyayasargabhedāḥ pañcāśat padārthāḥ, astitvādayaśca daśa / te cāsyāmeva saptatyāṃ nirdiṣṭāḥ / tathā cāha saṃgrahakāraḥ-
astitvamekatvamathārthavattvaṃ pārārthyamanyatvamakartṛbhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Existence, oneness, purposefulness, serving another's purpose, otherness, non-doership,

children.text: yogo viyogo bahavaḥ pumāṃsaḥ sthitiḥ śarīrasya ca śeṣavṛttiḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: conjunction, disjunction, the multiplicity of <s>Puruṣas</s>, the persistence of the body, and residual activity.

'The threefold goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>) precedes attainment (<s>siddhi</s>)' — that which precedes the eightfold attainment and has been described as threefold, namely error (<s>viparyaya</s>), incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>), and contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), is called a goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>). For, made unfree by it, the world remains in the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Among these, because of the statement 'from the opposite [of knowledge], bondage is obtained,' the fivefold ignorance is a goad. Incapacity is the deficiency of the instruments — since from that there is non-attainment of knowledge, it is a goad. Contentment too is a goad. Then [one thinks]: <s>Prakṛti</s>, material means, time, and fortune are the means of liberation, and one is liberated merely from the cessation of sense-objects — from just this much instruction, being contented, one does not seek knowledge. But when one does seek [knowledge], then [contentment] is no longer a goad — this is the meaning. These subdivisions of the intellectual creation are fifty topics; and there are also ten beginning with 'existence' (<s>astitva</s>). And these too are enumerated in this very <s>Saptati</s> (Seventy [verses]). And thus the author of the <s>Saṃgraha</s> (Compendium) says—

children.text: ekatvamarthavattvaṃ pārārthyaṃ ceti pradhānamadhikṛtyoktam / anyatvamakartṛtvaṃ bahutvaṃ ceti puruṣamadhikṛtya / astitvaṃ yogo viyogaścetyubhayamadhikṛtya / sthitirmūlasūkṣmamadhikṛtya / vakṣyati- 'tiṣṭhati saṃskāravaśāt'; iti / ete ṣaṣṭi padārthāḥ, tadarthaṃ śāstraṃ ṣaṣṭitantramityucyate // 51 //
children.translated_text: Oneness, purposefulness, and serving another's purpose are stated with reference to <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature). Otherness, non-doership, and multiplicity are stated with reference to <s>Puruṣa</s>. Existence, conjunction, and disjunction are stated with reference to both. Persistence is stated with reference to the root subtle [body]. He will say: 'It persists due to the force of impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>).' These are sixty topics — for the sake of [explaining] them, the treatise is called <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> (the Sixty-Topic System). ||51||

children.text: kārikā 52
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 52

children.text: pūrvotpannaṃ liṅgaṃ bhāvairadhivāsitaṃ saṃsaratītyuktam, tatra kiṃ bhāvā api pūrvamutpannāḥ kiṃ liṅgamevetyatrāha-
children.translated_text: It was stated that the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), which arose previously and is perfumed by the dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>), transmigrates. Now, did the dispositions also arise previously, or [did they arise] along with the <s>liṅga</s> itself? To this he says—

children.text: na vinā bhāvairliṅgam, na vinā liṅgena bhāvaniṣpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Without the dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>), the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) [does not function]; without the <s>liṅga</s>, there is no production of dispositions.

children.text: liṅgākhyo bhāvākhyastasmāddvividhaḥ pravartate sargaḥ || 52 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore a twofold creation proceeds — one called <s>liṅga</s> and one called <s>bhāva</s>. // ISk 52 //

children.text: 'na vinā'; ityādi / yadi bhāvā na pūrvotpannāstairvinā liṅgamapi nāsti / saṃsaraṇārthaṃ liṅgaṃ saṃsāranimittaṃ ca bhāvāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Without' etc. If the dispositions did not arise previously, then without them the <s>liṅga</s> too does not exist. The <s>liṅga</s> is for the purpose of transmigration, and the dispositions are the causes of transmigration.

children.text: 'na vinā liṅgena bhāvaniṣpattiḥ'; iti / liṅgaṃ vinā na bhāvāniṣpattiḥ, liṅgāśritatvādbhāvānām / yasmādevaṃ tasmāt liṅgākhyo bhāvākhyaśca dviprakāraḥ pradhānatvāt sargo bhavatīti / sṛjyata iti sargaḥ // 52 //
children.translated_text: 'Without the <s>liṅga</s>, there is no production of dispositions' — without the <s>liṅga</s>, there is no production of dispositions, because the dispositions depend on the <s>liṅga</s>. Since this is so, therefore the twofold creation — called <s>liṅga</s> and called <s>bhāva</s> — exists because of [their] primacy. That which is created is creation (<s>sarga</s>). ||52||

children.text: kārikā 53
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 53

children.text: yathā dvāvetau pūrvotpannau tatha bhūtasargo 'pīti darśayannāha-
children.translated_text: Just as these two [liṅga and bhāva] arose previously, so too the elemental creation (<s>bhūtasarga</s>) — showing this, he says—

children.text: aṣṭavikalpa daivastairyagyonyaśca pañcadhā bhavati /
children.translated_text: The divine [creation] is of eight varieties; the animal (<s>tairyagyoni</s>) comes about in five ways;

children.text: mānuṣyacaikavidhaḥ, samāsato bhautikaḥ sargaḥ || 53 ||
children.translated_text: and the human (<s>mānuṣya</s>) is of one kind — this, in brief, is the elemental creation (<s>bhautika sarga</s>). // ISk 53 //

children.text: 'aṣṭavikalpaḥ'; ityādi / devānāmayaṃ daivaḥ / so 'ṣṭavidhaḥ / tadyathā brāhmaḥ, prājāpatyaḥ, sauraḥ, āsuraḥ, gāndharvaḥ, yākṣaḥ, rākṣasaḥ, paiśācaśceti //
children.translated_text: 'Of eight varieties' etc. That which belongs to the gods is divine (<s>daiva</s>). It is of eight kinds. Namely: <s>Brāhma</s> (pertaining to <s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Prājāpatya</s> (pertaining to <s>Prajāpati</s>), <s>Saura</s> (pertaining to the <s>Sun</s>), <s>Āsura</s> (pertaining to the <s>Asuras</s>), <s>Gāndharva</s> (pertaining to the <s>Gandharvas</s>), <s>Yākṣa</s> (pertaining to the <s>Yakṣas</s>), <s>Rākṣasa</s> (pertaining to the <s>Rākṣasas</s>), and <s>Paiśāca</s> (pertaining to the <s>Piśācas</s>).

children.text: 'tairyagyonyaśca pañcadhā bhavati'; iti / tiryagyonīnāmayaṃ tairyagyonyaḥ / paśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpasthāvarabhedāt pañcavidhaḥ / tatra gavādyā rāsabhāntāḥ paśavaḥ / siṃhādyā biḍālāntā mṛgāḥ / haṃsādyā maśakāntāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ / sarpādayaḥ kṛmyantāḥ sarīsṛpāḥ / vṛkṣādayaḥ sthūṇāntāḥ sthāvarā iti //
children.translated_text: 'The animal [creation] comes about in five ways' — that which belongs to those born from animal wombs is <s>tairyagyoni</s> (animal [creation]). It is fivefold, according to the division into domestic animals (<s>paśu</s>), wild animals (<s>mṛga</s>), birds (<s>pakṣin</s>), reptiles (<s>sarīsṛpa</s>), and immobile beings (<s>sthāvara</s>). Among these: cows and the like up to donkeys are domestic animals. Lions and the like up to cats are wild animals. Geese and the like up to mosquitoes are birds. Snakes and the like up to worms are reptiles. Trees and the like up to stumps are immobile beings.

children.text: 'mānuṣyaścaikavidhaḥ'; iti / manuṣyāṇāmayaṃ mānuṣyaḥ / evaṃvidhasaṃsthānasyaikavidhatvāt / brāhmādibhedo 'pi sattvarajastamasāṃ vikalpāt kālavyavahāranimittam //
children.translated_text: 'And the human is of one kind' — that which belongs to humans is <s>mānuṣya</s> (human [creation]). It is of one kind because of having a single type of bodily form. Even the division into <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the others is due to the variation of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, and is merely a convention based on time.

children.text: 'samāsataḥ'; iti / saṃkṣepeṇa / vistaraṃ...tastasyaiva (?) - jarāyujāṇḍajoṣmajodbhijjākhyāścatvāro bhedāḥ śāstrāntare draṣṭavyāḥ / udbhijjāḥ sthāvarāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'In brief' — in summary. In detail... the four divisions known as <s>jarāyuja</s> (born from a womb), <s>aṇḍaja</s> (born from an egg), <s>svedaja</s> (born from moisture), and <s>udbhijja</s> (born by sprouting) should be seen in other treatises. The <s>udbhijjas</s> are the immobile beings.

children.text: 'bhautikaḥ sargaḥ'; iti / bhūteṣu bhavo bhautikaḥ, lokotpāda ityarthaḥ / sa ca dvividhaḥ // 53 //
children.translated_text: 'Elemental creation (<s>bhautika sarga</s>)' — that which exists among the elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) is <s>bhautika</s>, meaning the arising of the world. And it is twofold. ||53||

children.text:
kārikā 53
sthūlaśarīre sattvayi kaścideva kvacidadhikyena vartata iti darśayannāha-
children.translated_text:
<s>Kārikā</s> 53 [i.e., 54]
Showing that in the gross body, among the three [<s>guṇas</s>], one or another predominates in different [beings], he says—

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ sattvaviśālastamoviśālaśca mūlataḥ sargaḥ /
children.translated_text: Above, the creation is extensive in <s>sattva</s>; below, it is extensive in <s>tamas</s>;

children.text: madhye rajoviśālo, brahmādistambaparyantaḥ || 54 ||
children.translated_text: in the middle, it is extensive in <s>rajas</s> — from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass. // ISk 54 //

children.text: 'ūrdhvam'; ityādi / brahmā ādiryasya sargasya stambaśca tṛṇaviṭapaparyantaḥ, sa brahmādistambaparyantaḥ sargaḥ / sa ūrdhvaḥ sattvaviśālaḥ / ūrdhvaṃ devalokastasyotkṛṣṭatvāt tatra sāttvika ityarthaḥ / devalokasya sattvabahulatvāt //
children.translated_text: 'Above' etc. That creation whose beginning is <s>Brahmā</s> and whose end is a stump or blade of grass — that is the creation 'from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass.' Its upper [portion] is extensive in <s>sattva</s>. The upper [realm] is the world of the gods — because of its excellence, there it is <s>sāttvika</s> (predominated by <s>sattva</s>), this is the meaning — because the divine world abounds in <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: 'tamoviśālaśca mūlataḥ sargaḥ'; iti / tairyagyono mūlam, tasyādhamatvāt / tasmin mūle tamo 'dhikaṃ tamobahulatvāt //
children.translated_text: 'Below, the creation is extensive in <s>tamas</s>' — the animal birth is the lowest, because of its inferiority. In that lowest [realm], <s>tamas</s> predominates, because of the abundance of <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: 'madhye rajoviśālaḥ'; iti / manuṣyaloke madhye / uttarādharabhāvāt tatra duḥkhabahulatvāt // 54 //
children.translated_text: 'In the middle, it is extensive in <s>rajas</s>' — in the human world, which is the middle. Because of being between the upper and lower, and because of the abundance of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) there. ||54||

children.text: kārikā 55
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 55

children.text: yadi triṣu lokeṣu liṅgaṃ saṃsarati, tadeva tarhi sāṃsārikaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vāpnoti, tasyaiva sāṃsārikatvādityāha-
children.translated_text: If the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) transmigrates through the three worlds, then surely it alone experiences worldly pleasure or pain, since it alone is worldly — to this he says—

children.text: tatra jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpnoti cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, the conscious <s>Puruṣa</s> experiences suffering caused by old age and death;

children.text: liṅgasyāvinivṛttestasmād duḥkhaṃ svabhāvena || 55 ||
children.translated_text: because of the non-cessation of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), therefore suffering is [its] inherent nature. // ISk 55 //

children.text: 'tatra'; ityādi / teṣu lokeṣu jarāmaraṇakṛtamiti caturduḥkhopalakṣaṇārtham / garbhaduḥkham, janmaduḥkham, jarāduḥkham, maraṇaduḥkhamiti / tatra mātuḥ kukṣau andhatamasīva praviṣṭasya saṅkucanaprasāraṇaduḥkhaṃ garbhaduḥkham / jāyamānasya māturudarānnirgacchato janmaduḥkham / va.....pālataskhalanādiduḥkhaṃ jarāduḥkham / maraṇāvasthāyāṃ sthūlaśarīraṃ tyajato maraṇaduḥkham / etattvādhyātmikaṃ duḥkhe 'ntarbhūtamaprītaduḥkhaṃ buddhyādhyavasitaṃ puruṣaḥ prāpnoti tasya cetanatvāt, na tu liṅgamacetanatvāditi bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'There' etc. In those worlds, 'caused by old age and death' is meant to indicate all four [kinds of] suffering. The suffering of the womb (<s>garbha</s>), the suffering of birth (<s>janma</s>), the suffering of old age (<s>jarā</s>), and the suffering of death (<s>maraṇa</s>). Among these: for one who has entered the mother's womb as if into blind darkness, the suffering of contraction and expansion is the suffering of the womb. For one being born, emerging from the mother's belly, [there is] the suffering of birth. The suffering of [childish] stumbling and the like in... is the suffering of old age. At the stage of death, the suffering of abandoning the gross body is the suffering of death. This suffering, which is of the nature of displeasure and is included within the <s>ādhyātmika</s> (self-originated) type of suffering, is ascertained by <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and experienced by <s>Puruṣa</s>, because of its being conscious — but not by the <s>liṅga</s>, because of its being non-conscious. This is the purport.

children.text: kiyantaṃ kālamityāha- 'liṅgasyāvinivṛtteḥ'; iti / yāvalliṅgasyāvinivṛttistāvadityarthaḥ / tasya ca nivṛttiḥ pradhānapuruṣāntarajñānāt / yataścaivaṃ tasmādduḥkhaṃ svabhāvena / liṅgagarbhādyavasthāsu svabhāvato duḥkhamityarthaḥ / lokatraye sukhamapi prāpnoti, tannoktaṃ tasyāniyatatvāt / jarādiduḥkhaṃ tu niyatamiti // 55 //
children.translated_text: For how long? He says: 'Because of the non-cessation of the <s>liṅga</s>.' For as long as there is non-cessation of the <s>liṅga</s> — this is the meaning. And its cessation comes from the discriminative knowledge of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. And since this is so, therefore suffering is inherent by nature. In the states of the <s>liṅga</s> such as the womb and the rest, suffering is by nature — this is the meaning. [<s>Puruṣa</s>] also experiences pleasure in the three worlds, but that is not mentioned because of its non-invariability. But the suffering of old age and the rest is invariable. ||55||

children.text: kārikā 56
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 56

children.text:
yo 'yaṃ bhāvaliṅgabhūtatatsargaḥ sa kimīśvarāt, yathocyate-
īśvaraprerito gacchet svargaṃ vā śvabhrameva vā /
iti, kiṃ vā puruṣāt, yathocyate-
puruṣa evedaṃ sarvaṃ yadbhūtaṃ yacca bhavyam /
iti, kiṃ vā svabhāvāt, yathocyate-
svabhāvikamevedaṃ sarvaṃ jagannahi marudādayaḥ kenacit kriyante /
ityatrāha-
children.translated_text: This creation consisting of dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>), subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>), elements (<s>bhūta</s>), and their [products] — is it from God (<s>Īśvara</s>), as stated: 'Impelled by God, one goes to heaven or to a dog's den'? Or from <s>Puruṣa</s>, as stated: '<s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this, whatever has been and whatever will be'? Or from inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), as stated: 'All this entire world is natural, for no one creates the winds and such'? To this he says—

children.text: ityeṣa prakṛtikṛto mahadādiviśeṣabhūtaparyantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus this [creation], made by <s>Prakṛti</s>, extending from <s>Mahat</s> to the specific elements (<s>viśeṣa-bhūta</s>),

children.text: pratipuruṣavimokṣārthaṃ svārtha iva parārtha ārambhaḥ || 56 ||
children.translated_text: [functions] for the liberation of each individual <s>Puruṣa</s> — [this is] an undertaking for another's sake, though appearing as if for its own sake. // ISk 56 //

children.text: 'ityeṣa prakṛtikṛtaḥ'; ityādi / ārabhyata ityārambhaḥ / prakṛtikṛta iti pradhānakṛtaḥ, neśvarādikṛta ityarthaḥ / lokatrayaṃ triguṇātmakaṃ bhavati, tacca triguṇāyā eva prakṛterutpadyate / napai svabhāvikam, viparītaguṇadoṣaprasaṅgāddeśāniyamayogācca //
children.translated_text: 'Thus this, made by <s>Prakṛti</s>' etc. 'Undertaking' (<s>ārambha</s>) means that which is begun. 'Made by <s>Prakṛti</s>' means made by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature), not made by God or others — this is the meaning. The three worlds are constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>, and they arise only from <s>Prakṛti</s> which is [itself] constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>. Nor is it [merely] natural, because of the unwanted consequence of properties and defects being reversed, and because of the [observed] non-restriction to [particular] places.

children.text: sa kiṃsvarūpa ityāha- 'mahadādiviśeṣabhūtaparyantaḥ'; iti / buddhirādiryasyārambhasya / bhūtāni lokatraye yānyabhinnasaṃsthānāni sthūlaśarīrākhyāni / viṣayāśca / bāhyāśca viṣayāḥ sūkṣmāḥ sthūlāḥ / te paryante 'vasāne yasya sa tathoktaḥ / anena bhāvaliṅgabhūtasargākhyāstraya ākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: What is its nature? To this he says: 'Extending from <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One) to the specific elements.' <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) is the beginning of the production. The 'elements' are the beings in the three worlds that have distinct bodily forms, called gross bodies, and [their] objects. The external objects too, both subtle and gross. That which has these as its end-points — such is its designation. By this, the three [creations] called the creation of dispositions (<s>bhāvasarga</s>), the creation of the subtle body (<s>liṅgasarga</s>), and the creation of elements (<s>bhūtasarga</s>) are indicated.

children.text: kimarthamayaṃ pradhānasyārambha ityatrāha- 'pratipuruṣavimokṣārtham'; iti / ekaikasya puruṣasya puruṣasya vimuktyarthamārambhaḥ, puruṣāṇāṃ bahutvāt / bhāvasarge bhūtasarge cāneka iti darśayati / tathāhi mokṣārthaṃ viṣayopabhogārthaṃ cāyamārambha iti draṣṭavyam / pradhānena hi puruṣārthaḥ kartavyaḥ / sa ca dvividhaḥ / viṣayopabhogaḥ kaivalyaṃ ca / tadubhayaṃ kṛtvā nivartata iti //
children.translated_text: For what purpose is this production of <s>Pradhāna</s>? To this he says: 'For the liberation of each and every <s>Puruṣa</s>.' The production is for the liberation of each individual <s>Puruṣa</s>, since <s>Puruṣas</s> are multiple. He shows that in the creation of dispositions and in the creation of elements it is manifold. For this production should be understood as being for the purpose of liberation and for the purpose of experiencing objects. For the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> must be accomplished by <s>Pradhāna</s>. And that is twofold: the enjoyment of objects and <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation/liberation). Having accomplished both, it ceases.

children.text: 'svārthaḥ'; iti / yaḥ kaścit devadattasvārtha eva parārtho rahititaṃ pravartate na parastapastakaroti (?) tathā pradhānamapītyarthaḥ // 56 //
children.translated_text: 'For its own purpose' — just as someone's own purpose is accomplished for <s>Devadatta</s> without causing suffering to others, so too <s>Pradhāna</s> [acts selflessly] — this is the meaning. // 56 //

children.text: kārikā 57
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 57]

children.text: nanu ca sacetanasya buddhipūrvikā pravṛttirbhavati, pradhānasyācetanatvātkathaṃ lokatraye puruṣaṃ viṣayaiḥ saṃyojya dhyānena vipramocya nivarteta / kathamevaṃvidhā pravṛttiḥ / nāyaṃ niyamaḥ, acetanānāmapi loke pravṛttidarśanāt / yadāha-
children.translated_text: Objection: A sentient being's activity is preceded by deliberation (<s>buddhipūrvikā</s>). Since <s>Pradhāna</s> is insentient, how can it, having united <s>Puruṣa</s> with objects in the three worlds, liberate [him] through meditation and then cease? How is such activity [possible]? This rule does not hold, since activity is observed in the world even among insentient things. As he says:

children.text: vatsavivṛddhinimittaṃ kṣīrasya yathā pravṛttirajñasya /
children.translated_text: Just as the activity of insentient milk is for the purpose of nourishing the calf,

children.text: puruṣavimokṣanimittaṃ tathā pravṛttiḥ pradhānasya || 57 ||
children.translated_text: so too is the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> for the purpose of liberating <s>Puruṣa</s>. // ISk 57 //

children.text: 'vatsavivṛddhinimittam'; ityādi / vatsasya vivṛddhiḥ puṣṭiḥ / tasyā nimittam //
children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of nourishing the calf' and so on. The nourishment of the calf means its growth. That is the purpose.

children.text: 'kṣīrasya yathā pravṛttirajñasya'; iti / acetanasya / yathā tṛṇadikamacetanaṃ gavāśitaṃ pītaṃ ca, vatsasya puṣṭiḥ kartavyeti, kṣīrātmanā pariṇamati kṛtārthaṃ ca nivartata iti // 57 //
children.translated_text: 'Just as the activity of insentient milk' — of the insentient. Just as insentient grass and other [food] consumed and drunk by a cow transforms itself into milk, [thinking as it were] 'the calf's nourishment must be accomplished,' and having fulfilled its purpose, ceases. // 57 //

children.text: kārikā 58
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 58]

children.text: yadi puruṣavimokṣārthaṃ pradhānasya pravṛttiḥ, pravṛtteḥ prāk puruṣasya kaivalyaṃ sthitameva, tat kiṃ tena pravṛttena? tathā cāhuḥ -
children.translated_text: If the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> is for the liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s>, [then] prior to that activity, <s>Puruṣa</s>'s <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) was already established — so what is the use of that activity? And thus they say:

children.text: madhvarthaṃ prasthitaḥ kaścid grāmābhyāśe tu mākṣikam /
children.translated_text: 'Someone set out for the purpose of [obtaining] honey; but near the village he found bee-honey.',

children.text: akke cenmadhu vindeta kimarthaṃ parvataṃ vrajet // iti //
children.translated_text: 'If one could find honey on a milkweed plant, why would one go to the mountain?'

children.text: atrāha-
children.translated_text: To this he says:

children.text: autsukyanivṛttyarthaṃ yathā kriyāsu pravartate lokaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as people engage in activities for the purpose of allaying restlessness,

children.text: puruṣasya vimokṣārthaṃ pravartate tadvadavyaktam || 58 ||
children.translated_text: so too the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) operates for the liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s>. // ISk 58 //

children.text: 'autsukyam'; ityādi / yathautsukyanivṛttyarthamabhimatakriyāsu lokaḥ pravartate, tadvat pralayāvasthāyāṃ puruṣo 'pi mokṣanimittaṃ yadautsukyaṃ tannivṛttaye pravartayetpradhānamiti // 58 //
children.translated_text: 'Restlessness' and so on. Just as people engage in desired activities for the purpose of allaying restlessness, so too in the state of dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>), <s>Puruṣa</s> too has a restlessness whose purpose is liberation — and to allay that, [<s>Puruṣa</s>] sets <s>Pradhāna</s> in motion. // 58 //

children.text: kārikā 59
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 59]

children.text: udāharaṇāntaramāha-
children.translated_text: He gives another illustration:

children.text: raṅgasya darśayitvā nivartate narttakī yathā nṛttāt /
children.translated_text: Just as a dancer, having displayed [her art] to the audience, retires from the dance,

children.text: puruṣasya tathā '; 'tmānaṃ prakāśya vinivartate prakṛtiḥ || 59 ||
children.translated_text: so too <s>Prakṛti</s>, having revealed herself to <s>Puruṣa</s>, withdraws. // ISk 59 //

children.text: 'raṅgasya'; ityādi / nṛtyatīti narttakī / sā tathā raṅgasya nṛttaṃ darśayitvā tasmānnṛttānnivartate viramati, dṛṣṭāhamaneneti kṛtaprayojanā satī, tathā puruṣasyātmānaṃ saṃprakāśya devādibhāvarūpaṃ gatā nivartate prakṛtiḥ pradhānamityarthaḥ // 59 //
children.translated_text: 'To the audience' and so on. She who dances is a dancer. She, having displayed the dance to the audience, retires from that dance — ceases — [thinking] 'I have been seen by him,' her purpose having been fulfilled. Similarly, <s>Prakṛti</s>, i.e., <s>Pradhāna</s>, having fully revealed herself to <s>Puruṣa</s> — having gone through [various] forms such as the divine and other states of existence — withdraws. // 59 //

children.text: kārikā 60
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 60]

children.text: nanu ca naṭī raṅgāt svārthaṃ sādhayati, prakṛtestu puruṣārthaḥ svārtho yenaivamācarayatītyāha-
children.translated_text: But a dancer achieves her own purpose from the stage; whereas for <s>Prakṛti</s>, it is <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose that is her own purpose — by which she behaves thus. To this he says:

children.text: nānāvidhairupāyairupakāriṇyanupakāriṇaḥ puṃsaḥ /
children.translated_text: By various means, the one endowed with <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), serving the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is without <s>guṇas</s>,

children.text: guṇavatyaguṇasya satastasyārthamapārthakaṃ carati || 60 ||
children.translated_text: who does not reciprocate, acts for his purpose without [her own] purpose. // ISk 60 //

children.text: 'nānāvidhaiḥ'; ityādi / pūrvaṃ saptabhirdharmādibhirupāyaistriṣu viṣayeṣvātmanaṃ prakāśayatyupakāriṇī, tadanantaramekena jñānākhyena kaivalyaṃ kurvāṇopakāriṇī bhavati //
children.translated_text: 'By various means' and so on. First, through the seven means of <s>dharma</s> and the rest, she reveals herself in the three domains of objects, being a helper; subsequently, through the one [means] called knowledge, effecting <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation), she becomes a helper.

children.text: 'anapakāriṇaḥ puṃsaḥ'; iti / na pumāṃstāṃ pratyupakaroti, ahamanayopakṛta iti / punassā tamupakaroti //
children.translated_text: 'Of the <s>Puruṣa</s> who does not reciprocate.' <s>Puruṣa</s> does not reciprocate her favor — [he does not think] 'I have been helped by her.' Yet she again helps him.

children.text: nāsau tāmityāha - '; guṇavatyaguṇasya sataḥ'; iti / guṇasattvātprakṛtiḥ sakriyā, nirguṇatvāt puruṣo niṣkriya iti / tasyārthamapārthakaṃ carati / tasya puṃso 'rtho dvividhaḥ- viṣayopabhogaḥ kaivalyaṃ ca / tannirarthakaṃ karoti, yatastasyāḥ prayojanābhāvaḥ / vyaktātmanā '; 'tmānaṃ darśayati natvavyaktātmanā // 60 //
children.translated_text: He does not [help] her — to this he says: 'The one endowed with <s>guṇas</s>, of the one without <s>guṇas</s>.' Because of possessing <s>guṇas</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s> is active; because of being without <s>guṇas</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s> is inactive. She 'acts for his purpose without [her own] purpose.' The twofold purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> — the enjoyment of objects and <s>kaivalya</s> — that she accomplishes without her own purpose, since there is no benefit for her. She reveals herself through her manifest form, but not through her unmanifest form. // 60 //

children.text: kārikā 61
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 61]

children.text:
tathāhi - guṇānāṃ sāmyāvasthā prakṛtiḥ / kutaśca sā na sarvātmanā '; 'tmānaṃ prakāśayati, pumānapi na sarvathā paśyati ? tathā cāhuḥ-
guṇānāṃ paramaṃ rūpaṃ na dṛṣṭipathamṛcchati /
yattu dṛṣṭipathaṃ prāptaṃ tanmāyāvastu tucchakam // iti / atrāha -
children.translated_text: For indeed, the equilibrium state of the <s>guṇas</s> is <s>Prakṛti</s>. And why does she not reveal herself in her entirety, and why does <s>Puruṣa</s> not see her in every way? Thus they say: 'The supreme form of the <s>guṇas</s> does not come within the range of sight; that which comes within the range of sight is a mere illusion, an insubstantial thing.' To this he says:

children.text: prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ na kiñcidastīti me matirbhavati /
children.translated_text: Nothing more delicate than <s>Prakṛti</s> exists — such is my conviction;

children.text: yā dṛṣṭāsmīti punarna darśanamupaiti puruṣasya || 61 ||
children.translated_text: she who, [thinking] 'I have been seen,' does not again come into the sight of <s>Puruṣa</s>. // ISk 61 //

children.text: 'prakṛteḥ'; ityādi / sukumārataramiti sūkṣmataramitarat / etaduktaṃ bhavati- prāgvyaktātmanā prakāśayati na tvavyaktātmanāpi, yena jñānāvasthāyāṃ prakṛtermatirbhavati mama sūkṣmataraṃ na kiñcidaparamasti yaddraṣṭavyaṃ puruṣeṇa //
children.translated_text: 'Of <s>Prakṛti</s>' and so on. 'More delicate' means 'more subtle.' This is what is meant: she previously reveals herself through her manifest form, but not through her unmanifest form — yet in the state of knowledge, <s>Prakṛti</s>'s conviction is: 'there is nothing more subtle than me that remains for <s>Puruṣa</s> to see.'

children.text: ('yā dṛṣṭā 'smi'; iti / sā prakṛtirvyaktātmanā ca) dṛṣṭāhamaneneti na punardarśanamupaiti puruṣasya, draṣṭavyābhāvāt / tataścaivaṃ sarvathā prakṛtirātmānaṃ prakāśayati, puruṣaścaitāṃ sarvathā paśyati // 61 //
children.translated_text: 'She who, [thinking] "I have been seen"' — that <s>Prakṛti</s>, through her manifest form, [thinking] 'I have been seen by him,' does not again come into the sight of <s>Puruṣa</s>, since there is nothing left to be seen. And thus, <s>Prakṛti</s> reveals herself in every way, and <s>Puruṣa</s> sees her in every way. // 61 //

children.text: kārikā 62
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 62]
