children.text: tasmānna puruṣasya bandho nāpi saṃsaraṇaṃ mokṣo vetyāha-
tasmānna badhyate 'ddhā na mucyate nāpi saṃsarati kaścit /
children.translated_text: Therefore, no one is truly bound, nor released, nor does anyone transmigrate;

children.text: saṃsarati badhyate mucyate ca nānāśrayā prakṛtiḥ || 62 ||
children.translated_text: it is <s>Prakṛti</s>, with its manifold substrates, that transmigrates, is bound, and is released. // ISk 62 //
Therefore, there is no bondage, no transmigration, and no liberation for <s>Puruṣa</s> — to this he says:

children.text: 'tasmānna badhyate'; ityādi / bandhābhāvānna badhyate / puruṣasyāpi kāryatvādbandho nāsti / na vimucyate tasyā bandhanāt / nāpi saṃsarati niṣkriyatvāt / kaściditi puruṣa ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, no one is truly bound' and so on. Because of the absence of bondage, one is not bound. Even for <s>Puruṣa</s>, there is no bondage, because of being an effect [attribute of Prakṛti alone]. One is not released from her bondage. Nor does one transmigrate, because of being inactive. 'No one' means <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: kasya tarhi bandhādaya ityāha- saṃsarati badhyate mucyate ca prakṛtiriti / nanu ca tasyāḥ sukumāratvādbandhādayo na sambhavantyevetyatrāha- nānāśrayeṣurabhivajyate (?) / tatrāśrayāḥ bhāvaliṅgabhūtāssargāḥ / te prakṛtipuruṣavannānāvidhāḥ // 62 //
children.translated_text: Whose then are bondage and the rest? To this he says: 'It is <s>Prakṛti</s> that transmigrates, is bound, and is released.' But since she is subtle, how can bondage and the rest belong to her? To this he says: 'With manifold substrates.' There, the substrates are the creations of dispositions, of the subtle body, and of elements. These, like <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, are manifold. // 62 //

children.text: kārikā 63
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 63]

children.text: tataśca nānāśrayatvādeva darśayannāha-
children.translated_text: Showing that it is precisely because of the manifold substrates, he says:

children.text: rūpaiḥ saptabhireva tu badhnātyātmānamātmanā prakṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> binds herself by herself through seven forms;

children.text: saiva ca puruṣārthamprati vimocayatyekarūpeṇa || 63 ||
children.translated_text: and she alone liberates for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> through one form. // ISk 63 //

children.text: 'rūpaiḥ'; ityādi / dharmādayo buddhe rūpānyuktāni / 'saptabhiḥ'; / jñānaṃ tyaktvā te ca prakṛterātmabhūtāḥ / saivātmanaiva puruṣārthaṃ pratyātmānaṃ mahadādisūkṣmaparyantaṃ liṅgaṃ badhnāti / bandhaśca trividhaḥ / tacca liṅgaṃ bhāvādibhiradhivāsitamarthameva / saṃsaratīti / prakṛtireva saṃsarati //
children.translated_text: 'Through forms' and so on. <s>Dharma</s> and the rest have been stated as forms of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). 'Through seven' — excluding knowledge, and these are inherent in <s>Prakṛti</s>. She herself, by herself, binds the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) extending from <s>Mahat</s> to the subtle [elements] for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>. And bondage is threefold. That subtle body, perfumed by dispositions, indeed has a purpose and transmigrates. <s>Prakṛti</s> alone transmigrates.

children.text: 'saiva ca'; iti / prakṛtiḥ puruṣārthaṃ prati kaivalyārthaṃ vimocayatyātmānam //
children.translated_text: 'And she alone' — <s>Prakṛti</s> liberates herself for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, i.e., for the purpose of <s>kaivalya</s>.

children.text: 'ekarūpeṇa'; iti / ekaṃ ca tadrūpaṃ ceti / jñānākhyena rūpeṇetyarthaḥ / yaṃ puruṣamapekṣya jñānamutpādayati taṃ pratyavyaktamātmānaṃ saṃharatītyarthaḥ / nahi dharmādayaḥ puruṣadharmā yastairbadhyate / nāpi saṃsarati, aliṅgabhāvatvāt / nāpi mucyate, tasya bandhanatvāt // 63 //
children.translated_text: 'Through one form' — that which is one and is a form. The meaning is: through the form called knowledge. For which <s>Puruṣa</s> she generates knowledge, for that one she withdraws her unmanifest self — this is the meaning. For <s>dharma</s> and the rest are not properties of <s>Puruṣa</s>, so he is not bound by them. Nor does he transmigrate, since he is without a subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>). Nor is he released, since he was never bound. // 63 //

children.text: kārikā 64
children.translated_text: [Kārikā 64]

children.text: tadevaṃ jñānaṃ kathamutpadyate yena mocayatītyāha-
children.translated_text: How then does that knowledge arise by which she liberates? To this he says:

children.text: evaṃ tattvābhyāsānnāsmi na me nāhamityapariśeṣam /
children.translated_text: Thus, from the practice of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles), [the knowledge] 'I am not, nothing is mine, there is no I' — complete,

children.text: aviparyayādviśuddhaṃ kevalamutpadyate jñānam || 64 ||
children.translated_text: free from error, pure, and absolute knowledge arises. // ISk 64 //

children.text: 'evaṃ tattvābhyāsāt'; ityādi / evamiti vakṣyamāṇe yojyam / tattvāni pañcaviṃśatiḥ / teṣāṃ punaḥ punaḥ svarūpeṇābhyasanamabhyāsaḥ / yadetat sūkṣmaśarīraṃ bhautikaṃ ca tasminna bhavāmi, api tu prakṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Thus, from the practice of the <s>tattvas</s>' and so on. 'Thus' should be connected with what follows. The <s>tattvas</s> are twenty-five. Their repeated contemplation in their true nature is practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>). 'In this subtle body and physical body, I do not exist; rather, [it is] <s>Prakṛti</s>.'

children.text: 'na me'; ityādi / na mamedamapi tu prakṛteḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Nothing is mine' and so on — 'this is not mine, but <s>Prakṛti</s>'s.'

children.text: nāhamiti / nāpyahaṃ prakṛtirityevaṃ tattvābhyāsāt / kiṃviśiṣṭāt - aviparyayādahamityamānasaṃśayāt jñānamutpadyate //
children.translated_text: 'There is no I' — 'nor am I <s>Prakṛti</s>.' Thus, from the practice of the <s>tattvas</s>, knowledge arises. Of what kind? — Free from error, free from doubt of the form 'Am I [Prakṛti] or not?' — knowledge arises.

children.text: īdṛśamityāha- 'apariśeṣam'; iti / paripūrṇaṃ viśuddham saṃsāramalāpagamāt kevalamekamityarthaḥ // 64 //
children.translated_text: Describing what kind [of isolation it is], he says — '<s>apariśeṣam</s>' (complete). Complete, pure — due to the removal of the impurity of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) — <s>kevalam</s> (absolute), meaning singular. // 64 //

children.text: kārikā 65
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 65

children.text: nanu jñānena puruṣaḥ kiṃ paśyatītyāha-
children.translated_text: Now, what does <s>Puruṣa</s> see through knowledge? To this he says —

children.text: tena nivṛttaprasavāmarthavaśāt saptarūpavinivṛttām /
children.translated_text: Through that [knowledge], <s>Prakṛti</s>, whose creation has ceased and who has withdrawn from the seven forms due to the fulfillment of purpose,

children.text: prakṛtiṃ paśyati puruṣaḥ prekṣakavadavasthitaḥ svasthaḥ || 65 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> sees, remaining like a spectator, established in himself. // <s>ISk</s>_65 //

children.text: 'tena'; ityādi / yat prakṛtijñānamutpadyate taṃ prati nivṛtaḥ prasavo liṅgabhūtasargākhyo yasyāḥ prakṛteḥ sa tathoktā / prasavanivṛttyā vā yo viṣayo viṣayebhyo nivartate tadvaśāt, saptabhyo rūpebhyo dharmādibhyo nivṛttā prakṛtirbhavati / bhāvasaṃsargo 'pi yasyā nivartata ityarthaḥ / tāmevaṃvidhāmavyaktarūpāṃ paśyati puruṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: '<s>tena</s>' (through that) and so forth. With respect to the one in whom knowledge of <s>Prakṛti</s> arises, that <s>Prakṛti</s> whose creation — called the production of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) realm — has ceased, is described thus. Or, due to the cessation of creation, the object that withdraws from the sense objects — by virtue of that, <s>Prakṛti</s> becomes withdrawn from the seven forms, namely <s>dharma</s> and the rest. The meaning is that the association with the <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions) also ceases for her. <s>Puruṣa</s> sees her in such a form, in her <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest) nature.

children.text: 'prekṣakavadavasthitaḥ'; iti / yathā prekṣakaḥ pravarttitanṛttamupasaṃhṛtanṛttāṃ ca narttakīṃ paśyati, tathā puruṣo 'pi pravartitasargāmupasaṃhṛtasargāṃ ceti //
children.translated_text: '<s>prekṣakavadavasthitaḥ</s>' (remaining like a spectator). Just as a spectator watches a dancer who has performed her dance and then concluded it, so too <s>Puruṣa</s> [watches <s>Prakṛti</s>] who has initiated creation and then withdrawn it.

children.text: 'svasthaḥ'; iti / ātmani sthito na prakṛtisthaḥ, tataḥ prakṛternivṛttatvāt // 65 //
children.translated_text: '<s>svasthaḥ</s>' (established in himself). Abiding in the Self, not abiding in <s>Prakṛti</s> — because he has withdrawn from <s>Prakṛti</s>. // 65 //

children.text: kārikā 66
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 66

children.text: nanu ca yadi prakṛtirgarbhabhūḥpuruṣaṃ prati nivṛttaprasavā, tasyāśca prakṛtestadānīṃ sarvagatatvādastyeva saṃyogastatkimiti punaḥ śarīrotpattirna bhavatītyāha -
dṛṣṭā mayetyupekṣaka eko dṛṣṭā 'hamityuparamatyanyā /
children.translated_text: 'I have been seen by him,' [thinks one]; the other, [thinking] 'I have seen her,' desists.

children.text: sati saṃyoge 'pi tayoḥ prayojanaṃ nāsti sargasya || 66 ||
children.translated_text: Even though conjunction exists between them, there is no purpose for [further] creation. // <s>ISk</s>_66 //

Now, if <s>Prakṛti</s>, the womb of existence, has ceased her creation with respect to <s>Puruṣa</s>, and since that <s>Prakṛti</s> is all-pervading, conjunction with her still exists — then why does a new bodily birth not occur? To this he says —

children.text: 'dṛṣṭā mayā'; ityādi / tayordvayorekaḥ puruṣa upekṣakaḥ, sarvathā...tvāt / yathā prekṣako naṭīmupekṣate nivṛttābhilāṣatvāt //
children.translated_text: '<s>dṛṣṭā mayā</s>' (seen by me) and so forth. Of those two, one — <s>Puruṣa</s> — is indifferent, because [his purpose] has been entirely [fulfilled]. Just as a spectator disregards the actress, because his desire has ceased.

children.text: 'dṛṣṭā 'hamityuparatā 'nyā'; iti / aparā prakṛtiruparatā nivṛttaprasavā / sarvathā 'hamanena dṛṣṭeti //
children.translated_text: '<s>dṛṣṭā aham iti uparatā anyā</s>' (the other, [thinking] 'I have been seen,' has ceased). The other, <s>Prakṛti</s>, has ceased — her creation has stopped. [She thinks,] 'I have been entirely seen by him.'

children.text: tataśca saṃyoge 'pi tayoḥ prayojanaṃ nāsti sargasya / viṣayopabhogārthaḥ sargaḥ / tasminneva caritārthatvāt na punaḥ sargamārabhate / nahi naṭī raṅge prekṣakairnirākāṃkṣitaṃ punarnṛttamārabhate // 66 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though conjunction exists between them, there is no purpose for creation. Creation is for the purpose of the enjoyment of objects. Since that very purpose has been fulfilled, she does not initiate creation again. Indeed, a dancer does not begin dancing again on the stage when the spectators have no further desire [to watch]. // 66 //

children.text: kārikā 67
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 67

children.text: yadyātmajñānāt kaivalyaprāptiḥ, tadanantarameva śarīraṃ kasmānna nivartata ityāha-
children.translated_text: If the attainment of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) comes from self-knowledge, why does the body not cease immediately after that? To this he says —

children.text: samyagjñānādhigamāt dharmādīnāmakāraṇaprāptau /
children.translated_text: From the attainment of right knowledge, when <s>dharma</s> and the rest have reached the state of non-causality,

children.text: tiṣṭhati saṃskāravaśāt, cakrabhramavaddhṛtaśarīraḥ || 67 ||
children.translated_text: One continues bearing the body due to the force of <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions), like the spinning of a [potter's] wheel. // <s>ISk</s>_67 //

children.text: 'samyak jñānādhigamāt'; ityādi / samyak jñānamātmajñānam / tasyādhigamādātmajñānaprāpterityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: '<s>samyak jñānādhigamāt</s>' (from the attainment of right knowledge) and so forth. Right knowledge means self-knowledge. From its attainment — meaning from the acquisition of self-knowledge.

children.text: 'dharmādīnāmakāraṇaprāptau'; iti / na kāraṇamakāraṇam, tasyāmakāraṇaprāptāveva taduktaṃ bhavati / samyak jñānādhigamātteṣāṃ dharmādīnāmagnidagdhabījavadaśaktatvāt //
children.translated_text: '<s>dharmādīnām akāraṇaprāptau</s>' (when <s>dharma</s> and the rest have reached the state of non-causality). That which is not a cause is <s>akāraṇa</s> (non-cause); upon their reaching that state of non-causality, this is what is stated: from the attainment of right knowledge, <s>dharma</s> and the rest become incapable, like seeds burnt by fire.

children.text: janmāntarasaṃskāravaśāddhṛtaśarīraḥ pumāṃstiṣṭhati / katham- cakrabhramavat / yathā kulālavyāpāre nivṛtte 'pi vegavaśāt kiyantamapi kālaṃ cakrabhramastiṣṭhati tathā śarīramapītyarthaḥ // 67 //
children.translated_text: Due to the force of <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) from previous births, the person continues bearing the body. How? Like the spinning of a wheel. Just as, even after the potter's activity has ceased, the wheel continues spinning for some time due to the force of momentum — so too does the body [continue]. This is the meaning. // 67 //

children.text: kārikā 68
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 68

children.text: kadā sa mokṣo bhavatītyatra-
children.translated_text: When does that liberation occur? Regarding this —

children.text: prāpte śarīrabhede caritārthatvāt pradhānavinivṛttau /
children.translated_text: When the separation of the body has occurred, and <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) has ceased due to the fulfillment of purpose,

children.text: aikāntikamātyantikamubhayaṃ kaivalyamāpnoti || 68 ||
children.translated_text: One attains <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) that is both <s>aikāntika</s> (certain) and <s>ātyantika</s> (absolute). // <s>ISk</s>_68 //

children.text: 'prāpte śarīrabhede'; ityādi / liṅgabhautikaśarīre pṛthagbhūte yathā saṃbhūte layaṃ gati teṣvityarthaḥ (?) //
children.translated_text: '<s>prāpte śarīrabhede</s>' (when the separation of the body has occurred) and so forth. When the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle) and <s>bhautika</s> (gross) bodies become separated — meaning when, just as they were assembled, they undergo dissolution.

children.text: 'caritārthatvāt pradhānavinivṛttau'; iti / pradhānaṃ liṅgātmanā pariṇataṃ nivartate / nivṛttāvubhayaṃ kaivalyamāpnoti //
children.translated_text: '<s>caritārthatvāt pradhānavinivṛttau</s>' (upon the cessation of <s>Pradhāna</s> due to the fulfillment of purpose). <s>Pradhāna</s>, which had transformed in the form of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), ceases. Upon its cessation, one attains both [kinds of] <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation).

children.text: 'aikāntikamātyantikaṃ ca'; iti / tatrātmajñānotpādādavaśyaṃbhāvi kaivalyamityaikāntikam / satyapi tayoḥ saṃyoge prayojanābhāvānna punaḥ sarga ityātyantikamiti // 68 //
children.translated_text: '<s>aikāntikam ātyantikam</s> ca' (both certain and absolute). Of these, <s>kaivalya</s> is <s>aikāntika</s> (certain) because it inevitably arises from the production of self-knowledge. It is <s>ātyantika</s> (absolute) because, even though conjunction between them exists, there is no further creation due to the absence of purpose. // 68 //

children.text: kārikā 69
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 69

children.text: saptatyāṃ viśuddhiṃ darśayannāha-
children.translated_text: Showing the purity of the <s>Saptati</s> (Seventy [verses]), he says —

children.text: puruṣārthajñānamidaṃ guhyaṃ paramarṣiṇā samākhyātam /
children.translated_text: This knowledge for the sake of <s>Puruṣa</s>, secret, was declared by the supreme sage,

children.text: sthityutpattipralayāścintyante yatra bhūtānām || 69 ||
children.translated_text: Wherein the stability, origination, and dissolution of beings are contemplated. // <s>ISk</s>_69 //

children.text: 'puruṣārthajñānam'; ityādi / puruṣārthaṃ jñānaṃ ceti puruṣārthajñānam / yadidaṃ pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānaṃ tatpradhānam, puruṣārthamokṣo 'nena prāpyata iti kṛtvā / guhyamidamaprakāśyam / sādhujanādanyasmai na deyamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: '<s>puruṣārthajñānam</s>' (knowledge for the sake of <s>Puruṣa</s>) and so forth. <s>Puruṣārthajñāna</s> means both the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> and knowledge. This knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles) is primary, because through it <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, is attained. This is secret, not to be disclosed — the meaning is that it should not be given to anyone other than a virtuous person.

children.text: 'paramarṣiṇā samākhyātam'; iti / kapilamuninā prakāśitam //
children.translated_text: '<s>paramarṣiṇā samākhyātam</s>' (declared by the supreme sage). It was made known by the sage <s>Kapila</s>.

children.text: 'sthityutpattipralayāścintyante yatra bhūtānām'; iti / yatra jñāne bhūtānāṃ brahmādistambaparyantānāṃ sthityādayo vyavasthāpyante / tatrotpannānāṃ prabandhenāvasthānaṃ sthitiḥ / sā ca triṣu sthāneṣu daivamānuṣatairyagyoneṣu utpattiḥ sṛṣṭapradhānāt yāvat tanmātrebhyaḥ pañcamahābhūtāni / sṛṣṭyupasaṃhāre mahāpralayaḥ, sarvo 'pyutkrameṇa / tadyathā pṛthivyādayastanmātrādiṣu līyante yāvatpradhānamiti / tena pañcaviṃśatitattvavyatiriktaṃ nāstītyetaduktam // 69 //
children.translated_text: '<s>sthityutpattipralayāś cintyante yatra bhūtānām</s>' (wherein the stability, origination, and dissolution of beings are contemplated). In this knowledge, the stability and other [conditions] of beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass are determined. Among these, the continued abiding of those who have been produced in succession is <s>sthiti</s> (stability). And that [stability exists] in three stations — divine, human, and animal. <s>Utpatti</s> (origination) is from the creation of <s>Pradhāna</s> up to the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) from the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). At the withdrawal of creation, there is <s>mahāpralaya</s> (great dissolution), and everything [dissolves] in reverse order. That is: earth and the rest dissolve into the <s>tanmātras</s> and so on, up to <s>Pradhāna</s>. By this, it is stated that nothing exists beyond the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>. // 69 //

children.text: kārikā 70
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 70

children.text: muninā samākhyātamiti kuto jñāyata ityāha-
children.translated_text: How is it known that it was declared by the sage? To this he says —

children.text: etat pavitramagryaṃ munirāsuraye 'nukampayā pradadau /
children.translated_text: This purifying, foremost [teaching], the sage gave to <s>Āsuri</s> out of compassion;

children.text: āsurirapi pañcaśikhāya, tena ca bahudhā kṛtaṃ tantram || 70 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āsuri</s> also [gave it] to <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, and by him the <s>tantra</s> (system) was elaborated in many ways. // <s>ISk</s>_70 //

children.text: 'etat'; ityādi / 'pavitram'; iti / duḥkhatrayametat punātīti kṛtvā / sarvabhedānāmagrebhavatvādagryam //
children.translated_text: '<s>etat</s>' (this) and so forth. '<s>pavitram</s>' (purifying) — because this purifies [one from] the threefold suffering. It is '<s>agryam</s>' (foremost) because it precedes all [other] divisions [of knowledge].

children.text: 'munirāsuraye 'nukampayā pradadau'; iti / kapilasya mahāmuneḥ sahotpannāścatvāro dharmādayaḥ / tatra jñānākhyena bhāvenāndhe tamasi vartamānaṃ jagat dṛṣṭavato muneḥ karuṇotpannā / tayā ca preryamāṇa āsuriṃ sagotrabrāhmaṇaṃ varṣasahasrayātinamāgatyovāca / 'āsure ramase tvaṃ gṛhasthadharmeṇa'; iti / sa tamāha- 'bhagavan na rame 'ham'; iti / punarvarṣasahasre pūrṇe taṃ gatvā tathovāca / so 'pi 'bhagavan na rame 'ham'; ityuvāca / tato muninā 'yadi viraktastvam, ehi brahmacaryaṃ cara'; ityasāvuktaḥ / sa tu pradipadya gṛhasthadharmaṃ tyaktvā pravrajitaḥ / tasmai śiṣyāyānukampayā saṃkṣipya dattavān / 'tama eva khalvidamāsīt'; / tasmiṃstamasi kṣetrajña eva prathamaḥ / tamaḥ pradhānam, kṣetrajñaḥ puruṣa ucyate / āsurirapi tadeva saṃkṣiptaṃ pañcaśikhāya svaśiṣyāyānukampayā pradadau //
children.translated_text: '<s>munir Āsuraye anukampayā pradadau</s>' (the sage gave to <s>Āsuri</s> out of compassion). The great sage <s>Kapila</s> had four [dispositions] — <s>dharma</s> and the rest — born with him. Among these, through the disposition called <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), the sage, having seen the world dwelling in blind darkness, felt compassion. Impelled by that [compassion], he approached <s>Āsuri</s>, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the same lineage who had been a householder for a thousand years, and said: 'O <s>Āsuri</s>, do you delight in the householder's <s>dharma</s>?' He replied: 'Blessed one, I do not delight.' Again, after another thousand years had passed, he went to him and spoke thus. He too said: 'Blessed one, I do not delight.' Then the sage said to him: 'If you are dispassionate, come, practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy).' And he, having taken initiation and abandoned the householder's <s>dharma</s>, went forth as a renunciant. To that disciple, out of compassion, [<s>Kapila</s>] gave [the teaching] in condensed form: 'This was indeed darkness alone [in the beginning].' In that darkness, the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) alone was the first. Darkness is <s>Pradhāna</s>; the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is called <s>Puruṣa</s>. <s>Āsuri</s> also gave that very condensed [teaching] to <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, his own disciple, out of compassion.

children.text: 'tena'; iti / pañcaśikhena muninā bahudhā kṛtaṃ tantram / ṣaṣṭitantrākhyaṃ ṣaṣṭikhaṇḍaṃ kṛtamiti / tatraiva hi ṣaṣṭirarthā vyākhyātāḥ // 70 //
children.translated_text: '<s>tena</s>' (by him). By the sage <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, the <s>tantra</s> (system) was elaborated in many ways. A work called the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> (Sixty Topics), comprising sixty sections, was composed. For therein sixty topics were explained. // 70 //

children.text: kārikā 71
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 71

children.text: nanu ca ṣaṣṭitantramevāstu kiṃ saptatyeti svaśāstrakaraṇaprayojanamāha-
children.translated_text: Now, let the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> itself suffice — what is the purpose of composing the <s>Saptati</s> (Seventy [verses])? He states the purpose of composing his own treatise —

children.text: śiṣyaparamparayā '; 'gatamīśvarakṛṣṇena caitadāryābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Transmitted through a succession of disciples, this was [composed] by <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s> in <s>āryā</s> verses,

children.text: saṃkṣipyāryamatinā samyagvijñāya siddhāntam || 71 ||
children.translated_text: Having thoroughly understood the established doctrine, [it was] condensed by one of noble intellect. // <s>ISk</s>_71 //

children.text: 'śiṣyaparamparayā'; ityādi / munerāsureḥ pañcaśikhastathā gargagautamaprabhṛtirṇarāmataṃgramyā (?) īśvarakṛṣṇanāmānaṃ parivrājakamityanayā śiṣyaparamparayā / iti jñānamayarūpeṇāgataṃ siddhāntaṃ ṣaṣṭitantram / samyagvijñāya saṃkṣiptaṃ ṣaṣṭitantram, pañcaviṃśatitattvākhyaṃ jñānamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: '<s>śiṣyaparamparayā</s>' (through a succession of disciples) and so forth. From the sage [<s>Kapila</s>] to <s>Āsuri</s>, then <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, then through <s>Garga</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and others ... to the wandering ascetic named <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s> — through this succession of disciples. Thus the established doctrine, the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>, came down in the form of knowledge. Having thoroughly understood it, [he] condensed the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> — meaning the knowledge called the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles).

children.text: āryamatiḥ, adhigatatattvajñānatayāryamatiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Āryamati</s> (one of noble intellect) — [he is called] <s>Āryamati</s> because he has attained the knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s>.

children.text: 'āryābhiḥ'; iti / saptatyetyarthaḥ / 'duḥkhatrayābhighātāt'; 'etat pavitram'; iti saptatyābhihitam // 71 //
children.translated_text: '<s>āryābhiḥ</s>' (in <s>āryā</s> verses) — the meaning is: in seventy [verses]. What has been stated in the Seventy [verses] is [indicated by]: '<s>duḥkhatrayābhighātāt</s>' (from the affliction of the threefold suffering) [and] '<s>etat pavitram</s>' (this is purifying). // 71 //

children.text: kārikā 72
children.translated_text: <s>Kārikā</s> 72

children.text: atra ṣaṣṭitantre bahavo 'rthāḥ, te 'tra noktā ityāha-
children.translated_text: In the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> there are many topics; those are not stated here, he says —

children.text: saptatyāṃ kila ye 'rathāste 'rthāḥ kṛtsnasya ṣaṣṭitantrasya /
children.translated_text: The topics that are in the Seventy [verses] are indeed the topics of the entire <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>,

children.text: ākhyāyikāvirahitāḥ paravādavivarjitāścāpi || 72 ||
children.translated_text: Devoid of illustrative stories and free from rival doctrines. // <s>ISk</s>_72 //

children.text: 'saptatyām'; ityādi / 'eṣa pratyayasargo viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhyākhyaḥ'; ityādinā granthena ya uktāste kṛtsnasya ṣaṣṭitantrasyāpi //
children.translated_text: '<s>saptatyām</s>' (in the Seventy [verses]) and so forth. The topics that have been stated by the text beginning with '<s>eṣa pratyayasargo viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhyākhyaḥ</s>' (this intellectual creation consists of error, incapacity, contentment, and perfection) — those are also [the topics] of the entire <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>.

children.text: kintu 'ākhyāyikāvirahitāḥ paravādavivarjitāḥ śuddhāḥ'; iti / ākhyāyikā ākhyānam, tadvirahitāḥ / paracodyaṃ tena vivarjitāḥ / śuddhāḥ kevalāḥ / paraṃ bandhamokṣopayogino 'rthāḥ darśitā iti tasmāt sampūrṇeyaṃ saptatiriti // 72 //
children.translated_text: Rather, 'free from narratives (<s>ākhyāyikā</s>), devoid of opposing doctrines, [and] pure.' <s>Ākhyāyikā</s> means narration; 'free from them' means without them. 'Opposing objections' — free from those. 'Pure' means mere, i.e., unalloyed. Furthermore, the topics beneficial for bondage and liberation have been shown — therefore this <s>Saptati</s> (Seventy [verses]) is complete. ||72||

children.text: // iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyeṇa śrīśaṅkarabhagavatā kṛtā sāṃkhyasaptatiṭīkā samāptā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the commentary on the <s>Sāṃkhyasaptati</s> (Seventy Verses on <s>Sāṃkhya</s>), composed by the venerable <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>, the disciple of the venerable <s>Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda</s>, the <s>Paramahaṃsa Parivrājakācārya</s> (supreme wandering ascetic and preceptor).
